::: {#changelog .section .content-section}
API Documentation Changelog
===========================

This page tracks all significant changes, updates, and additions to the
TRIP API documentation. Stay informed about new features, endpoint
modifications, and important updates.

::: {.changelog-container}
::: {.changelog-entry}
::: {.changelog-header}
[Version 2.4]{.changelog-version} [10 Jun 2026]{.changelog-date}
:::

::: {.changelog-content}
-   [Updated]{.badge .badge-updated} **Payment API -- Hyperpay:** PCI
    DSS v4.0 update -- The Payment Proxy initialize response now
    includes a new `Data.integrity` field. This value must be added as
    the `integrity` attribute on the Hyperpay script tag in your
    platform (Subresource Integrity / SRI). A Security Guide is
    available in the Hyperpay section with a full initialize response
    example and a link to the [Open Payment Platform -- PCI DSS Widget
    Compliance
    documentation](https://wordpresshyperpay.docs.oppwa.com/tutorials/pci#widgetCompliance).
    See [Hyperpay Initialize Response](#hyperpay-initialize).
-   [Warning]{.badge .badge-warning} **User Accounts -- Assign Role:**
    Added a warning clarifying that when the User Confirmation Step
    feature is used (`ConfirmationRequired: 1`), the role assignment
    request (`POST /arba/apps/TRIP/roles/user/users`) must be performed
    only *after* the user completes account confirmation via
    `POST /auth/register-confirmation`. See [Assign Role](#assign-role).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **AIDA Packages:** Package Documents -- A
    new capability for retrieving and downloading documents attached to
    AIDA packages. Documents can be fetched at project, package, or
    entry level via GET or POST requests, and individual files can be
    downloaded as binary streams. See [Package
    Documents](#aida-package-documents).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **AIDA Packages -- Flight Service:** The
    AIDA Flight service is now available as transportation in AIDA
    packages. Packages that include a flight will expose a
    `Transportation` array in the API response with
    `ServiceGroupCode: "AIR"` and `ServiceTypeCode` set to either
    `Scheduled` or `Charter`. Each entry includes carrier, flight
    number, departure and arrival details. See [Packages List -- Flight
    Transportation](#aida-packages-list).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Hotels List -- Image with
    `summary=true`:** A new `image=true` parameter can now be added
    alongside `summary=true` to include hotel images in the partial
    (pre-100%) search response. Image retrieval is not included by
    default and must be enabled upon request. A performance
    consideration note has been added clarifying that including images
    may slightly increase response time. See [Obtain Hotels Search
    List](#hotels-get-list).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Hotel Search -- Provider Parameters:**
    Introduced the `providerParameters` structure in the hotel search
    request, allowing supplier-specific parameters to be passed per
    search (e.g., `sales_channel` or `test_property` for Expedia Rapid).
    Multiple suppliers and multiple parameters per supplier are
    supported. Parameters can also be configured at application level
    for global inclusion. Coordination with the TRIP Project Manager is
    recommended for setup. See [Hotel Search Provider
    Parameters](#hotels-provider-parameters).
:::
:::

::: {.changelog-entry}
::: {.changelog-header}
[Version 2.3]{.changelog-version} [18 May 2026]{.changelog-date}
:::

::: {.changelog-content}
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Payment API:** Added Viva Wallet payment
    gateway (Authorization and Refund). See [Viva Wallet Payment
    Gateway](#viva-initialize). Includes a setup guide for configuring
    the redirect URLs in the Viva management account.
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Payment API:** Added JCC payment gateway
    (Initialize with authorize and capture, and Refund). See [JCC
    Payment Gateway](#jcc-initialize).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Payment API:** Added Ngenius payment
    gateway (Initialize/authorize and Capture). See [Ngenius Payment
    Gateway](#ngenius-initialize).
:::
:::

::: {.changelog-entry}
::: {.changelog-header}
[Version 2.2]{.changelog-version} [20 Mar 2026]{.changelog-date}
:::

::: {.changelog-content}
-   [Updated]{.badge .badge-updated} **AIDA Packages:** Supplements --
    Documentation updated to clarify that supplements can be used
    without a price set ID. When a supplement is not linked to any price
    set, it can be selected stand-alone and sent directly in the
    availability request and in the order POST service data, without
    specifying a `price-set` parameter. Payload examples for both
    scenarios (with and without price set ID) have been added. See
    [Supplements](#aida-supplements).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Hotel Search & Hotels List:** Distance
    Calculation -- Documentation updated to clarify how distance is
    calculated based on `poiLat`/`poiLng` in the search request and how
    `lat`/`lng` can be used in the hotels list request when the POI was
    not provided in the search. See [Hotel Search](#hotels-search) and
    [Obtain Hotels Search List](#hotels-get-list).
:::
:::

::: {.changelog-entry}
::: {.changelog-header}
[Version 2.1]{.changelog-version} [23 Jan 2026]{.changelog-date}
:::

::: {.changelog-content}
-   [Warning]{.badge .badge-warning} **Hotel Booking:** Child age in
    hotel bookings is now calculated at check-in date instead of
    check-out date.
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Hotel Search:** Cancellation Deadline in
    Rooms List -- The cancellation deadline can now be included in the
    rooms list response. See [Hotel Search](#hotels-search).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Flight Booking:** Travelfusion Offers --
    Book Confirmation Step: Added documentation for handling user
    verification redirects required by certain airlines integrated via
    TravelFusion. See [Orders API -
    Reserve/Book](#orders-book-all-services).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **User Accounts:** Last Login Date is now
    included in the User Details response, enabling personalized user
    experiences. See [User Accounts - Get Data Saved](#user-data-saved).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **Orders API:** Booking Request in Progress
    -- Introduced `bookInProgress` field to prevent duplicate booking
    actions for the same order. Available starting with application
    version 3.0.4. See [Orders API -
    Reserve/Book](#orders-book-all-services).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **AIDA Packages:** Supplements --
    Supplements configured in AIDA for extra services are now fully
    supported in TRIP. When defined in AIDA, these supplements are
    included in the Extra Services API response and can be selected
    during the booking flow. See [Supplements](#aida-supplements).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **AIDA Packages:** Translations --
    Multi-language support has been added for AIDA packages. Package
    names, descriptions, room types, city names, and extra services now
    include translations in the API responses. See [Package
    Translations](#aida-package-translations).
-   [New]{.badge .badge-new} **AIDA Packages:** Reservation
    Synchronization -- Reservation changes made in AIDA are now
    reflected in TRIP through a daily cron job. Status updates (RQ to
    OK, or to Cancelled) are automatically synchronized. See
    [Reservation Synchronization & Amend](#aida-reservation-sync).
:::
:::

::: {.changelog-entry}
::: {.changelog-header}

::: {#travel-industry-flow .section .content-section}
Travel Industry Flow & Data {#travel-industry-flow-title}
===========================

Before diving into the specific API endpoints, it\'s important to
understand some fundamental concepts about how the travel industry
operates and how this affects data flow and availability in TRIP.

Dynamic Pricing & Availability {#dynamic-pricing}
------------------------------

Unlike traditional retail, travel services operate on dynamic pricing
models where prices and availability change constantly based on:

::: {.features-list}
-   **Real-time demand** Prices fluctuate based on current booking
    patterns, seasonal demand, and market conditions.
-   **Inventory management** Available seats, rooms, or services are
    limited and managed in real-time across multiple distribution
    channels.
-   **Time-sensitive offers** Prices and availability can change between
    search and booking, requiring immediate action from users.
-   **Supplier-specific rules** Each supplier (airline, hotel, activity
    provider) has unique booking rules, cancellation policies, and data
    requirements.
:::

Multi-step Booking Process {#multi-step-booking}
--------------------------

Travel bookings typically follow a complex multi-step process that
differs from simple product purchases:

1.  **Search & Availability Check**
    -   Real-time queries to multiple suppliers
    -   Filtering and sorting of available options
    -   Price comparison across different sources
2.  **Selection & Validation**
    -   Detailed offer validation with suppliers
    -   Price and availability confirmation
    -   Terms and conditions retrieval
3.  **Passenger Information Collection**
    -   Personal details for each traveler
    -   Document information (passport, ID)
    -   Special requirements and preferences
4.  **Booking Confirmation**
    -   Final price confirmation
    -   Payment processing
    -   Booking reference generation
5.  **Post-booking Management**
    -   Ticket issuance (for flights)
    -   Modification and cancellation handling
    -   Document delivery and management

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
#### Important Timing Considerations

Due to the dynamic nature of travel inventory, always implement proper
error handling for scenarios where offers become unavailable between
search and booking completion.
:::
:::

Data Flow Architecture
----------------------

Understanding how data flows through the TRIP system helps optimize your
implementation:

1.  **Request Processing**
    -   API requests are authenticated and validated
    -   Search parameters are normalized and distributed to suppliers
    -   Multiple supplier responses are aggregated and processed
2.  **Data Aggregation**
    -   Results from different suppliers are standardized
    -   Duplicate offers are identified and merged
    -   Pricing and availability are validated in real-time
3.  **Response Optimization**
    -   Results can be sorted and filtered based on user preferences
    -   Responses are cached where appropriate for performance
:::

::: {#authentication .section .content-section}
Authentication API {#authentication-title}
==================

::: {.sub-section-item}
Create a valid API request {#auth-create-request}
--------------------------

::: {.info-box}
#### API Endpoint & Application ID

The **API endpoint** and **Application ID** will be provided during the
installation process.

The base API endpoint is usually structured as:
`https://yourdomain.com/trip/public/index.php`

The rest of the endpoint path depends on the specific module/API you
need to use. For example:

-   `https://yourdomain.com/trip/public/index.php/en/authentication/token/generate`
:::

TRIP REST API\'s can be accessed using an unique application ID. Based
on the application ID, a request can be performed to obtain a token key.
The token will be added in each request therefore securing the
communication between browser and TRIP platform.

The authorization process can be done using the following steps:

1.  **Add in your request query:**
    -   `timestamp` = [current Unix timestamp]{.param-value}
    -   `applicationId` = [ApplicationId]{.param-value}
2.  **Add in your request header:**
    -   `Authorization` = [token value]{.param-value}

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Important Request Format

When an HTTP request includes a message body (e.g., in POST, PUT, or
PATCH methods), the body must be encoded using the
application/x-www-form-urlencoded media type.

Every HTTP request sent to the TRIP API must provide applicationId and
timestamp as query string parameters.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}
Generate token
--------------

On status = 1, the token object is received (only if the authentication
data is correct). The token received will be used on all the requests
performed (it must be added in the authorization header)

If the token is expired (token expired http status 511 with
message:Token expired , please refresh token before make another
request), it needs to be refreshed using the Refresh token request and
the new value must be used in the following request.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/en/authentication/token/generate]{.url}
:::

::: {.info-box}
**Full URL Example:**
`https://yourdomain.com/trip/public/index.php/en/authentication/token/generate?applicationId=YOUR_APP_ID&timestamp=1234567890`
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Query Parameters

  Description      Type     Query Parameter   Value
  ---------------- -------- ----------------- -------
  Application ID   string   aplicationId      
  Timestamp        string   timestamp         
:::
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}
Refresh token
-------------

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/en/authentication/token/refresh]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Query Parameters

  Description      Type     Query Parameter   Value
  ---------------- -------- ----------------- -------
  Application ID   string   aplicationId      
  Timestamp        string   timestamp         
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Header Parameters

  Description                  Type     Header parameter   Value
  ---------------------------- -------- ------------------ -------
  The token generated before   string   Authorization      
:::
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}
Authentication process configuration {#auth-process-config}
------------------------------------

After you manage to use the token authentication system, you should know
that there are also some configuration that can be performed for the
authentication process:

::: {.features-list}
### Characteristics

-   **token time to live** - time after which you have to refresh the
    token (on test environment is set to half an hour);
-   **token lives** - number of requests after which you have to refresh
    the token (on test environment is set to 100);
-   **request availability** - represents how long after you send the
    request we are no longer consider it available (on test environment
    is set to 30 seconds);
-   **token value header** - it is expected the token value in the
    authorization header, but this is configurable, if you can not use
    this header;
-   **hash header** - the x-hash header also is configurable;
-   **allowed orders on token** - represents the maximum number of empty
    orders (status = 0) made with a token (on test environment is set to
    30);
-   **allowed requests in a time interval** - represents the maximum
    number of requests you can make with a token in certain period (on
    test environment you can not make more than 10000 requests in one
    day);
-   **request source** - we can define an IP or user agent Regex and
    allow requests only from that source (on test environment this
    restriction is disabled).
:::
:::
:::

::: {#user-account .section .content-section}
User Account {#user-account-title}
============

::: {.sub-section-item}
Create new user {#user-create}
---------------

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/auth/register]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                             Type     Parameter   Value
  ------------------------------------------------------- -------- ----------- -------
  The email for the account that will be registered.      string   Email       
  The password for the account that will be registered.   string   Password    
:::

Assign Role
-----------

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
After making the request for registering an user, you have to assign
that user a role, so he can have the rights to make different requests
in application, so after the register request, you should make a POST
request to:`/arba/apps/TRIP/roles/user/users` with `UIF:UserEmail` in
body, where: UserEmail is the email address of the registered user and
\"users\" is a standard role in the application.
:::
:::

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  Important -- User Confirmation Step

If the **User Confirmation Step** feature is enabled (i.e.
`ConfirmationRequired: 1` is sent during registration), the role
assignment request (`POST /arba/apps/TRIP/roles/user/users`) **must be
made only after the user has completed the confirmation**, meaning after
the `POST /auth/register-confirmation` request has been successfully
completed.
:::
:::

### Add role to user

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/arba/apps/TRIP/roles/user/users]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                             Type     Parameter   Value
  --------------------------------------- -------- ----------- -------
  The email for the account registered.   string   UIF         
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Request Data Example
:::

    {
    UIF: "user@dcsplus.net"
    }
:::

### Users - E-mail notification for new registered users

On register new user you can send in form data SendNotification param
which has the follow behavior

-   if not sent =\> notification email will be sent to the new user
-   if 1 or everything else =\> notification email will be sent to the
    new user
-   if 0 =\> notification email will not be sent to the new user

Keep in mind the e-mail template must be created & asigned in TRIP admin
area/ Email section.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Register Response Example
:::

    {
      "Id": "613",
      "Name": "user@dcsplus.net",
      "Email": "user@dcsplus.net",
      "CreationDate": "2021-03-12 13:28:43",
      "Status": 1,
      "_links": {1 item}
    }
:::

### Add confirmation step

This step is optional, you can register a user without it. If you use
this step, the user will not be able to login in the account until the
register is confirmed by accessing the link from the e-mail and by
sending the token to the register-confirmation endpoint.

-   The parameter - **ConfirmationRequired: 1** - This parameter will
    trigger the confirmation e-mail that will be sent to the user\'s
    e-mail address (if added, ConfirmationReturnUrl is also required)
-   The parameter - **ConfirmationReturnUrl: \'\'** - (the absolute URL
    for the landing page where the registration will be confirmed) (if
    added, ConfirmationRequired field is also required)

This will generate an email message sent to user\'s address which will
contain a token-based authentication link to the ConfirmationReturnUrl
page. This URL will contain these query params:
UserId=\'\...\'&Token=\'\...\' Inside the return page use the query
params to make a request POST to /auth/register-confirmation with body
params: { UserId: \'\', Token: \'\'} (for confirming the account).

**Note:** response body for the confirmation POST request will be the
same as the one from the register endpoint
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}

::: {.sub-section-item}
Register & login with social media account {#user-social-media}
------------------------------------------

TRIP platorm allows you to register or sign in users with social media
(facebook, Instagram, others can be added at client request).

### Social media developers account configuration

The first step in the process is to add an account in the TRIP admin
area for your developer social media connection.

The module is available in the External services section/SSO ; Add a new
account after you have selected the type:

Fill in the required data and enable the account.

### Log in/Register steps with social media

Now that you have registered the account in TRIP, you can use it to add
the option in your website:

1.  When user selects Sign in /Log in with social media, a request needs
    to be done, using the exact provider name (azure, facebook, google,
    Instagram, etc) & account ID:
    /sso/protocols/:protocol\_name/provider/:provider\_name/accounts/:account\_id/initialize
2.  The response will have the following format:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Social Media Response Example
:::

    {
      "Action": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/182f2c54-bd57-43e1-8d56-70eabe532810/oauth2/v2.0/authorize",
      "Method": "GET",
      "Data": {
        "state": "e9f2ebe06063307e3c19a935898ec7fd",
        "scope": "openid profile email offline_access https://graph.microsoft.com/User.Read",
        "response_type": "code",
        "approval_prompt": "auto",
        "redirect_uri": "redirectURL/index.php/sso/protocols/openid/provider/azure/accounts/2/authenticate",
        "client_id": "3d4b8cb5-802a-480a-9588-acb1d811752c"
      },
      "authorizationUrl": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/182f2c54-bd57-43e1-8d56-70eabe532810/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?state=e9f2ebe06063307e3c19a935898ec7fd&scope=openid profile email offline_access https%3A%2F%2Fgraph.microsoft.com%2FUser.Read&response_type=code&approval_prompt=auto&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%2Fdynapack%2Fclients%2Fcsb%2Fpublic%2Fdevelop%2Findex.php%2Fsso%2Fprotocols%2Fopenid%2Fprovider%2Fazure%2Faccounts%2F2%2Fauthenticate&client_id=3d4b8cb5-802a-480a-9588-acb1d811752c"
    }
:::

3.  Redirect the user to the URL received in the Action property, using
    the method specified in Method section and make sure you add also
    the data payload. \*If the method is GET, then you can just use the
    authorizationURL for redirect.
4.  User will be redirected back from the identity provider\'s website.
    On the redirect URL (the one which you have configured in the admin
    area), you need to use the token retrieved at the end of the URL (
    the token will be received in authorization from query params) and
    use it by making the GET request on auth/login request. This will
    validate if the user is logged in and retrieves the user
    information. Based on this, the user is considered logged in.

### Additional requests (optional)

The provider\'s name and account ID can be either hardcoded in your
project or you can obtain them dynamically using the endpoints:

-   ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [GET]{.method .get} [/sso/protocols/:protocol\_name/provider]{.url}
    :::

    [list providers]{.endpoint-description}

-   ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [GET]{.method .get}
    [/sso/protocols/:protocol\_name/provider/:provider\_name/accounts]{.url}
    :::

    [list accounts]{.endpoint-description}
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}
Multi factor authentication -- TOTP {#user-mfa}
-----------------------------------

The log in process can be upgraded to offer the users the possibility of
two factor authentication using any TOTP platform/application.

The option can be implemented by adding the following flow to your
existing log in/user account or register process:

### Enable & Associate MFA TOTP device:

1.  Log in the user (standard request)
2.  Make a POST request to auth/mfa/totp and will receive a qrImageUrl.\
    This QR code should be scanned with an authentication mobile app.
    That authentication app will generate unique codes that will be used
    on authentication requests; at this point a device asociation with
    status unconfirmed will be created.
3.  Send the code generated by the MFA app as a POST request to
    /auth/mfa/totp with Code in params.

Once the association is done, the user will have to log in using both
the TRIP password and the MFA code generated by the linked device.

If the user needs to change the device, the user must have the option in
User account to remove the existing association and create a new
association.

To remove an association, user must be logged in and by making a new
DELETE request to /auth/mfa/totp or a PATCH request to /auth/mfa/totp.
For the PATCH request, a new QR code will be received, and user will
have to go again trough the above process (scan the code into the
Athenticator app and submit a POST request to /auth/mfa/totp with Code
in params).

Also, the agency admin that has access to manage users will be able to
remove association in the name of the user from Users/Edit User
section).

**Attention!** If the association is removed by agency admin, by default
the MFA will be disabled for that user and they will no longer be
required to log in with the extra code. In order for the user to
reactivate the MFA they need to go to their account and enable the
feature again.

Once you offer the MFA feature in your platform, the log in process must
be changed as following: In the Log in process add the following:

1.  Instead of the request to auth/login, send Username and Password
    through
    ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [POST]{.method .post} [/auth/mfa]{.url}
    :::

    and a list of user\'s configured mfa types will be received along
    with mfa\_required\_config flag (if its value is 1 and types is
    empty then the first request after login must be for adding mfa
    config
    ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [POST]{.method .post} [/auth/mfa/:type]{.url}
    :::

    ). This will generate the QR code and the same steps from „Enable &
    Associate MFA TOTP device\" must be followed
2.  According to received types list:
    -   **If is empty:**
        -   mfa\_required\_config flag is enabled (mfa\_required\_config
            = 1)\
            login request will be the same as usual but after
            authentication user will receive Please enable multi factor
            authentication error message at every request until they
            will add mfa config
            ::: {.endpoint-inline}
            [POST]{.method .post} [/auth/mfa/:type]{.url}
            :::

            \
            In this case, the first request after login must be for
            adding mfa config
            ::: {.endpoint-inline}
            [POST]{.method .post} [/auth/mfa/:type]{.url}
            :::

            . This will generate the QR code and the same steps from
            „Enable & Associate MFA TOTP device\" must be followed
        -   mfa\_required\_config flag is disabled
            (mfa\_required\_config = 0) ▪ login request will be the same
            as usual, it means user did not select multi factor
            authentication
    -   **If is not empty**\
        You need to display an extra input according to selected type
        and send it along Username and Password to login request (for
        totp the extra input text is Code where user will introduce the
        code from authentication app)
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}
Logout {#user-logout}
------

To logout the user, you need to make a basic POST request to
/auth/logout, no other data required.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/auth/logout]{.url}
:::
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}
Check Password Validity {#user-check-password}
-----------------------

This endpoint allows you to check if a password meets the security
requirements and generate strong password suggestions.

This works in conjunction with platform configurations. If specific
restrictions are required, be sure to request the appropriate
configurations.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/auth/check-password]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Query Parameters

  Description                            Type     Parameter     Default Value
  -------------------------------------- -------- ------------- ------------------
  Password (new one)                     string   length        
  Filters for what needs to be checked   string   filter\[0\]   pattern
  Filters for what needs to be checked   string   filter\[1\]   common-passwords
  Filters for what needs to be checked   string   filter\[2\]   old-passwords
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Check Password Validity Response Example
:::

    {
        "pattern": true,
        "common-passwords": true,
        "old-passwords": false,
        "_links": {
            "self": {
                "href": "\/auth\/check-password"
            }
        }
    }
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Response Fields

  Field              Type      Description
  ------------------ --------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  pattern            boolean   Indicates if the password meets the required pattern and complexity rules (length, character types, etc.)
  common-passwords   boolean   Shows if the password is found in common password dictionaries. **true** means it\'s a common password (not recommended)
  old-passwords      boolean   Indicates if the password matches any previously used passwords by the user. **true** means it was used before (not allowed)
:::
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}

---------------

::: {.endpoint}
[PATCH]{.method .patch} [/auth/register/:userId]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                                             Type     Parameter        Value
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -------- ---------------- -------
  The registration id for the user that will have the password changed.   int      {\$RegisterId}   
  The old password that will be defined for the user.                     string   Password         
  The new password that will be defined for the user.                     string   NewPassword      
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Change Password Response Example
:::

    {
      "Id": "613",
      "UserId": "613",
      "Username": "user@dcsplus.net",
      "Password": "******",
      "CreationDate": "2021-03-12",
      "Status": "1",
      "_links": {1 item}
    }
:::
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}
Forgot Password {#user-forgot-password}
---------------

Forgot password is the function that allows you to reset a password
using only the e-mail address registered for an user.

### Trigger Forgot password flow

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/auth/forgot-password]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                               Type     Parameter   Value
  --------------------------------------------------------- -------- ----------- ------------------------------------------------------------
  The username for the user                                 string   Username    
  Return URL of the page where user will add new password   string   ReturnUrl   Example: https://demo.trip.dcsplus.net/reset-password.html
:::

-   Make a request to the API using the username (e-mail address of the
    registered user)

-   You can also add the ReturnUrl and you can add on the e-mail
    template a variable to use the ReturnUrl variable

-   TRIP will automatically generate a secure token and will send it to
    the provided e-mail address, using a Forgot Password e-mail
    template. The template can be created or edited from TRIP\'s admin
    area/E-mails

    The available template variables for Forgot Password e-mail template
    are:

    Template variables:

-   user.Username

-   user.FirstName

-   user.LastName

-   data.token

-   data.returnUrl

-   After the user clicks on the link provided in the e-mail, he will be
    redirected to a page created by you in your project

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Forgot Password Response Example
:::

    {
      "Id": "1",
      "UserId": "613",
      "Token": "********",
      "Status": 0,
      "Date": "2021-03-12 15:03:17",
      "Timestamp": null,
      "_links": {1 item}
    }
:::

### Change password {#change-password}

::: {.endpoint}
[PATCH]{.method .patch} [/auth/forgot-password/:token]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                           Type     Parameter     Value
  ----------------------------------------------------- -------- ------------- -------
  Token                                                 string   :token        
  The new password that will be defined for the user.   string   NewPassword   
:::

-   Using the token in the URL generate by TRIP (the one from the
    e-mail), a request is made to TRIP\'s API with the new password
-   Once the password is changed, TRIP can send a confirmation e-mail to
    the user

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Reset Password Response Example
:::

    {
      "Id": "393",
      "UserId": "613",
      "Username": "user@dcsplus.net",
      "Password": "******",
      "CreationDate": "2021-03-12",
      "Status": "1",
      "_links": {1 item}
    }
:::
:::

::: {.sub-section-item}
User details & fields API {#user-data-api}
-------------------------

The User Data API (UDA) offers the possibility to assign data and
information to specific users across various configurable types.

::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  User Data Structure -- What You Need to Know

Before implementing user data management, make sure you understand the
key concepts of the user data structure:

###### User Types {#user-types style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

-   **Multiple types supported:** TRIP allows you to define multiple
    user types (e.g., Standard user, Company user) with custom field
    sets for each.
-   **Flexible data storage:** A single user can have data saved on
    multiple types simultaneously. For example, the same user can have
    data on both \"Standard\" and \"Company\" types.
-   **Booking flexibility:** On the book page, you can let the customer
    choose which user data type to use for the booking.

###### Fields Configuration {#fields-configuration style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

-   **Admin interface:** Create fields, user types, and multi-value
    fields directly from the TRIP admin interface.
-   **Default fields:** Email/username and password are default fields
    for each user -- mandatory in registration and automatically
    available (no need to add them as custom fields).
-   **Custom fields:** Add custom fields with different field types per
    user type. Restriction: you cannot add two fields with the same name
    on the same type.
-   **Default configuration:** The platform comes with a default
    \"Standard\" configuration with ID=1.

###### How to Obtain User Data {#how-to-obtain-user-data style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

-   `GET /auth/user-types` -- Retrieve all configured user types and
    their IDs
-   `GET /auth/user-types/{typeId}/fields` -- Get fields configuration
    for a specific user type
-   `GET /auth/users/{userId}/type/{typeId}` -- Get saved data for a
    specific user and type
-   `POST /auth/user-details/{userId}/{typeId}` -- Save or update user
    data

###### Implementation Steps {#implementation-steps style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

1.  Create user types in the TRIP admin area
2.  Configure the fields you want to save for each type
3.  Use the API to retrieve types and fields configuration
4.  Build your user account interface based on the retrieved
    configuration
5.  Save and retrieve user data using the appropriate endpoints
:::
:::

### Get all user types configured {#user-types-config}

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/auth/user-types]{.url}
:::

This request can be used to obtain all the types of user configuration
saved. This will retrieve the ID, based on which you can obtain the
fields details.

Usually, this request is done if you are using a more complex
configuration and you have multiple types saved in the admin area. If
you are using only one configuration for your users, you can use always
the one ID you have generated in the admin area. For example, the
platform comes with a default configuration \"Standard\" which has the
ID=1.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
User Types Response Example
:::

    {
        "_links": {
            "self": {
                "href": "   \/auth\/user-types"
            }
        },
        "_embedded": {
            "user_types": [
                {
                    "Id": "61",
                    "Name": "demo",
                    "Status": "1",
                    "_links": {
                        "self": {
                            "href": "   \/auth\/user-types\/61"
                        }
                    }
                },
                {
                    "Id": "65",
                    "Name": "b2c",
                    "Status": "1",
                    "_links": {
                        "self": {
                            "href": "   \/auth\/user-types\/65"
                        }
                    }
                },
                {
                    "Id": "66",
                    "Name": "VIP",
                    "Status": "1",
                    "_links": {
                        "self": {
                            "href": "   \/auth\/user-types\/66"
                        }
                    }
                },
                {
                    "Id": "67",
                    "Name": "Company",
                    "Status": "1",
                    "_links": {
                        "self": {
                            "href": "   \/auth\/user-types\/67"
                        }
                    }
                },
                {
                    "Id": "68",
                    "Name": "TEST1",
                    "Status": "1",
                    "_links": {
                        "self": {
                            "href": "   \/auth\/user-types\/68"
                        }
                    }
                },
                {
                    "Id": "70",
                    "Name": "Standard",
                    "Status": "1",
                    "_links": {
                        "self": {
                            "href": "   \/auth\/user-types\/70"
                        }
                    }
                }
            ]
        },
        "total_items": 6
    }
:::

### Obtain the fields configuration for a user type

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/auth/user-detail-field/:typeId]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description          Type     Parameter    Value
  -------------------- -------- ------------ -------
  The data type name   string   {\$typeId}   
:::

This request can be used to obtain the fields configuration. For
example, this can be used in user account to display the fields that a
user needs to fill in. The response will include field type and patterns
(if any).

### Get the data saved for a user {#user-data-saved}

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/auth/users/:userId/type/:typeId]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description          Type     Parameter          Value
  -------------------- -------- ------------------ -------
  The user ID          string   {\$userId}         
  The data type name   string   {\$UserDataType}   
:::

#### API Availability

User details can be retrieved using the following API endpoints:

-   `GET /auth/users/{userId}` -- Get user details by user ID
-   `GET /auth/users/{userId}/type/{userTypeId}` -- Get user details by
    user ID and user type

::: {.step-subsection}
#### User Details -- Last Login Date

**Last Login Date** is now included in the User Details response.

##### Example Use Cases {#example-use-cases style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

The Last Login Date can be used to enhance the user experience in
various ways, such as:

-   Displaying personalized greetings like \"Welcome back!\" or \"It\'s
    been a while since your last visit.\"
-   Highlighting new features, offers, or updates since the user\'s
    previous login.
-   Adjusting the interface or suggested content based on how recently
    the user interacted with the platform.
-   Providing contextual insights within the user profile or dashboard.
:::

### Save details for a user {#user-save-details}

Based on what fields were configured in the admin area for a type,
information can be saved by using the below endpoint. A user can have
saved data on all the types configured in the admin area.

The request URL must include the user ID and the type ID. The rest of
the data, must be added in the body, using the fields received in the
fields configuration response.

To save new data or update the current data, this specific request needs
to used.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [auth/user-details/userId/typeId]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description          Type     Parameter          Value
  -------------------- -------- ------------------ -------
  The user ID          string   {\$userId}         
  The data type name   string   {\$UserDataType}   
:::

### Get all data types {#user-all-data-types}

These options can be used whenever you want to save multiple values on
the same fields. For example, passports or frequent flyer cards would be
a perfect way to use this functionality. Just by going to the user
section, user entities, you can insert custom fields in the data base.
On the fields you will be able to store multiple values.

The fields are defined in TRIP admin area and you can retrive the
information configured by using this request.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/auth/user-data-types]{.url}
:::

**Use case:** Let\'s assume we need to offer the possibility to an user
to insert into the system his loyalty cards. This means an user can have
one, more or none loyalty cards. Let\'s also assume a loyalty card may
have the following properties: company, number and expiration date.
Using UDA we will define an user-data-type loyalty-cards. On this type
we will define some fields as follow: company field required, number
field required and expireDate field optional but with validation for a
correct formatted date. After that user can add how many that want of
this data type.
:::
:::

::: {#search-process .section .content-section}
Search Process {#search-process-title}
==============

How to obtain a city/location ID {#search-location-id}
--------------------------------

This API returns a list of location predictions for text-based
geographic search queries. The API uses the full word or substring
across all locations to match against a geographic search query. A
location can be an airport or city.

### Hotel Locations

Gives travelers a list of places that most closely match their search
query.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/hotel-locations.php]{.url}
:::

::: {.info-box}
**Note:** This is a direct endpoint. Example:
`https://yourdomain.com/trip/public/hotel-locations.php`
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                       Type     Parameter   Value
  ------------------------------------------------- -------- ----------- -------
  The full word or substring to be autocompleted.   string   q           
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Hotel Locations Response Example
:::

    [
      {
        "CityId": "1",
        "CityCode": "PAR",
        "RegionId": "0",
        "CountryId": "2",
        "NoHotels": "10292",
        "SubItem": "1",
        "Name": "PARIS",
        "CountryName": "France"
      },
      {8 items},
      {8 items}
    ]
:::

### Flight Locations

Gives travelers a list of places and airports that most closely match
their search query.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/flight-locations.php]{.url}
:::

::: {.info-box}
**Note:** This is a direct endpoint. Example:
`https://yourdomain.com/trip/public/flight-locations.php`
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  ------------------------------------------------- -------- ----------- -------
  The full word or substring to be autocompleted.   string   q           
:::

### Static data -- cities

The static data cities API can be used to obtain the city ID or code
that is necessary to a search.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/index.php/static-data/cities?limit=10&page=1&filter\[0\]\[name\]=Name&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Par&filter\[0\]\[type\]=startsWith]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                                    Type     Parameter                                                                                 Value
  -------------------------------------------------------------- -------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------
  The filter query to obtain the cities starting with a value.   string   filter\[0\]\[name\]=Name&filter\[0\]\[term\]={city name}&filter\[0\]\[type\]=startsWith   
:::

How to create container for a search request {#search-container}
--------------------------------------------

A search container has the following format:

**\_s\[\_containerid\_\]\[\_service\_\]\[\_searchidx\_\]\[\_variable\_\]**
where:

1.  **\_s (array):** containers array where the containerid is the array
    key;
2.  **\_s\[ContainerId\] (array):** associative array that contains the
    service(f for flight, h for hotel, p for packages) searches included
    in this container;
3.  **\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\] (array):** indexed array that contains the
    flight searches;
4.  **\_s\[ContainerId\]\[h\] (array):** indexed array that contains the
    hotel searches;
5.  **\_s\[ContainerId\]\[p\] (array):** indexed array that contains the
    package searches;

User launches multiple searches using this container. The container ID
is defined by de user and he can use this ID across multiple pages. User
will have the possibility to interrogate, using an API-check endpoint,
his \"grouped searches\" based on the container ID, which may contain
one or more searches. Each service will be set in a container, generated
by container ID + Token (this way we avoid container conflicts), a
search-key (generated from the search criteria =\> multiple similar
searches, from different users will be searched across) and will update
the status according to the results of the search.

After the search was launched, the status of each search must be
checked. Also, the inspect request can retrieve the information you
searched for, making this a useful tool for reusing information in your
flow or start a new search just based on the search ID (SID)

Inspect SID/ Get Search Result Code {#get-search-code}
-----------------------------------

After you make a search request, you will receive a search result code.
This code is used to retrieve the search results.

Make the inspect SID request to get the search result code. You need to
repeat the request until code is received. If the value is null, it
means there are no search results available for your request.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [dynamick-package/sid/{Search ID obtained from the
search request}]{.url}
:::

The search result code is available in the **code** field. If the value
is null or empty, it means there are no search results available for
your request.

Make the request untill the code parameter is received.

### Search expiry information

Extra properties were added to provide more details about the status of
the cached search. This information can be used in order to notify the
customer that search will expire and data needs to be refreshed or it
just can be used to restart search when the search it\'s about to
expire.

-   **updated** represents the timestamp when the result code was
    generated
-   **life** represents the current remaining lifetime in seconds

Keep in mind that the content you are working on is dynamic, this means
the offers are real time updated and some level of cache might be
applied on a search by suppliers and even by TRIP/IRIX. In this case you
might encounter the situation when search might expire in just a few
minutes after you started the search, This happens in case the same
identical search was already performed in the platform, and you were
given results from a cache. Caching systems are important in live
inventory (dynamic data) as it protects both your infrastructure and the
supplier\'s infrastructures. More than that, it helps you eficientisize
response time, especially in situations when you create campaigns and
the search volumes are increasing on certain search periods. Your
customers will receive results faster, creating a better experience with
your website/platform.

Multiple resellers {#search-multiple-resellers}
------------------

TRIP IRIX accounts module allows the possibility of using multiple
resellers on your website.In the TRIP admin area, you can add the IRIX
resellers that were already created and enabled for webservice.

By adding the accounts here, TRIP will generate a unique ID, based on
which the searches on the website can be made.The accounts are available
using the API: **/tbs/accounts** and performing a GET request.This will
retrieve the ID and the name of the account, based on which you can map
your own criteria and add into the search request the correspondent ID.

### Flow Overview

The reseller account (accId) defines the context for the entire Search →
Validate → Book flow.

If a specific account is used during search, the same account context
must be preserved through validation and order creation.

### GET /tbs/accounts

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/tbs/accounts]{.url}
:::

This endpoint is used to retrieve reseller accounts and determine the
accId that will be applied to subsequent Search and Book requests.

### Account Resolution Rules

-   If accId is provided, TRIP performs the search in the context of the
    specified reseller account.
-   If accId is not provided, TRIP defaults to the configured reseller
    account.
-   When a specific account is used during search, it must also be used
    during booking.

### Headers

-   **x-accid** --- IRIX reseller ID
    -   Required for scoped searches and booking operations.

### Search Parameters

-   **accId** --- IRIX reseller ID used to scope the search.
    -   Can be retrieved dynamically from the GET /tbs/accounts response
        or reused as a fixed value.

**Example:**

\_s\[hCID\]\[h\]\[0\]\[accId\]: 1

\_s\[hCID\]\[f\]\[0\]\[accId\]: 1

### Book / Create Order

When adding services to an order after a search performed with a
specific account, the same account ID must be included in the order
request.

**Example:**

services\[hotel\]\[0\]\[accountId\]: 27

services\[flight\]\[0\]\[accountId\]: 27
:::

::: {#flights-service .section .content-section}
Flights Service {#flights-service-title}
===============

### Flight Search & Book Process

1.  [**Search for flights:** Find flight offers for certain routes and
    dates](#flights-search)
2.  [**Validate Offer & Get Ancillary services** Confirm availability
    and pricing](#flights-validate)
3.  [**Get Upsell offers** (if any)](#flights-branded-fares)
4.  [**Get Seat map & Paid seats** (if available)](#flights-paid-seats)
5.  [**Validate Offer** with extra services (seats; optional services,
    upsell branded fares)](#flights-validate)
6.  [**Create Order:** Initialize the order process\
    Add Traveller & Offer Details\
    Add extra services if any](#flights-orders)
7.  [**Payment:** Process payment](#payment-general)
8.  [**Confirmation:** Receive booking
    confirmation](#orders-get-specific)

Flight Search {#flights-search}
-------------

As it was explained on the Search Process page, to perform a search on
different services you have to define a container, by choosing a
container id, then you can add different services, \"f\" for flight, in
our case, in the container and make the search request. There are 3
types of fight search requests: oneway, roundtrip, multidestinations.
Each of them are identified using a special parameter, named type. All
of these types of flight search requests, should receive basically the
same parameters.

A one-way flight search is the simplest, requiring only the origin city,
destination city, and departure date. In contrast, a roundtrip search
also requires a return date and return route details. A
multi-destination search is similar to a roundtrip but allows for
multiple stopovers based on your preferences.

**It\'s mandatory to send one of the fields that identifies the
destination (city ID; city Code; location Id, location Code), you can
use any one of them.** If you choose to send them all and you add the
location ID in the request, please note that the search results will be
according to the location ID selected.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/dynamic-package]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Flight Search Parameters

Description
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

Type

Parameter

Value

Search types

int

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[type\]

0 - One way; 1 - Round trip; 2 - Multi-destinations

Search type: calendar

bool

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[calendar\]

1

Number of passengers - type adult

int

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[adt\]

Departure date

date

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[date\]

2024-12-24

Origin --- use exactly one of the following options

Origin location id

int

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[oLocId\]

Origin city id

int

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[oCityId\]

Origin city code

string

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[oCode\]

IATA code - 3 letters (PAR)

Destination --- use exactly one of the following options

Destination location id

int

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[dLocId\]

Destination city id

int

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[dCityId\]

Destination city code

string

\_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[dCode\]

### Calendar Search {#flights-calendar-search}

The calendar search returns the cheapest available fares for the
selected travel dates, as well as for nearby dates, including one day
before the departure date and one day after the return date.

The calendar search returns results in the same format as the regular
flight search.

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Warning

The results are supplier dependent, make sure the suppliers used are
offering calendar search. Moreover, make sure all IRIX settings are
properly done. For some suppliers, the calendar search might generate
extra costs.
:::
:::

### Roundtrip Parameters/MultiCity {#flights-roundtrip}

Round trip means adding another route on the request with the
destination from first route as origin point and the origin point from
first route as destination.

For multi city search you need to add multiple routes, each one with its
own parameters. Up to 5 routes.

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Example Parameters

  Description                   Type     Parameter                                           Value
  ----------------------------- -------- --------------------------------------------------- -------
  Return date                   date     \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[1\]\[date\]      
  The origin location id        int      \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[1\]\[oLocId\]    
  The origin city id            int      \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[1\]\[oCityId\]   
  The origin city code          string   \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[1\]\[oCode\]     
  The destination location id   int      \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[1\]\[dLocId\]    
  The destination city id       int      \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[1\]\[dCityId\]   
  The destination city code     string   \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[1\]\[dCode\]     
:::

### Additional Parameters {#flights-additional}

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Passenger and Filter Parameters

  Description                                    Type   Parameter                             Value
  ---------------------------------------------- ------ ------------------------------------- -------
  Number of passengers - type child.             int    \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[chd\]   
  Number of passengers - type senior.            int    \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[sen\]   
  Number of passengers - type youth.             int    \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[yth\]   
  Number of passengers - type infants in lap.    int    \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[inf\]   
  Number of passengers - type infants in seat.   int    \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[ins\]   
  Nationality of passenger.                      int    \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[nat\]   
:::

### Flight filters {#flights-filters}

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description           Type     Parameter                                      Value
  --------------------- -------- ---------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Cabine type           string   \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[class\]          Y-Economy class; F-First class; C-Business class; W-Premium economy class
  System (supplier)     string   \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[system\]         
  Only direct flights   bool     \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[direct\]         
  Search by airline     string   \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[airline\]\[0\]   
                                 \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[airline\]\[1\]   
                                 \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[airline\]\[2\]   
:::

### Flight time filters per route {#flights-time-filters}

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Time Filter Parameters

  Description                Type     Parameter                                          Value
  -------------------------- -------- -------------------------------------------------- --------------------
  departure\|arrival         string   \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[tMode\]    departure; arrival
  Time window start (hour)   time     \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[tStart\]   06:00
  Time window end (hour)     time     \_s\[ContainerId\]\[f\]\[0\]\[r\]\[0\]\[tEnd\]     23:00
:::

### Important Notes

-   You have to complete only one of the parameters that indicate the
    origin place or destination place. Either if it is the location code
    (airport) or the City ID or the codes.
-   Nationality ID (see here the nationalities API to obtain the ID
    list) - LATAM suppliers like GOL and AZUL require sending the
    nationality (ID from IRIX) at search for example:
    \_s\[CID\]\[f\]\[0\]\[nat\]: 5

<div>

Get Search Result Code/ Inspect SID {#flights-get-search-code}
-----------------------------------

After you make a search request, you will receive a search result code.
This code is used to retrieve the search results.

Make the inspect SID request to get the search result code. You need to
repeat the request until code is received. If the value is null, it
means there are no search results available for your request.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [dynamick-package/sid/{Search ID obtained from the
search request}]{.url}
:::
