Add service to order {#activities-add-service}
--------------------

[Go to Orders section](#orders-create) to see how the order is created,
how the service data is added, and what are the particularities of the
service.

### Extra order data

Conditional data per passenger: see here

Some suppliers, for some activity offer might require extra details.
They require extra information by adding extra attributes on the
Activity offer details rse. The fields will be listed on the property:
ServiceConfigurationForm.Field These fields should be listed as extra
esponfields in your flow and the values collected must be passed through
in the service information, on the order
:::

::: {#aida-packages .section .content-section}
AIDA Packages {#aida-packages-title}
=============

The new version of AIDA packages API comes with a direct API GET
requests, which can retrieve all the packages in the catalog. The API is
designed to retrieve the minimum price entry. Nonetheless, the list
should be filtered based on client preferences or selections, otherwise
the dataset might be too large.

Keep in mind that AIDA packages are highly configurable and it\'s
advisable to discuss with the agency what type of packages they need to
sell, what is the information they want to make available in the website
and to have some example packages in AIDA to take as an example in the
implementation

Depending on the type of package, data might be missing, for example, a
package only requires that a hotel service is added in order to create
that package, this means that some packages might not have
transportation or extra services.

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Custom Fields for Extra Traveler Information

AIDA offers the possibility of storing and requesting extra information
per traveler in the booking process. For detailed information on how to
configure and use custom fields, see the [**AIDA Custom Fields
section**](#aida-custom-fields) in Content Particularities.
:::
:::

### AIDA packages flow

1.  [**Get list of packages:** Filters can be added to target certain
    content or give the posibility of a dynamic serach form (using the
    summary list option)](#aida-packages-list)
2.  [**Get package details**](#aida-package-details)
3.  [**Get other entries for selected package**(if
    any)](#aida-package-entries)
4.  [**Get extra services** full details](#aida-extra-services)
5.  [**Validate offer (availability)** with extra services and rooms
    configuration](#aida-availability-checking)
6.  [**Create Order:** Initialize the order process\
    Add Traveller & Offer Details\
    Add extra services if any](#aida-add-package-service)
7.  [**Payment:** Process payment](#payment-general)
8.  [**Confirmation:** Receive booking
    confirmation](#orders-get-specific)

Packages list {#aida-packages-list}
-------------

The GET request for the list will retrieve the entire list of packages
available in the AIDA catalog, it\'s advisable to use filters to display
the packages in a structured way, based on client selections like
destinations, prefered period, travelers, etc..

Details like destinations available or even periods when packages are
available, can be obtained by using the parameter summary=true on the
packages list API. This can be helpful in creating a destinations list,
a calendar with available dates or even a more complex search form using
the available data. See more details in section Packages catalog summary

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/v2/packages]{.url}
:::

### Filters:

The list can be filtered by any of the data received in the results.

#### Examples:

##### General Filters

-   **AIDA Project ID:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Project.Id&filter\[0\]\[term\]=425
-   **Package Name:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=PackageName&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Dubai Luxury
    Package
-   **Package Category:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=PackageCategories.Code&filter\[0\]\[term\]=adventure
-   **Special Offers:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=RateType&filter\[0\]\[term\]=spo

##### Destination & Departure

-   **Destination City:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=DestinationCity.Id&filter\[0\]\[term\]=128
-   **Multiple Destination Cities:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=DestinationCity.Id&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[0\]=128&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[1\]=16
-   **Departure City:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=DepartureCity.Id&filter\[0\]\[term\]=9
-   **Departure Country:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=DepartureCity.Country.Id&filter\[0\]\[term\]=5

##### Accommodation Filters

-   **Hotel Stars:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Accommodation.Stars&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[0\]=3&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[1\]=5
-   **Meal Type:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Accommodation.AccRateTypeName&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Bed
    & breakfast
-   **Facilities by Name:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Accommodation.Facilities.Name&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Beach
-   **Facilities by Code:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Accommodation.Facilities.Code&filter\[0\]\[term\]=wif

##### Transportation

-   **Airline:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Transportation.Carrier&filter\[0\]\[term\]=TAROM
-   **Flight Type (Scheduled):**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Transportation.ServiceTypeCode&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Scheduled
-   **Flight Type (Charter):**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Transportation.ServiceTypeCode&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Charter

##### Date & Duration

-   **Start Date After:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=EntryStartDate&filter\[0\]\[term\]=2025-05-15&filter\[0\]\[type\]=greaterThanOrEqual
-   **Valid On:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=RateValidFrom&filter\[0\]\[term\]=2025-05-15&filter\[0\]\[type\]=lessThanOrEqual\
    filter\[1\]\[name\]=RateValidUntil&filter\[1\]\[term\]=2025-05-15&filter\[1\]\[type\]=greaterThanOrEqual
-   **Night Duration Between:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=EntryDuration&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[0\]=5&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[1\]=10&filter\[0\]\[type\]=between

##### Price

-   **Price Between:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Price&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[0\]=500&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[1\]=1000&filter\[0\]\[type\]=between

##### Other Useful Filters

-   **Packages with Specific Room Type:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Accommodation.RoomTypeCategoryCode&filter\[0\]\[term\]=SGL
-   **Facilities with Value Filters:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=Accommodation.Facilities.Name&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Balcony
-   **City Names Starting With:**
    filter\[0\]\[name\]=DestinationCity.Name&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Vi&filter\[0\]\[type\]=startsWith

**Note:** Entry start date of a package is related to the accommodation
checkin, if you want to display in the list of filter by departure
actual date, we recommend using the field TripStartDate. The value
retrieved in this field is related to the transportation departure date
and it will reflect the exact date of departure, not check-in. In some
cases the departure date is not the same as the check in date.

::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  Multi-language Support

This endpoint returns translations for package information using the
standard AIDA format. Translated fields include:

-   **Package Name & Description** - Available in `Translations[].Name`
    and `Translations[].Description`
-   **Location Data** - Country and city names with translations

Each translation object contains a `Lang` property indicating the
language code. See [Package Translations](#aida-package-translations)
for complete details.
:::
:::

::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  Flight Transportation

When the transportation in a package is built from a **standalone AIDA
Flight service**, it can be identified by its service codes:
`ServiceGroupCode` will be `AIR` and `ServiceTypeCode` will be either
`Scheduled` or `Charter`. This is what distinguishes it from the regular
package transportation service.

Use the `ServiceId` from this array to request full itinerary details
(stopovers, segments) via the [Transportation
Itineraries](#aida-transportation) endpoint.
:::
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Flight Transportation in Package Response
:::

    "Transportation": [
        {
            "ServiceId": "5263",
            "ServiceGroupCode": "AIR",
            "ServiceTypeCode": "Scheduled",
            "Code": "RO121",
            "Carrier": "TAROM",
            "FlightNo": "RO121",
            "Name": "Bucharest - Prague",
            "Type": "Scheduled",
            "Departure": {

                }
            }
        },
        {
            "ServiceId": "5264",
            "ServiceGroupCode": "AIR",
            "ServiceTypeCode": "Charter",
            "Code": "CH202",
            "Carrier": "Blue Air",

Packages catalog summary {#aida-catalog-summary}
------------------------

The endpoint was created to retrieve a summary of destinations and dates
available in the current AIDA catalog. Based on the data received in the
response you can build a dynamic search form, create lists of
destinations, dates or display the information in whatever form is
required by the design. Users can select destinations and dates and,
based on that, you can filter the packages list to obtain accurate
content for the user.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/v2/packages?summary=true]{.url}
:::

### Get

-   **Departure & Return dates** -- This can help populate a calendar or
    a list and display only the dates in which packages are available.
-   **Departures** -- This section will return the possible departure
    sections. The item is dedicated to a country and under it, a list of
    cities can be available as well.
-   **Destinations** will return the same structure as the Departures
    section and can have vast applicability, from displaying the
    available destinations in a search form, to implementing a widget
    with destinations and minimum price per destination or displaying
    the destinations on a map (with a minimum starting price).
-   **Entries** -- This section retrieves a list of routes (departure
    and destination city) with the assigned categories and the periods
    in which packages are available for those specific routes.

::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  Multi-language Support

The summary response includes translations for location data (countries
and cities) in the Departures and Destinations sections. Each location
object contains a `Translations` array with translated names per
language.

See [Package Translations](#aida-package-translations) for complete
details on the translation structure.
:::
:::

Package entries {#aida-package-entries}
---------------

Each package can have multiple entries (departure dates). In the
packages list, TRIP retrieves the cheapest entry, based on the filters
applied and to obtain all available departures for a package, the
entries request must be performed.

The entries are retrieved per room configuration only, therefore the
request must always contain the rooms and travelers.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/v2/packages/:Id]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                              Type     Parameter                     Value
  ---------------------------------------- -------- ----------------------------- -------
  First room & traveler adult              string   rooms\[0\]\[adults\]          
  First room & traveler child age (0-18)   string   rooms\[0\]\[children\]\[0\]   
:::

**Maximum rooms that can be requested:** 5

**Maximum number of adults per room:** 5

**Maximum number of children per room:** 3

**Child age:** 0-18

Package details {#aida-package-details}
---------------

Package details API is designed to bring all the necessary information
about a package. The request must be specific for a certain entry
(information which is provided on the list) and the selected room
configuration.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/v2/packages/:Id]{.url}
:::

::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Alternative Request Method

You can also use a **GET** request by including the same parameters used
in the POST request, passed as query string parameters in the request
URL.

This provides a convenient alternative to the POST method when you only
need to fetch or display package information.

**Example:**
`GET /v2/packages/:Id?entry=123&rooms[0][adults]=2&rooms[0][children][0]=5`
:::
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Package Details Parameters

  Description                                                                                        Type     Parameter                     Value
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------- ----------------------------- -------
  First room & traveler adult                                                                        string   rooms\[0\]\[adults\]          
  First room & traveler child age                                                                    string   rooms\[0\]\[children\]\[0\]   
  Entry                                                                                              string   entry                         
  Include documents attached to the package in the response (project, package, and/or entry level)   bool     includeDocuments              1
:::

### Holiday package - rooms examples:

Room information is available under the Occupations section and under
the Accommodations. The tag is called accommodations because in case of
Tour type packages, for each room type, you will have multiple hotels.

-   **1 room search with more than one room type** -
    Occupations\[0\].Accommodations\[0\]: The list of rooms given here
    is the list of options from which the customer can choose.
-   **2 room search with 2 room types** - The response has more than one
    item under the Occupation and it reflects how many rooms you have
    searched. Each Occupation can have one or more Accommodations items
    under it.

### Tour package - rooms examples:

Tour package type has a slightly different structure as it needs to have
multiple transportation itineraries and multiple hotels in distinct
locations.

Tour is also reflected in the package details by the tag Tour instead of
Transportation and by the fact that each Accommodation has more than one
Hotels item.

-   Opposed to the Holiday package type, the tour might have more than
    one item under the Hotels property. Still, each group of hotels is
    under the Occupation section, so you will find each hotel listed
    every time in the accommodation section. Based on this you can group
    the rooms under the hotels and display to the user the options that
    they have.

::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  Multi-language Support

Package details response includes comprehensive translations for:

-   **Package Info** - `Translations[].Name` and
    `Translations[].Description`
-   **Accommodation** - `RoomTypeTranslations`,
    `RoomFeatureTranslations`, `ShortDescription`, `LongDescription`
-   **Hotel Details** - `Hotels[].Translations[].Name`
-   **Location** - `City.Translations[].Name`,
    `Country.Translations[].Name`

See [Package Translations](#aida-package-translations) for the complete
field mapping when adding translated data to orders.
:::
:::

### Package Documents {#aida-package-documents}

To include documents attached to a package in the response, add
`includeDocuments=1` to the standard package details request. Documents
can be returned at project, package, or entry level depending on the
parameters provided.

**GET -- Project + Package documents only:**

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/v2/packages/:Id?entry={entryId}&rooms\[0\]\[adults\]=2&includeDocuments=1]{.url}
:::

**GET -- Project + Package + Entry documents (add EntryId filter):**

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/v2/packages/:Id?entry={entryId}&rooms\[0\]\[adults\]=2&includeDocuments=1&filter\[0\]\[name\]=EntryId&filter\[0\]\[term\]={entryId}]{.url}
:::

**POST -- include `includeDocuments` in the request body alongside the
other parameters:**

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
POST Body Example
:::

    {
      "entry": 79723,
      "rooms": [...],
      "includeDocuments": 1
    }
:::

#### Document Response Format

When `includeDocuments=1` is used, the package details response will
include a `Documents` array. Each object contains the document ID, type,
title, file name, and file size:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Documents Response Example
:::

    "Documents": [
        {
            "Id": "18",
            "Type": "ProjectDocument",
            "Title": "Project doc",
            "FileName": "Project_document.docx",
            "FileSize": 13315
        },
        {
            "Id": "250",
            "Type": "PackageDocument",
            "Title": "Package document",
            "FileName": "Package_document.docx",
            "FileSize": 13354
        },
        {
            "Id": "70",
            "Type": "PackageEntryDocument",
            "Title": "Package entry document",
            "FileName": "Package_entry_document.docx",
            "FileSize": 13351
        }
    ]
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Document Object Fields

  Field        Type     Description
  ------------ -------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  `Id`         string   Unique document identifier -- used for download
  `Type`       string   Document scope: `ProjectDocument`, `PackageDocument`, or `PackageEntryDocument`
  `Title`      string   Human-readable document title
  `FileName`   string   Original file name including extension
  `FileSize`   int      File size in bytes
:::

#### Downloading a Document

To download the actual file content, use the document `Id` and `Type`
from the documents response in a GET request to the same package
endpoint:

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/v2/packages/{packageId}?document\[id\]={documentId}&document\[type\]={documentType}]{.url}
:::

**Example:**

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/v2/packages/1242?document\[id\]=18&document\[type\]=ProjectDocument]{.url}
:::

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Response

Returns a **binary stream** of the document content with appropriate
headers for file download.
:::
:::

Transportation itineraries {#aida-transportation}
--------------------------

Based on the serviceId received in the package details/transportation
section, you can request extra details about the transport. For example,
in case of a flight, by requesting the details for each transportation
service, you can receive all the segments available, thus making it easy
to group and display the stopovers, flight number and other useful
details about the flight itinerary.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/v2/:packageId/check/itinerary]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Transportation Itinerary Parameters

  Description   Type     Parameter   Value
  ------------- -------- ----------- -------
  Entry ID      string   entryId     
  Service ID    string   service     
:::

### Response Example

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Transportation Itinerary Response
:::

::: {.code-content}
    {
        "Id": 78557,
        "StartDate": "2025-08-08",
        "EndDate": "2025-08-15",
        "Transportation": {
            "ServiceID": 5201,
            "Name": "BUCHAREST - VIENA",
            "Segment": [
                {
                    "FlightNo": "RO123",
                    "FlightClass": "ECONOMY",
                    "Carrier": "TAROM",
                    "MaxKilos": 23,
                    "Departure": {
                        "Date": "2025-08-08",
                        "Time": "08:00:00",
                        "Place": "Henri Coanda International Airport",
                        "City": {
                            "Id": 9,
                            "Name": "Bucharest",
                            "ISO": "BUH",
                            "CountryId": 5,
                            "RegionId": 0,
                            "Latitude": null,
                            "Longitude": null
                        },
                        "Country": {
                            "Id": 5,
                            "Name": "Romania",
                            "ISO": "RO",
                            "Latitude": null,
                            "Longitude": null
                        },
                        "Location": null
                    },
                    "Arrival": {
                        "Date": "2025-08-08",
                        "Time": "10:00:00",
                        "Place": "Vienna International Airport",
                        "City": {
                            "Id": 16,
                            "Name": "Vienna",
                            "ISO": null,
                            "CountryId": 10,
                            "RegionId": 0,
                            "Latitude": null,
                            "Longitude": null
                        },
                        "Country": {
                            "Id": 10,
                            "Name": "Austria",
                            "ISO": "AT",
                            "Latitude": null,
                            "Longitude": null
                        },
                        "Location": null
                    }
                }
            ]
        },
        "_links": {
            "self": {
                "href": "\"
            }
        }
    }
:::
:::

Package extra services {#aida-extra-services}
----------------------

Besides the main services (accommodation and transportation), a package
can have a series of secondary services from which the user can choose.
Some of the services are mandatory, which means they are already
included in the price. The optional ones can be added to the package.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/v2/packages/:Id/check/extra-services]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Extra Services Parameters

  Description                       Type     Parameter                     Value
  --------------------------------- -------- ----------------------------- -------
  First room & traveler adult       string   rooms\[0\]\[adults\]          
  First room & traveler child age   string   rooms\[0\]\[children\]\[0\]   
  Entry                             string   entry                         
  Entry start date                  string   entryStartDate                
  Entry end date                    string   entryEndDate                  
  Package type (tour or holiday)    string   packageType                   
:::

The API will retrieve a list of additional services. Each service will
have a list of properties which will either determine how they can be
booked or will describe the services:

-   **Service is mandatory or optional:**
    \_extra\_services\[0\].Mandatory: false/true
-   **Who can buy or benefit of that service:**
    -   extra\_services\[0\].BookingRules.AllowedOccupantTypes: a/c/i -
        In case the option is only a or c/i, it means the service is
        designed only for adults or only for children, so it cannot be
        bought for the traveler type which is not mentioned in the
        response.
    -   extra\_services\[0\].BookingRules.BookOnlyForAllOccupants:
        true - This means that the user cannot choose this service only
        for some of the travelers.
    -   extra\_services\[0\].BookingRules.MandatoryGuests - The
        information provided in this section can provide details about
        the age requirement for booking that service or if it is
        mandatory only for a specific type of traveler.
-   **Period or date** - One service can have one or more entries and
    each entry can be designed as a period/interval or a fixed date.
-   **Price sets** - A service can have multiple options which can mean
    an upgrade or an addition to that service.
-   **If the option MultipleEntries on extra service is True,** it means
    that for the same service you can select multiple dates.

### Images for Extra Services

New data is available in the response of the Extra services AIDA package
response: **Gallery**. The information is available per extra service.

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Gallery Information

The tag `MainPicture` indicates if the image was marked as main in AIDA
configuration.
:::
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Extra Service Gallery Response Example
:::

::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  Multi-language Support

Extra services response includes translations for service names and
price set options:

-   **Service Name** - `extra_services[].Translations[].Name`
-   **Price Set Name** -
    `extra_services[].PriceSets[].Translations[].Name`

When adding extra services to an order, use the translated values to
ensure proper language display. See [Package
Translations](#aida-package-translations) for the complete order field
mapping.
:::
:::

### Supplements {#aida-supplements}

Supplements are optional add-ons that can be attached to an extra
service. They represent additional selections or upgrades that a
customer may choose on top of an extra service --- for example, a
specific seat category, a meal upgrade, or a room enhancement.

When defined in AIDA for an extra service, supplements are returned in
the Extra Services API response and can be selected by the customer
during the booking flow. They must then be included in both the
availability request and the order POST service data.

#### Relationship to Price Set IDs

Supplements may or may not be linked to a price set ID:

-   **Linked to a Price Set ID:** When a supplement has an associated
    price set ID, it means that supplement belongs specifically to that
    price set. In this case, the supplement must only be used together
    with the matching price set ID selected by the user. Your
    implementation should display or apply only the supplements whose
    price set ID matches the one the user selected.
-   **Not linked to a Price Set ID:** Supplements can also exist
    independently, without any association to a price set. In this case,
    they can be selected stand-alone and sent in both the availability
    request and the order POST service data without needing to specify a
    `price-set` parameter.

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Important

Whenever a supplement is selected --- with or without a price set ID ---
an availability request must be triggered to retrieve the updated price
that reflects the supplement\'s cost. The supplement (and the price set
ID, if applicable) must also be included in the order POST data.
:::
:::

#### Payload Examples

##### Availability Request

**Without price set ID** --- supplement selected stand-alone:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Availability Request --- Supplement without Price Set ID
:::

::: {.code-content}
    extra-services[5243][supplements][0]: 408
    extra-services[5243][entries][0]: 2026-04-06_1
:::
:::

**With price set ID** --- supplement linked to a specific price set:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Availability Request --- Supplement with Price Set ID
:::

::: {.code-content}
    extra-services[5243][supplements][0]: 408
    extra-services[5243][entries][0]: 2026-04-06_1
    extra-services[5243][price-set]: 32
:::
:::

##### Order POST Data for Package Service

**Without price set ID** --- supplement selected stand-alone:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Order POST Data --- Supplement without Price Set ID
:::

::: {.code-content}
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][occupants][0]: 1
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][occupants][1]: 2
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][entries][0]: 2026-04-06_1
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][name]: Transfer airport - hotel - airport Prague
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][supplements][0]: 408
:::
:::

**With price set ID** --- supplement linked to a specific price set:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Order POST Data --- Supplement with Price Set ID
:::

::: {.code-content}
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][occupants][0]: 1
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][occupants][1]: 2
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][entries][0]: 2026-04-06_1
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][name]: Transfer airport - hotel - airport Prague
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][supplements][0]: 408
    services[package][0][extra-services][5243][price-set]: 235
:::
:::

Package availability checking {#aida-availability-checking}
-----------------------------

Before finalizing a package booking, you must check availability to
ensure all selected services and rooms are still available at the
requested dates.

### Availability Check Process

1.  **Select Package:** Choose the desired package from the catalog
2.  **Select Rooms:** Choose room IDs for each searched room type
3.  **Select Extra Services:** Include mandatory and optional extra
    services
4.  **Configure Services:** Set dates and price sets for extra services
5.  **Validate Availability:** Check real-time availability

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/v2/packages/:Id/check/availability]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Availability Check Parameters

  Description                              Type     Parameter                                                                Value
  ---------------------------------------- -------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------ -------------------
  First room & traveler adult              string   rooms\[0\]\[adults\]                                                     2
  First room & traveler child age          string   rooms\[0\]\[children\]\[0\]                                              0-18\*
  Entry                                    string   entry                                                                    
  Entry start date                         string   entryStartDate                                                           2023-07-23
  Entry end date                           string   entryEndDate                                                             2023-07-30
  Package type (tour or holiday)           string   packageType                                                              holiday
  Rate group ID                            string   rateGroupId                                                              0
  Room ID                                  string   occupations\[0\]\[rooms\]\[0\]                                           4729\_7309\_25876
  Room ID room 1                           string   occupations\[0\]\[rooms\]\[0\]                                           4729\_7309\_25876
  Room ID room 2                           string   occupations\[1\]\[rooms\]\[0\]                                           73\_81\_118
  Extra services associated per traveler   string   occupations\[0\]\[extra-services\]\[:extra service ID\]\[a\]             1
  Extra services associated per traveler   string   occupations\[1\]\[extra-services\]\[:extra service ID\]\[a\]             1
  Extra services associated per traveler   string   occupations\[0\]\[extra-services\]\[:extra service ID\]\[c\]\[0\]: age   1
  Extra service entry date/period          string   extra-services\[:extra service ID\]\[entries\]\[0\]                      2022-07-14\_1
:::

### Extra Services Validation

When validating an offer with extra services, there are a few main
important things to remember:

#### Extra Service Selection Requirements

The extra services must be selected for:

-   **Room** - Specify which room the service applies to
-   **Type of occupant/passenger** - Use passenger type codes (a or c)

The price rates and dates (entries) must be selected for each extra
service that was selected. These configurations are available at extra
service level, no matter how many or what type of passenger selected
them.

If the option **MultipleEntries** on extra service is True, it means
that for the same service you can select multiple dates.

#### Passenger Type Codes

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
-   **\"a\"** - adults
-   **\"c\"** - children
-   **\"i\"** - infant
:::
:::

#### Booking Rules Configuration

For which type of passengers it is important to select the service based
on the indications:

-   **MandatoryGuests** - Defines which guests must have the service
-   **AgeQualifyingCode** - Specifies age-based passenger categories
-   **Count** - Number of passengers requiring the service
-   **Age** - Age restrictions for the service

### Availability Request Example

Below is a complete example of an availability request payload for two
rooms with extra services:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Availability Request Payload - Two Rooms Example
:::

::: {.code-content}
    entry=79131
    entryStartDate=2025-08-13
    entryEndDate=2025-08-20
    packageType=holiday
    rateGroupId=0
    rooms[0][adults]=2
    occupations[0][rooms][0]=5467_8529_30357
    rooms[1][adults]=2
    rooms[1][children][0]=8
    occupations[1][rooms][0]=5467_8529_30360
    occupations[0][extra-services][5219][a]=2
    occupations[1][extra-services][5219][a]=2
    occupations[1][extra-services][5219][c][0]=8
    extra-services[5219][entries][0]=2025-08-13_8
:::
:::

#### Request Breakdown

-   **Entry & Dates:** Package entry 79131 from 2025-08-13 to 2025-08-20
-   **Package Type:** Holiday package with rate group 0
-   **Room 1:** 2 adults in room 5467\_8529\_30357
-   **Room 2:** 2 adults + 1 child (age 8) in room 5467\_8529\_30360
-   **Extra Service 5219:** Applied to 2 adults in room 1, 2 adults + 1
    child (age 8) in room 2
-   **Service Entry:** Extra service entry for 2025-08-13 with period 8

### Tour Package Request Example

Here\'s an example of an availability request for a Tour package with
multiple room selections per accommodation:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Tour Package Availability Request
:::

::: {.code-content}
    entry=78251
    entryStartDate=2025-08-16
    entryEndDate=2025-08-26
    packageType=tour
    rateGroupId=0
    rooms[0][adults]=2
    occupations[0][rooms][0]=5163_5473_8541_30395
    occupations[0][rooms][1]=5188_5480_8552_30437
    occupations[0][rooms][2]=5189_5483_8558_30455
    rooms[1][adults]=2
    occupations[1][rooms][0]=5163_5473_8541_30395
    occupations[1][rooms][1]=5188_5480_8552_30437
    occupations[1][rooms][2]=5189_5483_8558_30455
:::
:::

#### Tour Package Request Breakdown

-   **Entry & Dates:** Package entry 78251 from 2025-08-16 to 2025-08-26
    (10-day tour)
-   **Package Type:** Tour package with rate group 0
-   **Room 1:** 2 adults with 3 different accommodation options
-   **Room 2:** 2 adults with the same 3 accommodation options
-   **Multi-Stop Tour:** Each room has multiple accommodation selections
    for different tour stops
-   **Accommodation IDs:**
    -   5163\_5473\_8541\_30395 - First accommodation stop
    -   5188\_5480\_8552\_30437 - Second accommodation stop
    -   5189\_5483\_8558\_30455 - Third accommodation stop

### Room Occupancy Validation

Make sure to align room selection fields with the RoomOccupancy
specifications from the availability response to ensure correct
validation and avoid rejection of the booking.

#### Important Notes:

-   **Always validate** the selected room against the RoomOccupancy
    definition before finalizing an order
-   **Child age eligibility** is strict; ages outside the specified
    range will not be accepted
-   **Room capacity** must match the specified adult and child limits
-   **Age requirements** must be verified for each child passenger

### Availability Request -- Prices for Each Extra Service

In the AIDA package availability response, for each extra service the
price and currency will be available. Along with the selling price, the
price components can be available as well.

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Pricing Information

Each extra service in the availability response now includes detailed
pricing information with currency and price components breakdown.
:::
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Availability Response - Extra Service Pricing Example
:::

::: {.code-content}
      "ExtraServices": [
            {
                "ID": null,
                "Name": "SPA treatment - Hilton Prague",
                "Type": "SPA Procedures per period",
                "Mandatory": null,
                "ServiceID": "5219",
                "Price": {
                    "Ammount": "160.00",
                    "CurrencyCode": "EUR",

                        "Ammount": "0.00"
                    }
                }
            }
        ]
:::
:::

Add package service on order {#aida-add-package-service}
----------------------------

After checking availability and confirming all details, you can add the
package service to an order for booking.

### Package Booking Process

After you have taken into consideration all of the above, the Check
availability request should be done in the following way:

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/orders]{.url}
:::

### Package Order Example

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Package Service Order Request
:::

    services[package][0][packageId]: PKG123456
    services[package][0][departureDate]: 2024-06-15
    services[package][0][rooms][0][roomId]: RM001
    services[package][0][rooms][0][adults]: 2
    services[package][0][rooms][0][children]: 1
    services[package][0][rooms][0][childAges][0]: 8
    services[package][0][extraServices][0][serviceId]: ES001
    services[package][0][extraServices][0][date]: 2024-06-16
    services[package][0][extraServices][0][priceSet]: premium
:::

### Mandatory vs Optional Services

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Service Configuration

  Service Type             Required   Configuration
  ------------------------ ---------- -------------------------------------------
  Mandatory Services       Yes        Must be included in every booking
  Optional Services        No         Can be added based on customer preference
  Date-specific Services   Varies     Must specify exact dates when applicable
  Price Set Services       Varies     Choose from available pricing tiers
:::

### AIDA Custom Fields for Extra Traveler Information {#aida-custom-fields}

AIDA offers the possibility of storing and requesting extra information
per traveler in the booking process. The fields are defined first in
AIDA, based on the information that you need to collect.

#### AIDA - How to Add and Configure the Fields:

In AIDA the custom fields can be added from **Reservations -- Passengers
custom Fields -- Add Field**. The custom fields information must
include:

-   **Name** (mandatory)
-   **Code** (mandatory)
-   **Description** (optional)

#### Integration with TRIP:

In TRIP the fields are imported whenever the static data request
**Codes** is done. The fields are available in the Package availability
response.

#### Custom Fields in Availability Response:

When custom fields are configured in AIDA, they appear in the package
availability response under the `CustomFields` section. Each field
includes the field ID, name, and other properties.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Package Availability Response - Custom Fields
:::

::: {.code-content}
    {
        "Transport": [...],
        "CustomFields":{
         "Pax":[
            {
                "FieldId": "101",
                "Name": "Dietary Requirements"
            },
            {
                "FieldId": "102",
                "Name": "Emergency Contact"
            },
            {
                "FieldId": "103",
                "Name": "Special Assistance"
            }
          ]
        },
        "Payment": {...}
    }
:::
:::

#### Booking Process:

At book, the fields can be sent per traveler using the FieldId from the
availability response in brackets.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Custom Field Booking Example
:::

::: {.code-content}
    // Package service with custom fields per passenger
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][0][docIssuingCom]: RO
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][0][docPaxNational]: RO
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][0][docExpiry][Date]: 2025-06-12
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][0][details][TEST]: YES
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][0][details][TEST2]: NO
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][0][details][Test]: Iaprovare

    // Second passenger
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][title]: 2
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][type]: 4
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][surname]: Joan
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][lastName]: Doe
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][links]: Ms
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][email]: alexandra.serban@dcsplus.net
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][phone]: 123123123
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][docType]: 0
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][docNumber]: 123123123123
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][docIssuingCom]: RO
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][docPaxNational]: RO
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][docExpiry][Date]: 2026-06-16
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][details][TEST]: NO
    services[package][0][occupations][0][occupants][1][details][Test]: Iaprovareaprovare

    // Package details
    services[package][0][packageId]: 1007
    services[package][0][entryId]: 1
:::
:::

#### Data Access in AIDA:

The information will be available in AIDA in **Reservations --
Reservation Details -- Passengers -- Custom Fields**.

Post Book Documents {#aida-post-book-documents}
-------------------

AIDA packages support automatic document delivery to customers after
booking completion. There are two distinct types of documents that are
generated by AIDA and sent by TRIP to enhance the customer experience.

### Document Types

There are two distinct types of documents available for AIDA packages:

#### 1. Vouchers

Vouchers are travel-related documents that contain booking confirmations
. These are only generated and sent when the order has been fully paid.

-   **Generation:** Created by AIDA after payment confirmation
-   **Delivery:** Sent by TRIP via email
-   **Trigger:** Only sent when payment is completed
-   **Content:** Booking vouchers

#### 2. Reservation Details Documents

Reservation details documents contain comprehensive travel information
and package details. These are sent regardless of payment status once
the reservation is completed.

-   **Generation:** Created by AIDA after reservation completion
-   **Delivery:** Sent by TRIP via email
-   **Trigger:** Sent immediately after reservation completion
-   **Content:** Travel itinerary, package details, important travel
    information

### Document Delivery Process

The timing and content of document delivery depends on the document type
and selected payment method:

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Document Delivery by Payment Method

  Payment Method   Vouchers                Reservation Details    Delivery Timing
  ---------------- ----------------------- ---------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Credit Card      ✓ Sent after payment    ✓ Sent after payment   Both documents sent together after payment completion
  Bank Transfer    ✗ Not sent until paid   ✓ Sent immediately     Reservation details sent in confirmation email; vouchers sent after payment
  Cash Payment     ✗ Not sent until paid   ✓ Sent immediately     Reservation details sent in confirmation email; vouchers sent after payment
:::

Reservation Synchronization & Amend {#aida-reservation-sync}
-----------------------------------

The reservation changes made in AIDA are also reflected in TRIP. Please
note that updates are not applied instantly; they are imported based on
a scheduled cron job that runs once per day.

### How it works

-   TRIP executes a daily cron job that queries AIDA for all active
    reservations (those with an entry date that is not in the past).
-   If a reservation has status AM, TRIP imports the updated
    information, replacing the existing service data and updating the
    reservation status accordingly.
-   Through this cron process, the reservation status in TRIP is also
    adjusted automatically - for example, from RQ to OK, or from RQ/OK
    to Cancelled (XX).

### Benefits

-   TRIP remains continuously synchronized with AIDA.
-   The latest reservation updates can be accurately displayed in the
    client account.

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  Attention

The order and service prices will remain unchanged and will not
interfere with any amounts already paid.

A new field (`NewAmount`) has been added at the order service level.
:::
:::

### Amends Data Structure

When a reservation is amended, the amendment details are available in
the order service response under the `Amends` array.

The `ServiceDataSnapshot` field contains a JSON-encoded string of the
complete service state. This is a snapshot of the old reservation before
the amendment was applied. If the initial reservation was amended in
AIDA multiple times, each amendment will be recorded as a separate entry
in the `Amends` array, preserving the history of all previous
reservation states.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Order Service - Amends Example
:::

    "Amends": [
        {
            "Id": 501,
            "ServiceId": 1001,
            "OldReservationId": "AIDA123456",
            "NewReservationId": "AIDA123457",
            "NewAmount": 2600.00,
            "Code": "AMEND001",
            "Status": "Confirmed",
            "AmendCount": 1,
            "ServiceDataSnapshot": "{...json snapshot...}",
            "Timestamp": "2026-02-01 14:30:00"
        }
    ]
:::

Package Translations {#aida-package-translations}
--------------------

Multi-language support has been added for AIDA packages, using the
standard AIDA format (a list of objects, each containing a `Lang`
property and the relevant translated fields).

### Translatable Fields

The following package elements support multi-language translations:

#### Package Information

-   **Name** - Package name translations
-   **Description** - Package description translations

#### Accommodation Details

-   **RoomFeatureTranslations** - Room feature descriptions in multiple
    languages
-   **RoomTypeTranslations** - Room type names in multiple languages
-   **ShortDescription and LongDescription** - Accommodation
    descriptions

#### Location Data

-   **Country names** - Translated country names
-   **City names** - Translated city names
-   **Location name** - Translated location names

### API Endpoints with Translations

The translations are available in the following API requests:

-   **Packages summary** - `/v2/packages?summary=true`
-   **Packages list** - `/v2/packages`
-   **Package Details** - `/v2/packages/:packId`

### Translation Structure

Understanding how translations are structured in API responses:

-   The translations will be encountered at the same level as the items
    translated
-   All translations will be available under objects per language
-   The language is indicated by the field `Lang`

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Translation Structure Example
:::

    {
        "Name": "Dubai Luxury Package",
        "Translations": [
            {
                "Lang": "en_EN",
                "Name": "Dubai Luxury Package"
            },
            {
                "Lang": "de_DE",
                "Name": "Dubai Luxuspaket"
            },
            {
                "Lang": "fr_FR",
                "Name": "Forfait Luxe Dubaï"
            }
        ]
    }
:::

### Adding Translated Information to Orders

To ensure the translated package information appears on the order, make
sure to save the order details in the translated format.

Below is a reference table listing the fields that can be added to the
order, along with the corresponding API sections from where the
translated information can be obtained:

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Order Field Mapping for Translations

  Order Field Path                  Source API                                      Translation Field Location
  --------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  `Package.Name`                    `v2/packages/:packId`                           `Translations[0].Name`
  `Rooms[0].RoomName`               `v2/packages/:packId`                           `Occupations[0].Accommodations[0].Hotels[0].RoomTypeTranslations[0].Name` + `Occupations[0].Accommodations[0].Hotels[0].RoomFeatureTranslations[0].Name`
  `Rooms[0].RoomTypeDescription`    `v2/packages/:packId`                           `Occupations[0].Accommodations[0].Hotels[0].RoomTypeTranslations[0].Name`
  `Rooms[0].RoomFeature`            `v2/packages/:packId`                           `Occupations[0].Accommodations[0].Hotels[0].RoomFeatureTranslations[0].Name`
  `Rooms[0].UnitName`               `v2/packages/:packId`                           `Occupations[0].Accommodations[0].Hotels[0].Translations[0].Name`
  `Rooms[0].CityName`               `v2/packages/:packId`                           `Occupations[0].Accommodations[0].Hotels[0].City.Translations[0].Name`
  `ExtraServices[0].Name`           `v2/packages/:packId`                           `ExtraServices[0].Translations[0].Name`
  `ExtraServices[0].PriceSetName`   `v2/packages/:packageId/check/extra-services`   `extra_services[0].PriceSets[0].Translations[0].Name`
  `ExtraServices[1].Name`           `v2/packages/:packageId/check/extra-services`   `extra_services[0].PriceSets[0].Translations[0].Name`
:::

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Note on Order Service Path

The order field paths listed above follow the structure:
`services[package][0].FieldName`

When adding package details to an order, use the translated values from
the corresponding API endpoints to ensure proper language display.
:::
:::
:::

Products Service APIs {#products-service-title}
=====================

Product types {#products-types}
-------------

The Products section will allow you to create and insert new fields,
using only TRIP\'s administration interface.

By going to the Admin area/ Services/Products/Products Fields
Definition, you will be able to:

-   Add a new type of product (+)
-   Create and customize fields that are automatically inserted in the
    database

The fields added will be saved in the database and they will be
available in the Products list section/ Add new product, based on the
type selected.Using the CONFIG section in the Products Fields Definition
section, you can create fields that will allow you to store multiple
values on the same field.

[GET]{.method .get} [/store/product-types]{.url}

### The products list with price categories

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/store/product-price-categories/\*/price-categories?limit=100]{.url}
:::

The number of results is limited, and it is highly recommended to
decrease the limit value if there are multiple price categories in each
event.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Product Price Categories Response Example
:::
:::

### Products with price categories and prices calculated - records API

Records endpoint is a versatile API that retrieves products and price
categories (with the price already calculated if you input the quantity
to book/selected by client.

It can be used to filter and retrive multiple products with their price
categories. For example to retrive all products with price categories
and their prices on a specific custom filed added, you can use:
/store/records?filter\[0\]\[name\]=Types.Field&filter\[0\]\[term\]=CityId&filter\[1\]\[name\]=Types.FieldValue&filter\[1\]\[term\]=12131&limit=100

It can also be used to GET the prices already calculated fir a specific
product and price category:
/store/records\[/:product\_id\[/quantity/:quantity\[/price-category/:product\_price\_category\_id\]\]\]

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/store/records]{.url}
:::

Product Filter {#products-filter}
--------------

### Product Price Category Details

The results can be filtered by any of the fields received in the
response. Multiple filters can be applied

For example, having the types, you can directly filter the results,
based on the type-
/store/products?limit=10&page=1&filter\[0\]\[name\]=Type&filter\[0\]\[term\]=
{name received in the products types list}

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/store/products?limit=10&page=1&filter\[0\]\[name\]=Type&filter\[0\]\[term\]=
{name received in the products types list}]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Filter Parameters

  Description                         Type     Parameter     Value
  ----------------------------------- -------- ------------- -------
  The Filter name                     string   :type         
  Filter field Value to be searched   string   :fieldvalue   
:::

The lists requests will always give you minimum information and it is
always paginated.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Filtered Products Response Example
:::
:::

### List Data

The results can be filtered by one custom field at a time. If you filter
by data from a second level (types --the custom fields), you need to add
also: filter\[1\]\[name\]=Types.Field&filter\[1\]\[term\]={field name}
&filter\[2\]\[name\]=Types.FieldValue& filter\[2\]\[term\]={value}

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Product Data Fields

  Description                                               Parameter     Value
  --------------------------------------------------------- ------------- ----------
  The default data for product is                                         
  Based on this you can request details about the product   Id            int
  Price for the product                                     Price         string
  Currency Code                                             Currency      string
  Status                                                    1/0           boolen
  The name of the event defined in the admin area           Name          string
  Extra fields from the custom area                                       
  Image                                                     Name          URL type
  Description about product defined in the admin area       description   string
  Other field about product defined in the admin area       other         text
:::

The fields need to be defined in the config area and the field name must
be a perfect match with the above items.

Products price categories
-------------------------

For each product you can have one or multiple price categories attached.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/store/product-price-categories/{ID}/price-categories]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description       Type     Parameter   Value
  ----------------- -------- ----------- -------
  The Filter name   string   {Id}        
:::

The request will return

-   Price category type -Price category name
-   Price category validity period
-   Price category quantity (RQ and OK)
-   Formula-from this you can calculate the price
    1.  AMT --product price
    2.  QTY --available quantity
    3.  RQTY --on request quantity
    4.  BQTY --booked quantity (number of items selected by the user)

Based on the formula retrieved, you can calculate the price of price
category received.

This is a direct API that will retrieve the raw data as it is stored in
the database.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Product Price Categories Response Example
:::
:::

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/store/records\[/:product\_id\[/quantity/:quantity\[/price-category/:product\_price\_category\_id\]\]\]]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Records Parameters

  Description                 Type     Parameter                        Value
  --------------------------- -------- -------------------------------- -------
  Product id                  string   {product\_id}                    
  Quantity                    string   {quantity}                       
  Product Price Category Id   string   {product\_price\_category\_id}   
:::

-   If you send the product ID, the request will retrieve the price of
    that product and for all the price categories (for one item)
-   If you will also the send the quantity, the request will retrieve
    the price already calculated based on the value sent by you
-   If you also send the product price category ID, you will receive the
    price calculated only for that category

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Product Records Response Example
:::
:::

Product Orders {#products-orders}
--------------

### Create the order with product on it

The book requests are the same that you make for hotel, the difference
is in the service information added when you create the order. After
creating the order and adding the service, the rest of the requests (add
payment method, pay and book are the same as they are for other
sevrices).

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/orders]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Product Order Parameters

  Description                              Type     Parameter                                        Value
  ---------------------------------------- -------- ------------------------------------------------ -------
  The product Id of service.               string   services\[product\]\[0\]\[productId\]            
  Price Category Id                        string   services\[product\]\[0\]\[priceCategoryId\]      
  Start date (price category start date)   date     services\[product\]\[0\]\[details\]\[DateIn\]    
  End Date (price category end date)       date     services\[product\]\[0\]\[details\]\[DateOut\]   
  The price of the price category.         float    services\[product\]\[0\]\[amount\]               
  The currency of the price category.      string   services\[product\]\[0\]\[currency\]             
  Quantity selected by customer.           float    services\[product\]\[0\]\[quantity\]             
:::

#### Owner data - Generic order information

::: {.parameters-table}
  Description                     Type     Parameter            Value
  ------------------------------- -------- -------------------- -------
  Mr, Mrs \...                    string   owner\[title\]       
  The first name of the person.   string   owner\[firstname\]   
  The last name of the person.    string   owner\[lastname\]    
  Owner e-mail.                   string   owner\[email\]       
:::
:::

::: {#event-module .section .content-section}
Event Module {#event-module-title}
============

The modules available under Event manager (Agency admin) are complex
tools with extended functionalities that will allow the configuration of
complex widgets and selling systems.

The admin area allows you to define event or entity types (unlimited),
each type can have a set of fields that can be created and managed from
the admin area. Those fields will allow you to create events on which
you can store information in the database in a structured manner.

The data stored will be available via REST API and can be filtered,
sorted and used in any way you need.

By defining the fields that need to store the content, defining
categories and adding the content itself, you can easily promote and
link the travel services to any event.

Having all this configured, pages can be created from where the user can
book services, request more details, or maybe just register for future
updates.

-   **Simple widgets to promote targeted offers.** By adding the fields
    to store destination, travel dates, even a specific hotel or an
    airline, the events module can feed a promotion widget for example
    from where the user can book a specific custom offer.

The events module also comes by default with a validity period and using
this, you don\'t have to worry about manually removing expired offers,
the validity period needs to be set and the front-end development needs
to take the validity period into consideration when listing the events.

Event types
-----------

If you have added multiple types and you want to obtain them
dynamically, you can use the below request.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/event-manager/event-types]{.url}
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Event Types Response Example
:::

    {
      "_links": {3 items},
      "_embedded": {1 item},
      "page_count": 1,
      "page_size": 1000,
      "total_items": 10,
      "page": 1
    }
:::

Event list
----------

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/event-manager/events]{.url}
:::

The results can be filtered by any of the fields received in the
response. For example, having the types, you can directly filter the
results, based on the type:
/event-manager/events?limit=10&page=1&filter\[0\]\[name\]=Type&filter\[0\]\[term\]=
{name received in the events types list}

The results can be filtered by any of the fields received in the
response.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Event List Response Example
:::

    {
      "_links": {3 items},
      "_embedded": {1 item},
      "page_count": 1,
      "page_size": 1000,
      "total_items": 25,
      "page": 1
    }
:::

If you want to obtain on the events list all data saved on an event, you
can use event-manager/events/\*/languages/default. Keep in mind that the
dataset in the response might become very large if you have a lot of
events and data on them, so we strongly advise in using filters and
pagination to have an optimal response time.

Event list with Filter {#event-list-filter}
----------------------

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/event-manager/events?limit=10&page=1&filter\[0\]\[name\]=Type&filter\[0\]\[term\]={name
from response}]{.url}
:::

The lists requests will always give you minimum information and it is
always paginated.

The fields need to be defined in the config area and the field name must
be a perfect match with the above items.

Always check the response JSON and if you have more than one page at
\"page\_count\", make sure you make the request for the rest of the
pages in order to receive all the possible results.

The results can be filtered by one custom field at a time. If you filter
by data from a second level (types -- the custom fields), you need to
add also: filter\[1\]\[name\]=Types.Field&filter\[1\]\[term\]={field
name} &filter\[2\]\[name\]=Types.FieldValue& filter\[2\]\[term\]={value}

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Filtered Event List Response Example
:::

    {
      "_links": {1 item},
      "_embedded": {1 item},
      "page_count": 0,
      "page_size": 10,
      "total_items": 0,
      "page": 0
    }
:::

Event multi language content {#event-multi-language}
----------------------------

TRIP admin area and the API can offer the multi language support for
events.

If the languages are defined in TRIP\'s admin area and the events added
are also configured in other languages, you can obtain the information
in the defined languages by using the events languages API.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [event-manager/events/\*/languages/:language
code]{.url}
:::

This request will retrieve the events list with the event information
added on the respective language.

Event details
-------------

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/event-manager/events/:Id]{.url}
:::

or

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [event-manager/events/:identifier]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                             Type     Parameter            Value
  --------------------------------------- -------- -------------------- -------
  id or identifier received in response   string   {identifier or id}   
:::

Either one of the above requests will return the event details added in
the admin area.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Event Details Response Example
:::

    {
      "_links": {3 items},
      "_embedded": {1 item},
      "page_count": 1,
      "page_size": 1,
      "total_items": 1,
      "page": 1
    }
:::

Linked entities {#event-linked-entities}
---------------

Based on the admin configuration, you can link entities to events and
use them based on project needs.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[event-manager/events-entities/{eventId}/entities]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                     Type     Parameter            Value
  ------------------------------- -------- -------------------- -------
  Event id received in response   string   {identifier or id}   
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Linked Entities Response Example
:::

    {
        "_links": {
            "self": {
                "href": "/index.php\/event-manager\/events-entities\/3\/entities?page=1"
            },
            "first": {
                "href": "/public\/index.php\/event-manager\/events-entities\/3\/entities"
            },
            "last": {
                "href": "/index.php\/event-manager\/events-entities\/3\/entities?page=1"
            }
        },
        "_embedded": {
            "events_entities": [
                {
                    "EventId": "3",
                    "EntityId": "2",
                    "Id": "2",
                    "CreationDate": "2020-04-08 18:04:15",
                    "Status": "1",
                    "Timestamp": "2020-04-08 18:04:15",
                    "Name": "en2",
                    "EntityTypeId": [
                        "1"
                    ],
                    "_links": {
                        "self": {
                            "href": "/index.php\/event-manager\/events-entities\/3\/entities\/2"
                        }
                    }
                }
            ]
        },
        "page_count": 1,
        "page_size": 1000,
        "total_items": 1,
        "page": 1
    }
:::

Linked Items {#event-linked-entities}
------------

Based on the admin configuration, you can link products, IRIX reseller
acount and event payment gateway account to a specific event

This service configuration allows dynamic behavior based on the event.
For example, if it\'s an IRIX reseller account, include it automatically
in the search and booking process to apply correct pricing and
availability. If it\'s a payment gateway account, use it during the
checkout step to initialize the proper merchant setup in the payment
gateway. This ensures that each event uses the right backend service
configuration without hardcoding it into the flow.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/events-services/:eventId]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description   Type     Parameter            Value
  ------------- -------- -------------------- -------
  Event id      string   {identifier or id}   
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Linked Products Response Example
:::

    {
        "_links": {
            "self": {
                "href": "/index.php\/events-services\/3"
            }
        },
        "_embedded": {
            "events_services": [
                {
                    "Id": "91",
                    "EventId": "3",
                    "Name": "NewAccount",
                    "Service": "micro-ice-saferpay.rest.accounts",
                    "ServiceId": "3",

                    "ServiceEndpoint": "\/saferpay\/accounts",

                    "_links": {
                        "self": {
                            "href": "/index.php\/events-services\/3\/services\/91"
                        }

                },
