::: {#entity-module .section .content-section}
Entity Module {#entity-module-title}
=============

The Entity module works in the same way as the Event module. The
difference is that the Entity module is designed to store information
about entities (people, companies, locations, etc.) rather than events.

The admin area allows you to define entity types (unlimited), each type
can have a set of fields that can be created and managed from the admin
area. Those fields will allow you to create entities on which you can
store information in the database in a structured manner.

The data stored will be available via REST API and can be filtered,
sorted and used in any way you need.

Entity types
------------

If you have added multiple types and you want to obtain them
dynamically, you can use the below request.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/entity-manager/entity-types]{.url}
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Entity Types Response Example
:::

    {
      "_links": {3 items},
      "_embedded": {1 item},
      "page_count": 1,
      "page_size": 1000,
      "total_items": 5,
      "page": 1
    }
:::

Entity list
-----------

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/entity-manager/entities]{.url}
:::

The results can be filtered by any of the fields received in the
response. For example, having the types, you can directly filter the
results, based on the type:
/entity-manager/entities?limit=10&page=1&filter\[0\]\[name\]=Type&filter\[0\]\[term\]=
{name received in the entity types list}

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Entity List Response Example
:::

    {
      "_links": {3 items},
      "_embedded": {1 item},
      "page_count": 1,
      "page_size": 1000,
      "total_items": 15,
      "page": 1
    }
:::

Entity list with Filter {#entity-list-filter}
-----------------------

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/entity-manager/entities?limit=10&page=1&filter\[0\]\[name\]=Type&filter\[0\]\[term\]={name
from response}]{.url}
:::

The lists requests will always give you minimum information and it is
always paginated.

The results can be filtered by one custom field at a time. If you filter
by data from a second level (types -- the custom fields), you need to
add also: filter\[1\]\[name\]=Types.Field&filter\[1\]\[term\]={field
name} &filter\[2\]\[name\]=Types.FieldValue& filter\[2\]\[term\]={value}

Entity details
--------------

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/entity-manager/entities/:Id]{.url}
:::

or

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [entity-manager/entities/:identifier]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                             Type     Parameter            Value
  --------------------------------------- -------- -------------------- -------
  id or identifier received in response   string   {identifier or id}   
:::

Either one of the above requests will return the entity details added in
the admin area.

Linked Events {#entity-linked-events}
-------------

### Events linked to the Entity

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/event-manager/events-entities/:entityId/events]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                      Type     Parameter            Value
  -------------------------------- -------- -------------------- -------
  Entity id received in response   string   {identifier or id}   
:::
:::

::: {#orders-api .section .content-section}
Orders API {#orders-api-title}
==========

### General information {#orders-general}

An order is an independent entity in the platform which you can create
and use at any point within the user\'s journey on the website.

The basic function of an order is to store the services that you want to
book, to store the customer information and to facilitate the booking
flow.

### Main Steps Overview

The main actions (and the most common used ones) are:

1.  **Create an order** - At this step you can either make the request
    to create a simple order or add the services and customer data as
    well. This is the common way to work and it\'s the most economic one
    as it allows you to mix 4 requests (or more) in a single one.
    ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [POST]{.method .post} [/orders]{.url}
    :::
2.  **Get available payment methods** - This step tells you what are the
    available payment methods (see more details).
    ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [GET]{.method .get} [/v2/orders/:{orderId}]{.url}
    :::
3.  **Set payment methods** - Configure the payment method for the
    order.
    ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [PATCH]{.method .patch} [/v2/orders/:{orderId}]{.url}
    :::
4.  **Pay and Reserve services** - Complete the payment and reservation
    process.
    ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [POST]{.method .post} [:{paymentGateway}/initialize]{.url}
    :::

    ::: {.endpoint-inline}
    [GET]{.method .get} [/v2/orders/:{orderId}?method=book]{.url}
    :::

::: {.step-subsection}
::: {.section-breadcrumb}
Decide payment flow
:::

In the booking process, you need to decide when the user should pay,
based also on the type of the offer or if the payment is required before
making the reservation.

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Important Notes

Make sure credit in IRIX is enabled & valid. Non refundable offers
cannot be booked without credit enabled in IRIX and without having the
payment on the order registered before trying to reserve the order
services.
:::
:::

The payment process can be either implemented by you and you need to
develop the communication with the payment provider, or you can use our
payment proxy with the payment gateways integrated in TRIP.

The redirect or the process of collecting the card data must be handled
from the FrontEnd implementation.

Based on the communication type with the PG, a return page might be
necessary. On that page you need to interpret the response from the
payment gateway and take the necessary actions.

**GET to/orders/{orderID}?method=getPaymentMethods** - This method needs
to be added in order to see paymentBefore information. At this point,
TRIP makes a request to the booking engine to check availability.

Based on the commitment modes available in the booking engine & the type
of offer (refundable/non-refundable), you receive the available methods
in this request: CREDIT (payment online), CASH, and BANK (pay directly
to the agency/offline). Credit might not be available when no credit is
available or credit is expired in the reseller configuration (IRIX).

::: {.section-breadcrumb}
Check payment before status
:::

-   **service\[n\].paymentBefore=0** - Offer can be reserved and payment
    can be made after the confirmation that the reservation was
    successful.
-   **service\[n\].paymentBefore=1** - Offer can be booked only after
    the order is marked as paid.
:::

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Attention

If multiple services are available in the order (such as flight and
hotel), check the paymentBefore flag from both services.
:::
:::

::: {.info-box .success}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Recommendation

If one of them has paymentBefore=1, initialize the payment before making
the booking. Of course, you can book them one by one if necessary; you
can make the reservation for the service with paymentBefore=0, then make
the payment, mark the order as paid, and then make the booking for the
service with paymentBefore=1.
:::
:::

Create the order {#orders-create}
----------------

An empty order can be created with a POST request.

Nonetheless, you can add all the data on the order while creating it,
just by adding the owner information, service and passengers and general
order information in the body of the POST request. This way the order
will be created and all the data will be added on the order.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/v2/orders]{.url}
:::

**Note:** When order is created and services are added, the order status
is 0. While in this status, other services can be added. Once the
method=book request is done, the order status will navigate into status
1 or 2.

### Order Data Structure Overview

The order main structure is always the same, the sub-items might vary,
depending on what the customer chooses. The main structure consists of
four key subsections:

-   **Order Generic Data** - Basic order information and metadata
-   **Owner Information** - Customer details and invoicing data
    (mandatory for booking)
-   **Services** - Travel services and related details (mandatory for
    booking)
-   **Order Details** - Additional order-specific information

### Order Generic Data

This subsection contains basic order information that applies to the
entire order regardless of the services included.

::: {.parameters-table}
  Description      Type     Parameter          Required      Notes
  ---------------- -------- ------------------ ------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Language         string   language           Optional      ISO language code (e.g., \'en\', \'es\', \'fr\'). This determines subsequent actions, such as sending a translated email notification.
  Application ID   string   applicationId      Conditional   Added in payload whenever discount is added on the order
  Discount Codes   array    discount\[code\]   Optional      
:::

### Owner Information

The owner information subsection contains all customer details required
for booking and invoicing. This section is mandatory for completing any
booking.

Depending on the fields added, the order can be registered as a company
order or a personal order.

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### TINA-TRIP Integration

If TINA-TRIP connection is enabled, TRIP will automatically add the
information as a backoffice remark. This information can be used in TINA
for various purposes including customer identification and compliance
tracking.
:::
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Owner Main Information (same for company and personal)

  Description       Type     Parameter              Required   Example
  ----------------- -------- ---------------------- ---------- ---------------------------
  Title             string   owner\[title\]         Yes        Mr, Mrs, Ms
  First Name        string   owner\[firstname\]     Yes        John
  Last Name         string   owner\[lastname\]      Yes        Doe
  Email             string   owner\[email\]         Yes        booker\@company.com
  Phone             string   owner\[phone\]         Yes        322332
  Phone Prefix      string   owner\[phonePrefix\]   Yes        +40
  Street Address    string   owner\[street\]        Yes        Calea Șerban Vodă
  House Number      string   owner\[houseNr\]       Yes        216
  City              string   owner\[city\]          Yes        Bucharest
  City Name         string   owner\[cityName\]      Optional   Bucharest
  Province/State    string   owner\[province\]      Optional   32
  ZIP/Postal Code   string   owner\[zipcode\]       Yes        040215
  Country           string   owner\[country\]       Yes        RO (ISO country code)
  Invoicing Type    int      owner\[type\]          Yes        1 = Personal, 0 = Company
:::

#### Owner personal {#owner-invoicing-data}

::: {.parameters-table}
  Description                    Type     Parameter      Required   Example
  ------------------------------ -------- -------------- ---------- -------------
  Personal Identification Code   string   owner\[PIC\]   Optional   pic38348734
:::

#### Owner company {#owner-invoicing-data}

::: {.parameters-table}
  Description             Type     Parameter                                 Required   Example
  ----------------------- -------- ----------------------------------------- ---------- -----------------------------
  Company name            string   owner\[company\]\[CompanyName\]           Optional   Company LTD
  Trade Registry Number   string   owner\[company\]\[TradeRegistryNumber\]   Optional   344345334
  Vat Number              string   owner\[company\]\[VatNumber\]             Optional   232232
  Bank name               string   owner\[company\]\[Bank\]                  Optional   Bank name
  Bank account number     string   owner\[company\]\[BankAccount\]           Optional   RO2632873RZBR32983498899834
:::

### Order Details

Extra details can be added on the order. This method allows you to
attach custom general-purpose data directly to the order. It is meant
for internal or integration-specific use, not for supplier
communication.

::: {.parameters-table}
  Description        Type     Parameter                    Required   Example
  ------------------ -------- ---------------------------- ---------- -------------------------------
  Special Requests   string   details\[specialRequests\]   Optional   Customer special requirements
:::

### Services {#services-information}

The services subsection contains all travel-related services that will
be included in the order. Each service type has its own specific
parameters and requirements.

#### Service Types

TRIP supports multiple service types that can be combined in a single
order:

-   **Flight Services** - `services[flight][0]`
-   **Hotel Services** - `services[hotel][0]`
-   **Activity Services** - `services[activity][0]`
-   **AIDA packages** - `services[package][0]`
-   **Product Services** - `services[product][0]`

#### Common Service Parameters

All services share certain common parameters regardless of their type:

::: {.parameters-table}
  Description          Type     Parameter Pattern                              Required   Notes
  -------------------- -------- ---------------------------------------------- ---------- -------------------------------
  Service Amount       float    services\[{type}\]\[0\]\[amount\]              Yes        Total cost of the service
  Currency             string   services\[{type}\]\[0\]\[currency\]            Yes        ISO currency code
  Account ID           string   services\[{type}\]\[0\]\[accountId\]           Optional   Reseller account identifier
  Result Code          string   services\[{type}\]\[0\]\[resultCode\]          Optional   Search result reference
  Backoffice Remarks   array    services\[{type}\]\[0\]\[BackOfficeRemarks\]   Optional   Internal notes and references
:::

#### Passenger Data/Travelers {#passenger-data}

This section covers all traveler-related data requirements for booking
services. The information required is based on the service validation
response. Select your service type below to see specific requirements,
or explore all data categories.

::: {.traveler-tabs-container}
::: {.traveler-tabs-nav}
All Services

Flights

Hotels

Activities

Below is a comprehensive example showing all subsections

::: {.code-header}
Exampla POST data
:::

                            
    //General info
    language: en
    applicationId: myapp_v1.0
    discount[code][0]: 2237

    // Owner Information - Company
    owner[title]: Mr
    owner[firstname]: John
    owner[lastname]: Doe
    owner[phone]: 322332
    owner[email]: booker@company.com
    owner[type]: 0
    owner[PIC]: pic38348734
    owner[street]: Calea Șerban Vodă
    owner[houseNr]: 216
    owner[city]: Bucharest
    owner[province]: 32
    owner[zipcode]: 040215
    owner[country]: RO
    owner[company][CompanyName]: Company LTD
    owner[company][TradeRegistryNumber]: RO2836
    owner[company][VatNumber]: 278273
    owner[company][Bank]: Bank name
    owner[company][BankAccount]: RO283RZBR23783283

    // Order Details
    details[specialField]: Extra info


    // Service Example (Hotel)
    services[hotel][0][hotelId]: 22511
    services[hotel][0][amount]: 13985.63
    services[hotel][0][currency]: EUR
    services[hotel][0][checkin]: 2023-10-12
    services[hotel][0][checkout]: 2023-10-24
    services[hotel][0][adultsNr]: 3
    services[hotel][0][childrenNr]: 2

    services[hotel][0][BackOfficeRemarks][0][Code]: termAccepted

    services[hotel][0][room][0][packagecode]: 0
    services[hotel][0][room][0][code]: 0

Get available payment methods {#orders-get-payment-methods}
-----------------------------

This step retrieves the available payment methods for the order. This
request tells you what payment methods are available based on the
services in the order and the booking engine configuration.

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Important

At this point, TRIP makes a request to the booking engine to check
availability and determine payment requirements.
:::
:::

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/v2/orders/{orderId}?method=getPaymentMethods]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                               Type     Parameter   Required   Notes
  ----------------------------------------- -------- ----------- ---------- -------------------------------
  The ID that identifies an order           int      {orderId}   Yes        
  Method parameter to get payment methods   string   method      Yes        Must be \"getPaymentMethods\"
:::

### Response Details

Based on the commitment modes available in the booking engine & the type
of offer (refundable/non-refundable), you receive the available methods
in this request:

-   **CREDIT** - Payment online through payment gateway
-   **CASH** - Offline - outside platform payment - Order payment status
    remains 0
-   **BANK** - Offline - outside platform payment - Order payment status
    remains 0

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Credit Availability

Credit might not be available when no credit is available or credit is
expired in the reseller configuration (IRIX).
:::
:::

### PaymentBefore Flag

The response will include the `paymentBefore` flag for each service,
which determines the payment flow:

-   **service\[n\].paymentBefore=0** - Offer can be booked and payment
    can be made after confirmation
-   **service\[n\].paymentBefore=1** - Offer can be booked only after
    the order is marked as paid

Set payment methods {#orders-set-payment-methods}
-------------------

After determining the available payment methods, you need to set the
chosen payment method for the order. This step configures how the
customer will pay for their booking.

::: {.endpoint}
[PATCH]{.method .patch} [/v2/orders/{orderId}]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Querry params

  Description                       Type   Parameter   Required   Notes
  --------------------------------- ------ ----------- ---------- -------------------------------------
  The ID that identifies an order   int    {orderId}   Yes        Order must exist and be in status 0
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Data

  Description           Type     Parameter           Required   Notes
  --------------------- -------- ------------------- ---------- -----------------------
  Payment method type   string   payment\[method\]   Yes        credit, cash, or bank
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Set Payment Method Example
:::

    {
      payment:{ 
      method: "credit"
      }
    }
:::

### Payment Method Options

-   **CREDIT** - Online payment through integrated payment gateways
-   **CASH** - Cash payment at agency or on delivery
-   **BANK** - Bank transfer or offline payment to agency

Reserve services {#orders-reserve-services-api}
----------------

This is the final step where you actually reserve/book the services in
the order. The booking behavior depends on the payment requirements of
each service.

::: {.method=book}
### Reserve/Book all services {#orders-book-all-services}

The request will initiate the book process within the systems. If there
are multiple services on the order, TRIP will try to book them all. If
the services are non-refundable (the cancellation policy started), the
book process won\`t start and the request will have no effect.

Unless the order is paid, TRIP will initiate book request only for the
refundable offers.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/v2/orders/:orderId?method=book]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                        Type   Member     Value
  ---------------------------------- ------ ---------- -------
  The id that identifies an order.   int    :orderId   
:::

::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
#####  Booking Rules Summary -- What You Need to Know

Before implementing the booking flow, make sure you understand these key
concepts and exceptions:

###### Payment Requirements {#payment-requirements style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

-   **paymentBefore=0:** Offer can be reserved first, payment can be
    made after confirmation.
-   **paymentBefore=1:** Offer can only be booked after the order is
    marked as paid. See [Get Payment Methods](#orders-payment-methods)
    section.
-   If multiple services exist on the order, check the `paymentBefore`
    flag for each service.

###### Refundable vs Non-Refundable Offers {#refundable-vs-non-refundable-offers style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

-   **Non-refundable offers:** Cannot be booked without payment. The
    book process won\'t start if the cancellation policy has already
    started.
-   **Refundable offers:** Can be booked before payment is completed.
-   **Hotels & Activities:** Check the cancellation policy in the offer
    response to identify if the offer is refundable or non-refundable.
-   **Flights:** Check the `IsAutoTicketable` flag -- if `true`, the
    offer requires payment before booking (auto-ticketable offers).

###### Supplier-Specific Exceptions {#supplier-specific-exceptions style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

-   **Travelfusion (Auto-Ticketable):** Flights from Travelfusion are
    one-step book & issue offers. Tickets are issued automatically upon
    booking. These offers require payment before booking and have
    `IsAutoTicketable=true`. Additionally, some airlines may require
    user verification redirects. See [Travelfusion Offers -- Book
    Confirmation Step](#orders-book-all-services).
-   **Credit Card on Book:** Some hotel suppliers require credit card
    data to be sent during the booking process. See [Send Credit Card
    Data](#orders-book-hotel-cc) section.

###### Order Status & Automatic Cancellation {#order-status-automatic-cancellation style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

-   After booking, always check both order status and individual service
    status (`Services[n].Status`).
-   If one service fails during booking, TRIP may automatically cancel
    other successful refundable reservations (configurable behavior).
    See [Automatic Order Cancel](#orders-book-all-services) section.

###### Further Reading {#further-reading style="margin-top: 1rem; color: #60a5fa;"}

-   [Get Payment Methods](#orders-payment-methods) -- Check payment
    requirements and available methods
-   [Order Status After Booking](#orders-book-all-services) --
    Understand status combinations
-   [Travelfusion Offers -- Book Confirmation
    Step](#orders-book-all-services) -- Handle user verification flows
-   [Automatic Order Cancel](#orders-book-all-services) -- Understand
    cancellation rules
:::
:::

### Booking Rules and Requirements

You can reserve a service only if:

-   The order is still available for booking (Status = 0)
-   The service is still available for reservation (Status = 0)
-   The order is complete (has owner and payment status if required)
-   If payment wasn\'t made, the service must be available for
    reservation before payment

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Payment Before Booking

If you choose to reserve all services at once but payment was not made,
only services with paymentBefore=0 will be reserved. Services requiring
payment first (paymentBefore=1) can only be reserved after payment is
completed.
:::
:::

### Booking Request in Progress

A temporary field on order detail - `bookInProgress` - with the value
`1` is now introduced to help prevent duplicate booking actions for the
same order.

This mechanism can ensure that only one booking request is processed at
a time for a given order, if it\'s properly integrated in your project.

::: {.step-subsection}
[How It Works]{.section-breadcrumb}

When a booking request is initiated for an order:

-   The system adds the key `bookInProgress` with the value `1` to the
    order details.
-   While this flag is active, any additional booking requests for the
    same order (such as retries or repeated user actions) will not
    trigger new booking operations.
-   Any subsequent requests will stay in a pending state until the
    initial booking request completes.

Once the first booking request is finalized successfully:

-   All pending requests for the same order will receive a successful
    response, reflecting the completed booking.
:::

::: {.step-subsection}
[Error Handling]{.section-breadcrumb}

If the initial booking request fails or is not finalized correctly:

-   All pending booking requests for the same order will return an HTTP
    error status, indicating the failure reason.
-   This includes cases such as system errors, timeouts, or booking
    validation issues.
-   The front end (FE) can then handle the error gracefully -- for
    example, by displaying an appropriate message or retry option.
:::

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Important Implementation Note: Verifying Booking Completion

To reliably determine that a reservation has been successfully
completed, the implementation must not rely solely on the booking
request response.

It is essential to validate the final state of the order by checking:

1.  **Order status** -- the overall status of the order.
2.  **Reservation status at the service level** -- to confirm that the
    specific service within the order was booked successfully.

Only when both statuses indicate a successful completion (`status = 1`)
should the booking be considered finalized.

This validation step ensures data accuracy and prevents false positives
caused by delayed or incomplete booking processes.
:::
:::

### Order Status & Payment Status Combinations

Understanding the relationship between order status and payment status
is crucial for proper booking flow management. Here are the key
combinations and their meanings:

::: {.step-subsection}
### Order Status After Booking

-   **Status = 1** - Order completed successfully, all services reserved
-   **Status = 2** - Order failed or cancelled
-   **Status = 0** - Order still in progress, some services may be
    booked while others are pending, check individual service statuses

::: {.info-box .success}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Important Note

Order status and individual service status might be different. Always
check the status of each service (Services\[0\].Status) to understand
the complete booking state.
:::
:::

::: {.section-breadcrumb}
Status Combination Examples
:::

-   **Order status 2 & Payment status 1** → Payment was successful
    however the reservation fails (at this point you can even trigger
    the payment refund action if you want to refund automatically the
    amount back to the client)
-   **Order status 1 & Payment status 1** → Payment and reservation were
    successful and client will receive automatically the travel vouchers
    via e-mail
-   **Order status 1 & Payment status 2** → Reservation successful, but
    payment failed - Customer must pay until order payment deadline or
    hotel autocancel date, otherwise booking might be cancelled by IRIX
    (depending on IRIX setup)
-   **Order status 0 & Payment status 1** → Method book request must be
    done
-   **Order status 0 & Payment status 2** → Payment failed - Customer
    should start over the process - search book/pay
-   **Order status 1 & Payment status 0 but payment method is cash or
    bank** → Reservation done but payment must be performed until
    payment deadline or hotel autocancel date.

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Status Reference

**Order Status:** 0 = Pending, 1 = Confirmed, 2 = Failed\
**Payment Status:** 0 = Pending, 1 = Successful, 2 = Failed
:::
:::
:::

### Order Status Messages

Besides the order status, an extra information is available per service
and order - **StatusMessage**.

::: {.step-subsection}
::: {.section-breadcrumb}
Possible Status Messages
:::

-   **Empty** -- Order created, booking was not attempted
-   **OK** -- Services booked
-   **NOT OK** -- Booking request failed
-   **Cancelled by external supplier** - when booking is cancelled in
    IRIX for from IRIX interface
-   **Cancelled by \[username\]** -- cancelled from TRIP
-   **AM** -- Reservation amended in IRIX
    ::: {.info-box .warning}
    ::: {.info-box-content}
    ##### Attention!

    For the moment the reservation changes are not imported into TRIP.
    The only information available is the status of the reservation.
    :::
    :::
:::

### Travelfusion Offers -- Book Confirmation Step

Certain airlines integrated via TravelFusion require additional user
verification steps during booking. To support this flow, the front-end
must handle user redirections based on specific URLs returned in the
order response.

::: {.step-subsection}
::: {.section-breadcrumb}
Changes in Order Requests
:::

#### 1. Order Create Request (when service is added on the order)

When creating a new order with the flight service, in the request data
you must also add `services[flight][0][returnUrl]` in the request
parameters.

-   **returnUrl** represents the FE endpoint where the user will be
    redirected after successful verification

#### 2. Book Order Request -- Check Response

A new property **UserConfirmations** will be added under order →
Services:

-   **UserConfirmations** is an array of confirmation objects
-   Each object contains a **Url** field
-   The user must be redirected sequentially to each of these URLs until
    the Status changes to **CONFIRMED** or is not **REQUIRED** anymore
:::

::: {.step-subsection}
::: {.section-breadcrumb}
Example Implementation (Website)
:::

In a typical website flow, after creating the order:

1.  The order response includes the **UserConfirmations** array.
2.  The FE iterates through each confirmation **Url** and opens it
    (e.g., in a modal, new tab, or redirect).
3.  Once the user completes the required verification and the API
    reports **Status: CONFIRMED**, the FE redirects the user back to the
    provided **returnUrl** endpoint - typically the booking confirmation
    or summary page.
4.  Make sure to check also reservation status to ensure the service is
    also booked (**status 1**).
:::

### Automatic order cancel

When it comes to TRIP, the option to bundle services and book them
together it\'s an important functionality that facilitates the booking
process and post booking actions.

Cancel order is a function that can be triggered automatically by the
platform and through API. Canceling an order is a complex process as it
needs to handle multiple reservations.

::: {.step-subsection}
::: {.section-breadcrumb}
Automatic Cancellation Rules
:::

-   **Cancel order automatically when one of the reservations on the
    order fails.** The platform is fully configurable, and the default
    functionality is to cancel the reservations Ok & refundable that
    were registered on the order until the failed reservation process
    happened.

The platform can be configured to:

-   Not cancel non-refundable offers at all
-   Cancel all of them, no matter if they are refundable or not
-   Not cancel reservations at all and only notify the admin that order
    reservation failed for some of the services included on the order

Until now, the platform would cancel the reservations if all of them
were refundable. Now it cancels all the reservations refundable and the
non-refundable will remain booked, needing the attention of the agency.

-   **Cancel order through the API will cancel all reservation in the
    order, no matter if they are refundable or not**
:::

### Booking Strategies

You can combine different approaches:

-   **Book all services at once** - Send request without serviceIds
    parameter
-   **Book services individually** - Send multiple requests with
    specific serviceIds
-   **Mixed approach** - Book some services individually, then book
    remaining services together

### Reserve a single service

TRIP gives you full control over the booking process, allowing you to
submit individual requests for each service and confirm them based on
your own customized workflow.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/v2/orders/:orderId/services/:serviceId/book]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                        Type   Member       Value
  ---------------------------------- ------ ------------ -------
  The id that identifies an order.   int    :orderId     
  The id of service booked.          int    :serviceId   
:::

#### Send credit card data in the book process - Hotel service

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Applies Only to Selected Suppliers

This flow is applicable only to certain suppliers and is not a standard
process
:::
:::

On the hotel availability response if supplier payment is available you
will receive a SupplierPayment property with the all required fields in
the book request. Use the data to display the fields and collect the
data. You can collect data before or after you create the order, however
the data is required only when you send the method book request (so
after the order is created already).

Once the order is created on the hotel service a CommitmentMethod
property is available), which has the value supplier if the supplier
payment was selected

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/v2/orders/:orderId/book]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                        Type   Member     Value
  ---------------------------------- ------ ---------- -------
  The id that identifies an order.   int    :orderId   
:::

The form data is dynamic and it needs to be built based on the
validation response for the room. The fields received in the
SupplierPayment section will indicate which fields must be sent at book.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Hotel Service Credit Card Example
:::

    service[144][payment][cardHolderEmail]: demo@demo.com
    service[144][payment][cardHolderName]: John Doe
    service[144][payment][cardNumber]: 44443333222233311
    service[144][payment][cardType]: VI
    service[144][payment][cvc]: 123
    service[144][payment][firstName]: John
    service[144][payment][lastName]: Doe
    service[144][payment][title]: MS
    service[144][payment][cardExpiryDate]: 8/35
:::

Get orders {#orders-get}
----------

### Get a specific order {#orders-get-specific}

This request will return details about a specific request in a JSON
format. You can get only the order created by you if you use the same
Token as used in the Create order request. An order can be retreived
also by the user that made that order (while logged in).

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/v2/orders/:orderId]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                        Type   Parameter   Value
  ---------------------------------- ------ ----------- -------
  The id that identifies an order.   int    :orderId    
:::

### Get orders for a logged in user {#orders-get-user}

An order can be access in 2 scenarios:

-   Using the same token that was used during order creation.
-   **Requesting the orders while the user that created it is logged
    in:**\
    If you want the user/customer to have access the order, in his
    account, the user needs to be logged in when the order is created.
    This way, TRIP will automatically associate that order with the
    user, and when the user will be logged in, he will be able to access
    his orders. You will notice that when you will log in a user and
    make the orders request, you will receive the orders of that user.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/v2/orders?limit=10]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                Type     Parameter             Value
  -------------------------- -------- --------------------- -------
  Filter by                  string   filter\[1\]\[name\]   
  Id of the logged in user   string   filter\[1\]\[term\]   
:::

### Get all orders API {#orders-get-all}

This API endpoint allows you to retrieve all orders from the system.
Access is restricted based on authentication and user permissions.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/orders]{.url}
:::

### Get all orders Export csv {#orders-export-csv}

**Export orders**

API dedicated to exporting reports in a csv format. The API is
accessible only based on authentication and the user authenticated must
have rights over the orders. Usually, only admin users have this type of
access.

A new report can be generated by using:

**GET** on the endpoint `/orders` with `export=file-name` in query
params and other filters to generate report and then download using
download from `_links`

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/orders?export=file-name]{.url}
:::

The endpoint to check status of reports is:

**GET** `/export`

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/export]{.url}
:::

Once the report is generated, the response includes the download URL

Remove services from orders {#orders-remove-services}
---------------------------

As long as the order is in selecting service stage Status=0, you can
also remove services from order, with this delete request.

::: {.endpoint}
[DELETE]{.method .delete}
[/v2/orders/:orderId/services/:serviceId]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                         Type   Parameter   Value
  ----------------------------------- ------ ----------- -------
  The id that identifies an order.    int    :orderId    
  The id that identifies a service.   int    serviceId   
:::

Download financial documents {#orders-download-financial-documents}
----------------------------

The new API can be used to automate and improve the user experience when
booking a trip. More than that, you can achieve a touchless flow which
doesn\'t require any travel agent intervention.

Starting from the website, where the customer can book, pay, and
download the travel documents, you can include this option to download
the invoice as well. Of course, you need to make sure you automate the
TINA invoicing flow as well (for more details please contact our team).
Once the invoice is available in TINA, based on the API request which
uses only order ID, you can give your customers the option to download
the invoice as well. You can even display if it is paid or not, or you
can create a custom experience based on the due date and the amount
paid.

This endpoint returns both invoices and payment-related caching
documents based on TINA configuration.

### Get invoices and caching documents

This request returns both invoices and caching documents for a specific
order. Caching documents are usually payment-related documents issued
based on the TINA configuration.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/tina/invoice/:orderId/cachingDocuments]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description     Type   Parameter   Required
  --------------- ------ ----------- ----------
  TRIP order ID   int    :orderId    Yes
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Response Example
:::

::: {.code-content}
    {
      "invoices": [
        {
          "CashedTotal": "11.32",
          "Total": "228.19",
          "VAT": "5.68",
          "DueDate": "2023-10-29",
          "IssueTime": "2023-10-19 13:50:19",
          "InvoiceSeriesCode": "WIZINV",
          "Value": "222.51",
          "Currency": "EUR",
          "Comments": "",
          "Remarks": "idTripReservation=00a2d859-c068-56a0-ae77-796434326734",
          "Status": "ok",
          "Documents": [
            {
              "DocId": "2860000069",
              "DocType": "invoice",
              "DocDate": "2023-10-19",
              "IdPivot": "2860000058",
              "PivotCode": "invoice",
              "IdDocumentSeries": "83"
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "cachingDocuments": [
        {
          "DocType": "receipt",
          "DocDate": "2023-10-19",
          "DocNumber": "5",
          "Value": "11.320",
          "Currency": "EUR",
          "Documents": [
            {
              "DocId": "2860000070",
              "DocType": "cashing_receipt",
              "DocDate": "2023-10-19",
              "IdPivot": "2860000004",
              "PivotCode": "cashing",
              "IdDocumentSeries": "81"

        }
      }

### Download documents

To download the actual documents, use the existing invoice endpoint with
the document IDs. This endpoint supports both invoice and caching
document IDs.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/tina/invoice/:orderId?documents=:documentIds]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                      Type     Parameter   Required
  -------------------------------- -------- ----------- ----------
  TRIP order ID                    int      :orderId    Yes
  Document IDs (comma-separated)   string   documents   Yes
:::

::: {.info-box}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### Download Behavior

-   **Multiple documents:** Returns a ZIP archive containing all
    requested documents
-   **Single document:** Returns the PDF file directly
-   **Example URLs:**
    -   Multiple: `/tina/invoice/2791?documents=2860000070,2850000082`
    -   Single: `/tina/invoice/2791?documents=2850000081`
:::
:::

Discount codes {#orders-discount-codes}
==============

For discount, all the services along with the discount must be added at
the same time on the order (see how to create order). When you create
the order, make sure you add the services and owner information. Besides
that, add in the payload the discount code/codes inputed by the client,
using the following fields:

-   applicationId:
-   discount\[code\]\[0\]:
-   discount\[code\]\[1\]:

Make sure you initiate payment only after the discount is applied on the
order

### Check details & Validate Code

If you want to check if the code is within the validity period, you can
use the below GET request. This request will retrieve some details about
the code and some details based on which you can validate if the voucher
code is valid.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/discount-codes/check/:code]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description     Type   Member   Value
  --------------- ------ -------- -------
  Discount code   int    :code    
:::

### Check estimated value

If you want to obtain the final value of the order, after discount is
applied and you want to make sure it can be applied with success on the
order, you can make a POST request to the same endpoint. If the voucher
code cannot be applied due to various reasons, a generic error will be
retrieved.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/discount-codes/check/:code]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description      Type     Parameter                          Value
  ---------------- -------- ---------------------------------- -------
  The code/s       string   discount\[code\]\[0\]              
  applicationId    string   applicationId                      
  Service amount   int      services\[hotel\]\[0\]\[amount\]   
:::

::: {#payment-api .section .content-section}
Payment API {#payment-api-title}
===========

General info {#payment-general}
------------

In TRIP, we offer a payment proxy that allows you to connect your
payment gateway account from a list of supported payment gateways.

To start the payment process, you need to use the following APIs:

-   Get payment methods: Retrieve available payment methods.
-   Set payment methods: Assign a payment method to an order.
-   Get payment gateways: Retrieve available payment gateways for
    flexibility and future expansion.
-   Get payment accounts: Based on the payment gateway selected by the
    customer, retrieve associated payment accounts.
-   Initialize payment: Begin the payment process for the order.

If the payment gateway implies a redirect, make sure to keep the token
used at order create so post payment request on order can be performed.
In the ReturnUrl you can add information like Token and order ID to make
sure that the information is available when user is redirected back from
the payment gateway\'s page. Storing information in the browser storage
might be a reliable option in all situations.

Get payment methods {#payment-get-methods}
-------------------

To book the services included in an order, besides the services and the
owner, it is necessary to add the payment method as well.

At this step, the services are validated once again and the available
payment methods are sent. This new method needs to be added in order to
see paymentBefore information.

Based on the commitment modes available in the booking engine & the type
of offer (refundable/non refundable) in the Get Payment methods request
you receive the methods available: CREDIT (payment online), CASH and
BANK (pay directly to the agency/offline). Credit might not be available
when no credit or credit is expired on the reseller configuration
(IRIX).

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/orders/:orderId?method=getPaymentMethods]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                        Type   Parameter   Value
  ---------------------------------- ------ ----------- -------
  The id that identifies an order.   int    :orderId    
:::

The payment methods can be find in the PaymentMethods array.

Set payment methods {#payment-set-methods}
-------------------

Once the payment method is decided, based on what client has selected or
by choosing automatically in the frontend flow, you need to make an API
request to \"Set the payment method\". This means to add on the order
the selected method.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Payment Method Example
:::

    {
      "payment": {"method":"credit"}
    }
:::

::: {.endpoint}
[PATCH]{.method .patch} [/orders/:orderId]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                    Type     Member              Value
  ------------------------------ -------- ------------------- -------
  The payment method selected.   string   payment\[method\]   
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### URL Parameters

  Description                        Type   Parameter   Value
  ---------------------------------- ------ ----------- -------
  The id that identifies an order.   int    :orderId    
:::

Once you have set the payment method, you can either proceed with
performing the book request or, if the payment method is credit (online)
and you want to collect the money, you can proceed to a payment gateway
using TRIP\'s payment proxy.

Online payment - Payment proxy {#payment-online-proxy}
------------------------------

TRIP\'s Payment Proxy provides a unified interface for integrating with
multiple payment gateways. All payment operations follow a common API
structure with gateway-specific variations handled automatically.

### Common Payment Endpoints {#common-endpoints}

The following endpoints are available for all payment gateways. Replace
`{payment gateway}` with the gateway code (e.g., nuvei, paytrail,
hyperpay, mobilpay, stripe, knpay, svea, viva, jcc, ngenius).

#### 1. Initialize Payment

Starts the payment process for an order. This is the first step in the
payment flow.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/payment-proxy/{payment
gateway}/initialize]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                                                                         Type     Member               Required
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------- -------------------- ----------
  The order you want to pay                                                                           string   OrderId              Yes
  The HTML page URL where the payment gateway should return the user after the payment is processed   string   ReturnUrl            Yes
  Payment gateway code (required when using multiple payment accounts)                                string   paymentGatewayCode   Optional
  Specific payment account ID (for projects using multiple payment accounts)                          string   AccountId            Optional
:::

::: {.response-guide-section}
#####  Response Structure

All payment gateways return a standardized response structure:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Initialize Response Format
:::

    {
        "Id": "746",
        "Action": "\/charge",
        "Method": "POST",
        "Data": {
            "merchantId": "859078680624153089",
            "merchantSiteId": "219188",
            "sessionToken": "eeac3095a0bb46b396b12b9d866c93380121",
            "env": "test",
            "requestId": "8366nuvei1779114773"
        },
        "_links": {
            "self": {
                "href": "/index.php\/payment-proxy\/nuvei\/initialize"
            }
        }
    }
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
  Field      Purpose
  ---------- --------------------------------------------------------------------
  `Action`   The URL to redirect or submit to
  `Method`   How to send the user: `GET` = redirect, `POST` = form submit
  `Data`     Parameters to include (form fields for POST, query params for GET)
  `Params`   Alternative to Data (same purpose - check both fields)
:::
:::

::: {.response-guide-section .decision-logic}
#####  Frontend Decision Logic {#decision-logic}

Use this decision tree to handle the response correctly:

::: {.decision-tree}
::: {.decision-node .root}
::: {.node-content}
Check `Method` value
:::

::: {.decision-branches}
::: {.decision-branch .get-branch}
::: {.branch-label .get}
GET
:::

::: {.sub-decisions}
::: {.sub-decision}
::: {.condition}
Has `Data.scriptSrc`?
:::

::: {.action .widget}
Load Widget (HyperPay)
:::
:::

::: {.sub-decision}
::: {.condition}
Has `Data` or `Params` with values?
:::

::: {.action .redirect-params}
Redirect with Query Params
:::
:::

::: {.sub-decision}
::: {.condition}
Empty `Data`/`Params`?
:::

::: {.action .redirect-simple}
Simple Redirect to Action
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.decision-branch .post-branch}
::: {.branch-label .post}
POST
:::

::: {.sub-decisions}
::: {.sub-decision}
::: {.action .form-submit}
Create form with `Data` as hidden fields → Submit form
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.response-guide-section .gateway-examples}
#####  Examples by Gateway {#gateway-examples}

Quick reference for how each gateway behaves:

::: {.parameters-table .gateway-table}
  Gateway           Method                        Data/Params Content                  Frontend Action
  ----------------- ----------------------------- ------------------------------------ -----------------------------------------------
  **Stripe**        [GET]{.method-badge .get}     `Empty {}`                           Direct redirect to Action URL
  **Viva**          [GET]{.method-badge .get}     `Empty {}`                           Direct redirect to Action URL
  **Saferpay**      [GET]{.method-badge .get}     `{ Token, MerchantId }`              Redirect to `Action?Token=abc&MerchantId=123`
  **Datatrans**     [POST]{.method-badge .post}   `{ merchantId, amount, currency }`   Create form with hidden fields, submit
  **CreditGuard**   [POST]{.method-badge .post}   `{ terminal, txId }`                 Create form with hidden fields, submit
  **HyperPay**      [GET]{.method-badge .get}     `{ scriptSrc, brands }`              Load JS widget on page
:::
:::

::: {.response-guide-section .return-url}
#####  Return URL Handling

::: {.info-callout}
::: {.callout-icon}
:::

::: {.callout-content}
On the `ReturnUrl`, TRIP will append the Order ID and Request ID to the
URL:

`?orderId=1232&requestId=13123123`{.block-code}
:::
:::

::: {.steps-container}
::: {.step}
::: {.step-number}
1
:::

::: {.step-content}
**Verify Payment Status**

On the return page, make a GET request to `/orders/:OrderId` to verify
payment status.
:::
:::

::: {.step}
::: {.step-number}
2
:::

::: {.step-content}
**Check Status Code**

If `payment status = 1`, payment was successful. Any other status means
payment failed.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.warning-callout}
::: {.callout-icon}
:::

::: {.callout-content}
**Important:** Pass the token used when creating the order. Without it,
you cannot access the order on the return page.
:::
:::

::: {.success-callout}
::: {.callout-icon}
:::

::: {.callout-content}
TRIP automatically updates the order status, triggers the issue process,
and sends vouchers via email, if the book request on order was done
prior to payment.
:::
:::
:::

#### 2. Capture Payment (Optional) {#capture-payment}

If the payment gateway supports two-step payment (Authorize and
Capture), use this endpoint to capture an authorized payment.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/payment-proxy/{payment gateway}/capture]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                                         Type     Member               Required
  ------------------------------------------------------------------- -------- -------------------- ----------
  The order you want to capture payment for                           string   OrderId              Yes
  The request ID from order details, payment section as ExternalRef   string   RequestId            Yes
  Payment gateway code                                                string   paymentGatewayCode   Optional
:::

*Note: Not supported by all payment gateways.*

#### 3. Cancel Transaction (Optional) {#cancel-payment}

If the payment gateway supports two-step payment with a Cancel option,
you can cancel an authorized payment before capture.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/payment-proxy/{payment gateway}/cancel]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                                         Type     Member               Required
  ------------------------------------------------------------------- -------- -------------------- ----------
  The order you want to cancel payment for                            string   OrderId              Yes
  The request ID from order details, payment section as ExternalRef   string   RequestId            Yes
  Payment gateway code                                                string   paymentGatewayCode   Optional
:::

*Note: Not supported by all payment gateways. You can only cancel an
authorized payment, not a captured one.*

#### 4. Refund Payment (Optional) {#refund-payment}

If the payment gateway supports refunds, use this endpoint to refund a
payment. Use this when a reservation fails after payment.

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/payment-proxy/{payment gateway}/refund]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                                         Type     Member      Required
  ------------------------------------------------------------------- -------- ----------- ----------
  The order you want to refund                                        string   OrderId     Yes
  The request ID from order details, payment section as ExternalRef   string   RequestId   Yes
:::

*Note: Not supported by all payment gateways. You can only refund a
captured payment, not an authorized one.*

Payment Gateways
----------------

Each payment gateway in TRIP\'s payment proxy has specific
implementation requirements and flows. Below are the detailed
implementation guides for each supported payment gateway. Click on any
gateway to expand its documentation.

::: {.payment-gateway-section}
::: {.gateway-toggle onclick="toggleCollapsible('nuvei-content')"}
::: {.gateway-title}
[Nuvei Payment Gateway]{.gateway-name}
:::
:::

::: {#nuvei-content .gateway-content}
Nuvei payment gateway uses a dynamic form approach where you build the
payment form using their JavaScript SDK and submit card data through
their secure API.

#### Nuvei Initialize Response {#nuvei-initialize}

Use the [common Initialize endpoint](#initialize-payment) with
`/payment-proxy/nuvei/initialize`. Nuvei returns form data that you use
to build the payment form:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Response Example
:::

    {
        "Id": "746",
        "Action": "\/charge",
        "Method": "POST",
        "Data": {
            "merchantId": "859078680624153089",
            "merchantSiteId": "219188",
            "sessionToken": "eeac3095a0bb46b396b12b9d866c93380121",
            "env": "test",
            "requestId": "8366nuvei1779114773"
        },
        "_links": {
            "self": {
                "href": "/index.php\/payment-proxy\/nuvei\/initialize"
            }
        }
    }
:::

**Implementation:** Use response.Data key:values to instantiate nuvei
API aka the dynamic form in the page, as per the example attached in
\'nuveiForm.html\'

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Nuvei Form Implementation Example
:::

    <html>

    <head>

            <script src="https://cdn.safecharge.com/safecharge_resources/v1/websdk/safecharge.js"></script>

    </head>

    <body>

    <form action="/charge" method="post" id="payment-form">

            <div class="form-row">

                    <label for="card-field-placeholder">

                            Credit or debit card

                    </label>

                    <div id="card-field-placeholder" class="some initial css-classes">

                            <!-- SFC Card widget is inserted here. -->

                    </div>

                    <!-- Used to display form errors. -->

                    <div id="scard-errors" role="alert"></div>

            </div>

    </form>

    <button onclick="main();">Submit Payment</button>

    <script type="text/javascript">

            // set state field style/ check Nuvei Fields for details.

            var style = {

                    base: { // default idle state

                            fontSize: '16pt',

                            fontFamily: 'Roboto, sans-serif',

                            color: "#045d47",

                            fontSmoothing: 'antialiased',

                            '::placeholder': {

                                    color: '#ccb654'

                            }

                    },

                    invalid: { //when invalid input detected o the field

                            color: '#e5312b',

                            ':focus': {

                                    color: '#303238'

                            }

                    },

                    empty: { //empty field

                            color: '#BADA55',

                            '::placeholder': {

                                    color: '#cc3ac2'

                            }

                    },

                    valid: { //when the input is valid

                            color: '#48ef39'

                    }

            };


            // Instantiate Nuvei API

            var sfc = SafeCharge({

                    env: 'test', // the environment you are running on, 'prod' for production

                    merchantId: '859078680624153089', // your Merchant ID provided by Nuvei

                    merchantSiteId: '219188' // your Merchant site ID provided by Nuvei

            });

            //Instantiate Nuvei Fields

            var ScFields = sfc.fields({

                    fonts: [ { cssUrl: 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Roboto'} ]  // e.g.  https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Source+Code+Pro
            })

            // Instantiate Nuvei Fields

            //setting the styles when creating the Nuvei Fields

            var scard = ScFields.create('card', {

                    style: style

            });

            // attach the Nuvei fields to the html placeholder

            scard.attach(document.getElementById('card-field-placeholder'));

            function main() {

                    // call this from your main() in order for it to work with the html sample

                    sfc.createPayment({

                            "sessionToken": "973234d8-78cb-423a-bc60-28c09d40509a",

                            // "clientUniqueId": "12345", // optional

                            "cardHolderName": "john smith",

                            "paymentOption": scard,

                            // "billingAddress": {

                            //     "email": "john.smith@email.com",

                            //     "country": "US"

                            // }

                    }, function(res) {

                            console.log(res);

                    })

            }

    </script>

    </body>

    </html>
:::

**Next Step:** After the payment form submission, the authorization
request can be called in the callback function of the createPayment
method (in main function from the example) - which will trigger checking
the payment status and updating the order. From there, you can redirect
to a final page for checking order statuses etc.

**Documentation:** See dynamic form detailed info:
<https://docs.nuvei.com/documentation/payment-overview/intro/>

**Testing data:**
<https://docs.nuvei.com/documentation/payment-overview/intro/>

#### Nuvei Authorization

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/payment-proxy/nuvei/authorize/\[RequestId\]]{.url}
:::

#### Nuvei Cancel & Refund

Use the [common Cancel endpoint](#cancel-payment) and [common Refund
endpoint](#refund-payment) with `/payment-proxy/nuvei/cancel` and
`/payment-proxy/nuvei/refund`.

**Important:** Cancel payment has very specific rules. Check Nuvei
guidelines before deciding between Refund or Cancel actions.
:::

[Hyperpay Payment Gateway]{.gateway-name}

::: {#hyperpay-content .gateway-content}
Hyperpay payment gateway uses a script-based approach where a JavaScript
widget is automatically inserted into your page to handle the payment
form and card data collection.

#### Hyperpay Initialize Response {#hyperpay-initialize}

Use the [common Initialize endpoint](#initialize-payment) with
`/payment-proxy/hyperpay/initialize`. Hyperpay returns a script that you
insert into your page:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Response Example
:::

    {
      "Action": "url",
      "Method": "GET",
      "Data": {
        "scriptSrc": "url",
        "brands": "VISA MASTER AMEX",
        "integrity": "sha384-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
      }
    }
:::

::: {.info-box .warning}
::: {.info-box-content}
##### PCI DSS v4.0 -- Integrity Security Requirement

As of PCI DSS v4.0, the `Data.integrity` field is now returned in the
initialize response. This value must be included as the `integrity`
attribute on the Hyperpay script tag to ensure Subresource Integrity
(SRI) verification. Security Guide
:::
:::

**Implementation:** Add the following lines of HTML/JavaScript to your
page using the values from the response:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Hyperpay Form Implementation
:::

    <script src="{scriptSrc}" integrity="{integrity}" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
    <form action="{Action}" class="paymentWidgets" data-brands="{brands}"></form>
:::

#### Hyperpay Capture, Cancel & Refund

Use the [common Capture](#capture-payment), [Cancel](#cancel-payment),
and [Refund](#refund-payment) endpoints with
`/payment-proxy/hyperpay/capture`, `/payment-proxy/hyperpay/cancel`, and
`/payment-proxy/hyperpay/refund`.

**Important:** You can only cancel an authorized payment, and can only
refund a captured one.
:::

successful authorization unless automatic capture is enabled for your
account.

Payment gateway - accounts {#payment-gateway-accounts}
--------------------------

TRIP allows multiple payments accounts for a single payment gateway. The
payment account is the account in which the agency receives the money.
If the accounts are added in the TRIP\'s admin area, the accounts can be
accessible in the API, and they can be used in the initialize request.
This way, the front-end implementation can dictate the payment account
that needs to be used for the payment.

### Payment gateways

This request will retrieve the payment gateways available in your TRIP
configuration. The most important aspect of this request is that it
retrieves the payment gateway name, which is mandatory in the request of
the account and usually a project has only one payment gateway
connection.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/payment-proxy/payment-gateways]{.url}
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Payment Gateways Response Example
:::

    {
      "_links": {1 item},
      "_embedded": {1 item},
      "total_items": 7
    }
:::

### Payment gateway Accounts {#payment-gateway-accounts-1}

This is an optional request that needs to be used only in the case you
have a project that uses multiple payment gateway accounts (which are
configured in TRIP\'s admin area). This request will retrieve the
account ID that needs to be added din the payload of the payment
initialize request.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/payment-proxy/\[PG name\]/accounts]{.url}
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Payment Gateway Accounts Response Example
:::

    {
      "_embedded": {1 item}
    }
:::

### Using Multiple Accounts with Common Endpoints

When using multiple payment accounts, include the `AccountId` parameter
in your requests to the [common payment endpoints](#common-endpoints)
(Initialize, Capture, Cancel, Refund). Use the Account ID retrieved from
the GET accounts request above.

See the [common Initialize endpoint](#initialize-payment) for the full
parameter reference, which includes the optional `AccountId` and
`paymentGatewayCode` parameters.
:::

::: {#flight-issue-process-section .section .content-section}
Flight -- Issue process with card {#flight-issue-process}
---------------------------------

A new flow is available within the application: Pay/Send credit card
data to the supplier.

You can implement this flow by default to check, after the reservation
is confirmed. Nonetheless, this flow is needed only in case you are
using suppliers and supplier configuration that implies adding the card
data on the PNR.

This new flow allows you to send the customer\'s card data to the
supplier, so the full fare amount to reach the account of the supplier
directly (airline).

Full Fare means the amount of the flight offer without service
fee/mark-up or commission.

For flight service (GDS), the information about the payment
possibilities are available after the reservation is made. Order details
request will retrieve the Issue Methods available
(Services\[0\].IssueMethod):

-   creditCard
-   simple

When creditCard is the received as Issue method on the order, at service
level, another request is required to obtain the form to collect the
card data.

### Get issue method

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/orders/:orderId/services/:serviceId/getIssueMethods]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                        Type   Member       Value
  ---------------------------------- ------ ------------ -------
  The id that identifies an order.   int    :orderId     
  The id of service booked.          int    :serviceId   
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Get Issue Methods Response Example
:::

            {
                "Code": "CC",

### Issue ticket

The issue tickets request must be done using the as POST data the fields
received in the previous request (Get Issue methods)

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post}
[/orders/:orderId/services/:serviceId/issueTickets]{.url}
:::

The POST data can variate based on what the response to getIssueMethods
was.

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Issue Tickets POST Data Example
:::

    fields[creditCardNumber]: 4153013999700313
    fields[creditCardType]: VI
    fields[creditCardHolderName]: test
    fields[cardExpirationMonth]: 11
    fields[cardExpirationYear]: 2026
    fields[creditCardCvc]: 313
    issueMethodCode: CC
:::

If a flight ticket is issued, on the order details, at service level,
the IsTicketed field will have the value 1. Also, if the response to the
POST request to issue is \"Tickets issued, documents not available.\",
means that the tickets were in fact issued, however the travel documents
cannot be obtained, and a travel manager needs to intervene. This
situation is usually encountered when there is a mark-up/service fee
included in the flow and the amount of the order was not fully paid.
:::

::: {#general-apis .section .content-section}
General APIs {#general-apis-title}
============

Static Data {#static-data-title}
-----------

The static data APIs will provide information like list of countries,
cities, even hotel details. The data is imported from IRIX and it
includes the IDs or Codes that can be used in search or even book
(country code for passport/identification document).

### Countries {#static-countries}

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/static-data/countries]{.url}
:::

### Cities {#static-cities}

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/static-data/cities]{.url}
:::

### Nationalities {#static-nationalities}

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/static-data/nationalities]{.url}
:::

### Hotels {#static-hotels}

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/hotels]{.url}
:::

#### Autocomplete Feature

A new option is now available on the hotels static data API which can
enable an autocomplete filter option that skips the pagination
processing, thus retrieving results efficiently and quicker than the
standard filters.

You can enable this feature by adding the parameter `autocomplete=true`
to the hotels GET request.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/hotels?filter\[0\]\[name\]=Name&limit=10&filter\[0\]\[type\]=startsWith&filter\[0\]\[term\]=Marriot&autocomplete=true]{.url}
:::

### Areas (TRIP regions) {#static-areas}

Areas API was created to offer the possibility of having different types
of areas that contain multiple locations. TRIP is now configured to
defined Regions, which are country type areas, meaning countries can be
grouped under different regions.

#### Use cases examples:

Depending on the need, the Regions module can serve various purposes and
can be adapted based on needs.

##### Example 1:

Create SEO pages with destinations and use Regions to create generic
pages that describe a certain region, under which you can list countries
(and create pages for countries). This ca help create a comprehensive
and well structed sitemap which will help index your website and provide
structured content for the search engines.

##### Example 2:

Create widgets with entities or events which are happening or are
available in a certain region. Define regions, and then use them
whenever you create a new entity or event. Display a list of regions and
filter in your platform the events or entities based on the region
selected by the customer.

#### Get regions

This request will retrieve the list of regions defined in the admin
area.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/areas/country]{.url}
:::

#### Get countries in a region

This request will retrieve all the countries defined inside a region
(information which is configured from TRIP\`s admin area -- Regions
module). The countries will be retrieved with an Id which is the country
ID stored in the database, this way it can be linked or used for other
purposes as well.

**\*areaId is the ID received in the response of areas/country**

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/areas/country/:areaId/locations]{.url}
:::

### Standalone POIs API:

In case you want to use the points of interest by themselves, TRIP
provides a standalone API for the list of points of interest
(locations). By making an API GET request to `/pois`, you can obtain a
paginated list of items with specific properties.\
\

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/pois]{.url}
:::

\
**Standalone POIs Response example:**\

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Standalone POIs API Response Example
:::

::: {.code-content}
    {
      "_links": {
        "self": {
          "href": "domain.com/pois?page=1"
        },
        "first": {
          "href": "domain.com/pois"
        },
        "last": {
          "href": "domain.com/pois?page=1"
        }
      },
      "_embedded": {
        "pois": [{
          "Id": "1",
          "SupplierId": "10",
          "ExternalId": null,
          "FeatureClass": "S",
          "FeatureCode": null,
          "CountryCode": "AT",
          "Name": "Vienna Intl Arpt",
          "Latitude": "48.1158333",
          "Longitude": "16.5665751",
          "Status": "1",
          "Timestamp": "2023-07-14 12:55:12",
          "_links": {
            "self": {
              "href": "/pois/1"
            }
          }
        },
        {

#### Important Notes:

-   To use POIs you need to make a synchronization in TRIP admin to
    import Locations. It\'s important to do this synchronization.
-   Make sure to add valid coordinates as this is the main processing
    factor in linking a location to a hotel.
-   The POIs feature is available in Version 3 of the hotels API.

Currencies {#general-currencies}
----------

### Get all currencies

Returns a list with all currencies (active & inactive) descendently
sorted by timestamp

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/currencies]{.url}
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Currencies Response Example
:::

    {
          "_links": {3 items},
          "_embedded": {1 item},
          "page_count": 1,
          "page_size": 999,
          "total_items": 178,
          "page": 1
        }
:::

### Get a currency

Returns the properties for the currency code given

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/currencies/:currencyId]{.url}
:::

or

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/currencies/:currencyCode]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                    Type   Parameter                            Value
  ---------------------------------------------- ------ ------------------------------------ -------
  The id or code that identifies the currency.   int    {\$CurrencyId} or {\$CurrencyCode}   
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Currency Response Example
:::

    {
          "Id": "1",
          "Code": "AED",
          "Name": "United Arab Emirates dirham",
          "Symbol": "د.إ",
          "Locations": "United Arab Emirates",
          "Default": "0",
          "Common": "0",
          "Status": "1",
          "CreationDate": "2018-10-22 14:05:46",
          "Timestamp": "2018-10-31 13:32:39",
          "_links": {1 item}
        }
:::

### Get all active currencies

Returns a list with all active currencies

    {
          "_links": {3 items},
          "_embedded": {1 item},
          "page_count": 1,
          "page_size": 178,
          "total_items": 178,
          "page": 1
        }
:::

Returns a history list with all registered exchange rates for the

          "page_size": 999,
          "total_items": 0,
          "page": 0
        }
:::

### Get an exchange rate

Returns all exchange rates having the given currency as base currency

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/currencies/:currencyCode/exchange]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}

  Description                              Type     Parameter          Value
  ---------------------------------------- -------- ------------------ -------

  Description                                                         Type     Parameter              Value
  ------------------------------------------------------------------- -------- ---------------------- -------
  The code that identifies the currency which will be converted.      string   {\$FromCurrencyCode}

:::

        }

Languages {#general-languages}
---------

While TRIP offers tools for translations, the project translation is
depenedent on the framework you are using for development. In case of
our CMS we do offer support inside the CMS framework for managing
translation keys, translate in any language and apply translations on
the interface. You can find more details about the CMS functionalities
here trip cms - configurations and here in the section Agency
Admin/Translate.

In case you are using only TRIP API, the translation system must be
managed by you, based on your frontend implementation. What TRIP API
offers is a languages endpoint which can be managed from TRIP\`s admin
area where you can add languages (not translations) trip cms - apis.

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/languages?limit=10]{.url}
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Languages Response Example
:::

    {
          "_links": {3 items},
          "_embedded": {1 item},
          "page_count": 1,
          "page_size": 25,
          "total_items": 2,
          "page": 1
        }
:::

### E-mail templates -- multi language

In case you want to use multi-language in your project, the e-mail
templates can ne translated or can be added for each language in TRIP\`s
admin area.

TRIP already allows saving e-mail templates per language or translating
the e-mail templates in multiple languages, and now, besides sending the
language on order request, it allows adding a property in headers on any
of the requests related to e-mail templates.

The property must be added as x-lang in header based on the language
selected by user - two letters code.

Example of requests that generate e-mails:

-   Register new user
-   Forgot password
-   Reset password
