<div>

Carbon Footprint API
--------------------

The emissions estimate can be requested for flight and hotel.

A new API is available in TRIP to request an estimate carbon footprint
for flight and hotel offers. The information is provided by third-party
suppliers, and you can connect to one of the following suppliers:

-   KlimAPi
-   Carbonsutra
-   GoClimate (Flights Only)
-   Google Travel impact

**Note:** These are estimates based on route and flight class (for
flights), and destination, stars, and number of rooms (for hotels).

### API Endpoint {#carbon-api-endpoint}

To request carbon emission estimates, make a POST request to the
following endpoint:

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/carbon-emissions]{.url}
:::

#### Flight Request {#carbon-flight-request}

In the case of flight requests, each segment should include the
following fields:

-   **from** -- Segment take off airport IATA code
-   **to** -- Segment landing airport IATA code
-   **class** -- Possible values: economy, premium, business, first
-   **roundTrip** -- \"Y\" for round-trip; \"N\" for one-way. Any other
    value will default to \"Y\"
-   **passengers** -- Number of passengers

##### Flight Request Example

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Flight Carbon Footprint Request Example
:::

    services[flight][0][from]: LGW
        services[flight][0][to]: FRA
        services[flight][0][class]: economy
        services[flight][0][passengers]: 1
        services[flight][0][roundTrip]: N
        services[flight][1][from]: FRA
        services[flight][1][to]: CDG
        services[flight][1][class]: economy
        services[flight][1][passengers]: 1
        services[flight][1][roundTrip]: N
:::

#### Hotel Request {#carbon-hotel-request}

In the case of hotel requests, the required fields include:

-   **countryCode** -- ISO 2-letter country code of the destination
-   **nights** -- Number of nights for the stay
-   **cityName** -- Name of the destination city
-   **guests** -- Total number of guests
-   **hotelRating** -- Number of hotel stars

##### Hotel Request Example

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Hotel Carbon Footprint Request Example
:::

    services[hotel][0][countryCode]: GB
        services[hotel][0][nights]: 11
        services[hotel][0][rooms]: 1
        services[hotel][0][cityName]: LONDON
        services[hotel][0][guests]: 1
        services[hotel][0][hotelRating]: 1
        services[hotel][1][countryCode]: GB
        services[hotel][1][nights]: 11
        services[hotel][1][rooms]: 1
        services[hotel][1][cityName]: LONDON
        services[hotel][1][guests]: 1
        services[hotel][1][hotelRating]: 2
:::

</div>

<div>

Consents Module
---------------

The Consents Module empowers agencies to streamline and manage user
consents seamlessly across their websites, ensuring compliance with data
privacy regulations and providing users with enhanced control over their
personal information. This module enables agencies to define, implement,
and track consents tailored to their specific requirements, catering to
the needs of both logged-in users and agency administrators.

### API Implementation:

-   **Consents Listing:** Agencies can access the API to retrieve a list
    of all defined consents. The consents are defined by the agency in
    the TRIP agency admin area. This information is crucial for
    displaying consent options to users.
-   **Register Consent Selection:** Upon a user\'s consent selection,
    the agency can submit a request to the API using the predefined
    consent ID and the user\'s consent choice (accept or decline). This
    ensures that consent information is accurately recorded and tracked.

By implementing the Consents Module and adhering to the provided API
guidelines, agencies can effectively manage user consents, maintain
compliance with data privacy regulations, and empower users to control
their personal information.

#### List {#consents-list}

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get} [/gdpr-consents-management/consents]{.url}
:::

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Consents List Response Example
:::

    {
      "_links": {3 items},
      "_embedded": {1 item},
      "page_count": 1,
      "page_size": 25,
      "total_items": 2,
      "page": 1
    }
:::

#### Register consent selection {#consents-register}

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post}
[/gdpr-consents-management/users-consents/:useremail]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
##### Parameters

  Description                       Type     Parameter        Value
  --------------------------------- -------- ---------------- -------
  Email user                        string   :useremail       
  consent Id received in response   int      ConsentId\[0\]   
:::

</div>

<div>

Batch {#general-batch}
-----

Allow executing multiple commands (Command Queue Pattern). It has a flag
that indicates that the batch is transactional (if one command fail,
revert all other which are done already) or not.

In computer science, a command queue is a queue for enabling the delay
of command execution, either in order of priority, on a first-in
first-out basis, or in any order that serves the current purpose.
Instead of waiting each command to be executed before sending the next
one, the program just puts all the commands in the queue and goes on
doing other things while the queue is processed by the executor
component (e.g. hard drive).

::: {.endpoint}
[POST]{.method .post} [/batch]{.url}
:::

::: {.endpoint}
[DELETE]{.method .delete} [/batch]{.url}
:::

::: {.parameters-table}
#### Parameters

  Description                                                                              Type      Parameter
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------- ---------------------------
  Sequential - FALSE - if the commands must be executed async, TRUE - in the given order   boolean   TRUE / FALSE
  Batch - Array of commands                                                                array     batch\[\]
  Endpoint - Url to be accessed                                                            string    batch\[0\]\[endpoint\]
  ContentType - Http header content type                                                   string    batch\[0\]\[contentType\]
  Data - Array of data to be posted                                                        array     batch\[0\]\[data\]\[\]
:::

</div>
:::

::: {#filtering-sorting .section .content-section}
Filter TRIP API responses {#filtering-sorting-title}
=========================

TRIP API Filtering Guide {#filtering-guide}
------------------------

TRIP API supports a standardized filtering structure for most of its
endpoints, allowing for precise data retrieval. Exceptions apply for
Flight, Hotel, and Activity services, which utilize custom filtering
implementations.

### Filter Parameters

Each filter follows a consistent parameter schema:

-   **filter\[index\]\[name\]:** Property to filter by (must match the
    property name returned in the API response).
-   **filter\[index\]\[term\]:** Value or list of values to match
    against.
-   **filter\[index\]\[type\]:** Condition type for the filter.

Indexing starts from 0 and should increment for each additional filter
(e.g., filter\[1\]\[name\], filter\[2\]\[name\], etc.).

### Supported Filter Types

::: {.parameters-table}
  Type                 Description
  -------------------- ----------------------------------------------------
  equal                Exact match with term value
  notEqual             Value must not equal the term
  lessThan             Value must be less than the term
  greaterThan          Value must be greater than the term
  lessThanOrEqual      Value must be less than or equal to the term
  greaterThanOrEqual   Value must be greater than or equal to the term
  like                 Partial match using wildcards (e.g., Ba%)
  between              Value must fall within a range of two values
  contains             Checks if an array-type property contains the term
  startsWith           Value begins with the term
  endsWith             Value ends with the term
  isNull               Property must be null
  isNotNull            Property must not be null
:::

### Multi-Value Filtering

Some endpoints support multiple values for a single field. These are
passed as an array of terms:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Multi-Value Filter Example
:::

    filter[0][term][0]=128
    filter[0][term][1]=15
:::

This structure can be combined with appropriate types like equal, in, or
between.

### Filter Examples

#### Cities from a Specific Country

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/static-data/cities?limit=10&filter\[0\]\[name\]=CountryId&filter\[0\]\[term\]=12]{.url}
:::

#### Countries with ID \> 2

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/static-data/countries?limit=10&filter\[0\]\[name\]=Id&filter\[0\]\[term\]=2&filter\[0\]\[type\]=greaterThan]{.url}
:::

#### Cities Starting with \"Ba\" in Country ID Range 5--20

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Complex Filter Example
:::

    GET /static-data/cities?limit=10
    &filter[0][name]=Name&filter[0][term]=Ba%&filter[0][type]=like
    &filter[1][name]=CountryId&filter[1][term][0]=5&filter[1][term][1]=20&filter[1][type]=between
:::

#### Filter Packages by Multiple Destinations

::: {.endpoint}
[GET]{.method .get}
[/v2/packages?filter\[0\]\[name\]=DestinationCity.Id&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[0\]=128&filter\[0\]\[term\]\[1\]=15]{.url}
:::

Sort TRIP API Responses {#sorting-guide}
-----------------------

TRIP REST API responses can be sorted using any field returned in the
results.

In order to sort by a specific field, you need to add another filter
parameter that will contain direction instead of term, where direction
can have the following values:

-   **asc** - ascending
-   **desc** - descending

### Example:

Cities that start with Ba, with the ID between 5 and 20, sorted by ID:

::: {.code-example}
::: {.code-header}
Sorting Example
:::

    https://yourdomain/static-data/cities?filter[0][name]=Name&filter[0][term]=Ba%&filter[0][type]=like&filter[1][name]=CountryId&filter[1][term][0]=5&filter[1][term][1]=20&filter[1][type]=between&limit=10&filter[2][name]=Id&filter[2][direction]=desc
:::
:::

::: {#rest-basics .section .content-section}
REST Basics {#rest-basics-title}
===========

General informations {#rest-general}
--------------------

### Security

All request and response exchanges are sent over Hypertext Transfer
Protocol Secure (HTTPS).

All security is based on Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) and a time based
token. If you have not obtained an authentication token, see the
authentication page for steps on how to obtain a token and then make
subsequent API calls.

Client requests that must be encrypted using SSL from a third party
device or server to the API endpoints and URIs.

### Stateless services

All TRIP REST APIs are stateless. Each request from client to server
contains all the information necessary to understand the request.
Session state is therefore kept entirely on the client server.

TRIP configures your token with authorization to make subsequent TRIP
API calls. If your token expires, you must request a new token. If you
have not obtain an authentication token, see the authentication page for
steps on how to obtain a token and then make subsequent API calls.

### Token and transaction limits

Tokens have a finite lifetime and must be refreshed. Design a workflow
that detects when an access token expires.

For example, you have to keep track of the status value returned in the
response when an expired token is detected. The response will be 511:
Network Authentication Required

If the concurrent transactions per interval of time is exceeded or the
token maximum number of request allowed is exceeded, the system will
throttle the requests and respond with a 511: Network Authentication
Required\" with the next message \"Token expired, please refresh token
before make another request\".

See the status codes and errors page for a full list of authentication
errors.

### API standards

TRIP REST APIs use the data structures that HAL - Hypertext Application
Language convention defines. See also: stateless.co for more information
regarding data types.

Our REST APIs strictly define values that can be passed as request
parameters. Refer to each REST API documentation page to identify the
data type and description for each parameter in the request and all
elements in the response.

### API versioning

Each of our REST APIs is versioned. When any of these APIs are called,
an application must include the API version in the request URI, in the
form of v n, where n represents the version number or in a custom media
type, the basic format should be Content-Type:application/vnd.\< apiname
\>.v\< version \>+json , where the API name is normalized to lowercase,
dash-separated words.

See also the endpoints and URIs page for each of our REST API methods
and endpoints.

-   **Changes to existing API versions:** when an existing API version
    receives fixes or different changes that do nor impact clients
    negatively.
-   **New API versions:** a new API version will be added when new
    functionality and major changes are not backward compatible

### Workflow for using our REST APIs

-   Format a HTTPS request header and include your applicationID, the
    secretKey and the timestamp. See also: the authentication page for
    instructions and to construct your request and how to obtain this
    elements.
-   Call the token authentication generator endpoint using the GET
    method to get the token.
-   If successful, your application receives a token. Format a HTTPS
    request header and include your token.
-   Format an HTTPS request header and include your token to the
    appropriate URL for the API you want to call and add, also the
    x-hash. See also: the authentication page for instructions on how to
    make subsequent calls
-   After you receive the response, you can continue to make more API
    calls.

HTTP headers {#rest-http-headers}
------------

The APIs expect a request header in standard HTTP 1.1 format and return
a standard HTTPS response header.

The servers return an HTTP status code. If a request fails, TRIP APIs
also return a type and message in JSON format. For more information, see
Status codes and errors.

### HTTP request headers

::: {.parameters-table}
  HTTP Request Header Fields   Required/Optional   Value                                           Description
  ---------------------------- ------------------- ----------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Content-Type                 Required            application/x-www-form-urlencoded               This field is required with the value shown for authentication requests on the authentication endpoint.
  Token                        Required            Your authentication token                       This field must be included for authenticated requests. Obtain the token from the access\_token field in the payload of the authentication response. Do not include this field in requests for authentication.
  x-hash                       Required            Your x-hash created as in authentication page   This field must be included for authentication requests on the authentication endpoint. Do not include this field in authenticated API calls.
:::

### HTTP headers for successful responses

The TRIP HTTP servers do not fully control the HTTP header fields. Some
of the header fields are controlled by libraries that are compliant with
the HTTP specification.

The following table includes headers that are returned in successful
responses. Failed responses also return some of these headers plus
additional fields.

::: {.parameters-table}
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  HTTP Request Header Fields          Description
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Vary                                Conditional\
                                      • If the request header has Accept
                                      or Accept-Encoding fields, the
                                      return of a corresponding variable
                                      is required.\
                                      • The value in this response field
                                      varies, and is dependent on
                                      specific Accept-\* headers and
                                      their values in the corresponding
                                      request.\
                                      • Example: When a client requests a
                                      response in a compressed format,
                                      pass gzip in an HTTP header with
                                      the response.

  Content-Length                      If the response has a fixed length,
                                      this header is used. It specifies
                                      the size in bytes of the body of
                                      representation.\
                                      If the response is chunked, this
                                      header is omitted.

  Transfer-Encoding                   Describes the transformation type
                                      used to transfer the message body
                                      from the sender to the recipient\
                                      If the response is chunked, the
                                      value is chunked.

  Date                                Date-timestamp\
                                      Returned in all authenticated
                                      responses.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
:::

Status codes and errors {#rest-status-codes}
-----------------------

### HTTP status codes

#### General status codes

After your request is processed, the HTTP servers return a response with
an HTTP status code.

::: {.parameters-table}
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  HTTP status code and description    Possible reasons
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  200 (OK)                            Request was successful.

  201 (Created)                       Successful creation occurred (via
                                      POST).

  204 (No content)                    Status when wrapped responses are
                                      not used and nothing is in the body
                                      (on DELETE).

  400 (Bad Request)                   Invalid format for request.\
                                      The API call includes incorrect
                                      request parameters or values, such
                                      as:\
                                      • The return date precedes the
                                      departure date.\
                                      • A required parameter is not
                                      valid.\
                                      • A required parameter or value is
                                      missing.

  403 (Forbidden)                     Request is for a resource that is
                                      forbidden.\
                                      Your client authentication
                                      credentials do not include
                                      authorization to call the API.

  404 (Not Found)                     Used when the requested resource is
                                      not found.\
                                      A URI is not valid or has missing
                                      segments, such as a version
                                      number.\
                                      A URL is incorrect.

  405 (Method not allowed)            A client called a method that is
                                      not authorized to use.\
                                      Additional headers are also
                                      returned.

  413 FULL head                       Request Entity Too Large.\
                                      The API returns this error when a
                                      request URI is too long. For
                                      example, the HTTP request\'s query
                                      string exceeds the server limit.\
                                      The response will be empty as a
                                      result.\
                                      Please consider reducing the number
                                      of request parameters in the URI or
                                      separating parameters into multiple
                                      HTTP requests.

  413 (Expectation Failed)            The server cannot meet the
                                      requirements of the expect
                                      request-header field.

  500 (Server Error)                  The service encountered an
                                      unexpected condition that prevented
                                      it from fulfilling the client is
                                      request.\
                                      The general catch-all error when
                                      the server-side throws an
                                      exception.

  511 (Network Authentication         The client needs to authenticate to
  Required)                           gain network access.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
:::

Advanced features {#rest-advanced-features}
-----------------

TRIP has introduced new capabilities to help developers deal with large
volumes of data, including pagination and predefined links for each
response. By making use of these new features, client applications can
specify the number of items (e.g. items per page), as well as the
individual data elements to be returned. The response is reduced payload
sizes, and consequently, faster and more efficient processing on the
client-side.

Pagination requests allow client applications the ability to request
only a subset of assets, rather than the complete API response. This
allows client applications to select the information needed at each step
of the workflow, cutting down bandwidth required, and improving
processing times for each request (versus returning all itineraries, for
example).

The following parameters are supported, for pagination purposes:

-   **page:** the start page represented by the number specified
-   **limit:** this is the number of individual assets that are returned
    in each page
-   A limit of 0 will return no results.

For pagination purposes, also responses have the next values:

-   **page:** the start page represented by the number specified
-   **page\_count:** the number of total pages
-   **page\_size:** this is the number of individual assets on each page
-   **total\_items:** the number of total items
-   **\_links:** a collection with the links for the first, last, next
    and current(self) page
:::
:::

::: {.footer-container}
::: {.footer-row}
::: {.footer-col}
::: {.footer-col-inner}

::: {#hyperpay-integrity-modal .pg-modal-overlay onclick="closeHyperpayIntegrityModal()" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="hyperpay-integrity-modal-title"}

::: {.pg-modal-title-group}

### Hyperpay -- PCI DSS v4.0 Integrity Guide {#hyperpay-integrity-modal-title}
:::

×
:::

::: {.pg-modal-body}
As part of the **PCI DSS v4.0** requirements for the CopyAndPay
integration, Hyperpay now returns a `Data.integrity` field in the
Payment Proxy initialize response. You must include this value in the
payment script tag on your platform.

1.  ::: {.pg-step-content}
    **Read `Data.integrity` from the initialize response**
    The initialize response now includes an `integrity` field alongside
    `scriptSrc` and `brands`. This value is a SHA-384 hash generated by
    Hyperpay to verify the authenticity of the payment script.

    ::: {.code-example style="margin-top:0.75rem;"}
    ::: {.code-header}
    Initialize Response Example
    :::

        {
          "Id": "39",
          "Action": {
            "Data": {
              "brands": "VISA MASTER",
              "integrity": "sha384-6pc5kYwI8emU3IdcwRiMTS1QQRr+xSXkTocuHHVqJxSeByqEhfhdgJye9hPxx6UB",
              "scriptSrc": "https://eu-test.oppwa.com/v1/paymentWidgets.js?checkoutId=58011A8AB0BF081001885ED86A239312.uat01-vm-tx02"
            }
          },
          "Method": "GET",
          "_links": {
            "self": {}
          }
        }
    :::
    :::

2.  ::: {.pg-step-content}
    **Add the `integrity` attribute to the script tag**
    When inserting the Hyperpay script into your page, include the
    `integrity` and `crossorigin` attributes as shown below:

    -   [integrity]{.pg-field-label} [Set to the value of
        `Data.integrity` from the initialize response (e.g.
        `sha384-abc…`).]{.pg-field-desc}
    -   [crossorigin]{.pg-field-label} [Must be set to `anonymous` for
        SRI verification to work correctly.]{.pg-field-desc}

    ::: {style="margin-top:0.75rem;"}
    `<script src="{scriptSrc}" integrity="{integrity}" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>`
    :::
    :::

3.  ::: {.pg-step-content}
    **Reference**
    For full details, see the [Open Payment Platform -- PCI DSS Widget
    Compliance
    documentation](https://wordpresshyperpay.docs.oppwa.com/tutorials/pci#widgetCompliance).
    :::
:::
:::
:::

::: {#viva-setup-modal .pg-modal-overlay onclick="closeVivaSetupModal()" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="viva-modal-title"}
::: {.pg-modal-container onclick="event.stopPropagation()"}
::: {.pg-modal-header}
::: {.pg-modal-title-group}

### Viva Wallet -- Setup Guide {#viva-modal-title}
:::

×
:::

::: {.pg-modal-body}
The payment gateway has a specific flow and the **redirect back URL**
needs to be configured in the Viva management account.

1.  ::: {.pg-step-content}
    **Access the Viva configuration account**Go to
    ::: {.pg-path}
    SALES → Online Payment
    :::

    and click on [Website/Apps]{.pg-badge}
    :::

2.  ::: {.pg-step-content}
    **Add a new Website/App** and configure the following fields:
    -   [Code]{.pg-field-label} [This code is important and must be
        configured in [TRIP]{.pg-badge} when enabling the payment
        gateway.]{.pg-field-desc}
    -   [Protocol]{.pg-field-label} [Based on your server setup (usually
        `HTTPS`).]{.pg-field-desc}
    -   [Domain name]{.pg-field-label} [Configure this with your
        domain.]{.pg-field-desc}
    -   [Integration method]{.pg-field-label} [Must be set to
        `Redirection / Native checkout v2`.]{.pg-field-desc}
    -   [Success URL & Failure URL]{.pg-field-label}
        `[TRIP API endpoint]/viva/payment/*?Redirect=true`{.pg-url-code}
        [Advanced configuration]{.pg-field-label} [Order Code: s ;
        Transaction Id: t; Language: lang]{.pg-field-desc}
    :::
:::
:::
:::
:::

# Best Practices

Source: http://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc/best-practices.md

CMS]{.brand-title}](https://developers.dcsplus.net){.navbar-brand}

::: {.doc-main role="main"}
::: {.content-section}
 Best Practices
==============

::: {.layout__panel .layout__panel--preview style="font-size: 18px;"}
::: {.gutter style="left: 0px;"}
:::

::: {.preview}
::: {.preview__inner-1}
::: {.preview__inner-2 style="padding: 10px 25px 0px;"}
::: {.cl-preview-section}
Colaborative work and versioning recommendations {#versioning .section-title}
------------------------------------------------

::: {.section-block}
In this article, we\'ll explore best practices to enhance teamwork
efficiency and have a working protocol that can be applied in your day
to day development work.

### Versioning best practices:

Create a CMS project for each state needed (development; stage; master;
production, etc\...).

Get familiar with the CMS Export/Import process

Set up a GitHub repository for your project. When you export from CMS,
the zip file will have:
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
-   pages
-   snippets
-   uploads.zip
-   translate.zip
-   config.enc
-   config.json
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
⦁ Upload all your files and folders to GitHub. This saves your project's
current state.\
⦁ To use this project in another workspace, download your code from
GitHub, zip it, and import it into your project using the CMS "Import"
button.\
This version should provide clearer instructions on how to manage
project exports and imports using CMS functionalities and GitHub
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
To work together on the same project with Git, you can follow these steps: {#git-workflow}
==========================================================================
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
Suppose developers are working on different parts of a project
(`projectX`) in the CMS workspace.
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
⦁ `projectX` repository should have a "**develop**" branch that will
eventually merge all developments from all developers\
⦁ the project repository should also have a "**master**" branch for the
version of the project that will be released, after multiple
developments will be gathered\
⦁ each developer will clone the `projectX` repository to their own local
computer and keep the "**develop**" branch regularly updated (every time
before starting a new development branch).\
⦁ each developer should have their own workspace on the CMS and have
imported the latest updated "**develop**" branch archive:
`/users/developer1/projectX` and `/users/developer2/projectX`\
⦁ for every new feature or change, each developer will make a separate
branch (eg: "dev-123-change-btn") on the project repository (locally,
then publish the branch to remote location)\
⦁ after finishing the development, the developer will push the changes
to the respective branch ("dev-123-change-btn"). Then, create a 'merge
request' in the project's github repository, for the respective branch
into the "**develop**" branch\
⦁ the merge request changes can then be reviewed and merged into the
"**develop**" branch
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
::: {.info-box .info}
::: {.info-box-content}
#### Merge Request Best Practices

Multiple **merge requests** can be opened as long as code modifications
are not done in the same area (same code chunk). Of course, this cannot
be completely prevented, so then a merge request might present
conflicts, that can be reviewed and merged manually for each conflict
zone. This can generally be avoided by keeping developments as small
(isolated) as possible and keeping up to date with the main \"develop\"
branch.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
⦁ each developer, has to update (pull the changes) their local develop
branch, from which the new development branches are created (to get the
latest developments merged into develop). Also, each time a developer
gets updates from remote repository, he has to create a zip archive file
(on local cloned project) that will be imported into their own CMS
project\
⦁ after multiple developments are done and multiple development branches
have been merged into develop and we want to release the combined
version of the project, a merge request can be created to merge
"develop" into "master"\
⦁ after this merge, the master branch will contain the snapshot of the
project that can be released and will hold that same released version
(until it's time for the next release and the new develop branch will be
merged over)\
⦁ to release the updated project, download the code from Git (master
branch), zip it, and use the CMS's "Import" function to update the
project.
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
This way, multiple developers can work on the project at the same time
and merge their changes for releases.
:::
:::

::: {.gutter style="left: 0px;"}
:::
:::
:::

::: {.gutter style="left: 0px;"}
:::
:::

::: {.clearfix style="margin-bottom:50px;"}
:::

::: {.section .diagrams-section}
::: {.cl-preview-section}
Logical Schema
==============
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}
-   given the github ProjectX repository - remote github repo
-   each developer initially clones it to their local computer with
    `git clone {URI}` -\> Local Repository N
-   each developer creates zip file from local repository files and
    import resulted archive into his own CMS workspace
-   each developer works on their own CMS projectX
-   when development is done, each developer can export from CMS and
    obtain new archive zip file that can be unzipped in local repository
    folder
-   changes can be committed on newly created branch (*from updated
    develop branch*), that will then be published to remote repository
-   each developer can open a merge request (for new published branch to
    be merged into develop branch)
-   cycle repeated (without cloning step)
:::

::: {.cl-preview-section}

# Cms Config

Source: http://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc/cms-config.md

::: {.nav-container}
[![TRIP](./images/logo-good.png) [ TRIP
CMS]{.brand-title}](https://developers.dcsplus.net){.navbar-brand}

::: {.nav-links}
[ Back to Docs](https://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc){.back-to-docs}
[Login](https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/login.html){.nav-link-item}
[Sign
Up](https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/register.html){.btn-signup}
:::
:::

::: {#doc-overlay .doc-overlay onclick="closeDocSidebar()"}
:::

::: {.doc-page}
::: {.doc-sidebar-header}
::: {.doc-sidebar-title}
CMS Configuration
:::

::: {.doc-sidebar-subtitle}
Navigation
:::
:::

-   [Project configuration and basic
    settings](#basic-settings){.nav-link}
    -   [My project uses multiple languages?](#languages){.nav-link}
    -   [Does my project use multiple currencies / exchange
        rates?](#currencies){.nav-link}
    -   [Do I need specific data before actually rendering any
        content?](#pre-render-data){.nav-link}
-   [Other project settings and
    configurations](#other-settings){.nav-link}
    -   [Using the minified PostScripts file](#postscripts){.nav-link}
    -   [Decloaking settings](#decloaking){.nav-link}

::: {.doc-main role="main"}
::: {.content-section}
 CMS Configuration
=================

Project configuration and basic settings {#basic-settings .section-title}
----------------------------------------

::: {.section-block}
The CMS interface now includes multiple configuration options in the
Config page:

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1694616846/developers.dcsplus.net/Picture1.png)\
\

Here, we can set values on different preset properties of the
\`\_\_globals\` variable, but also some custom properties as well.

By default, a new project won't have any values set here and it should
work as normal.

These configs will be able to be exported with the archive, in the
export area. The option is not checked by default because it is not
needed in the archive for the destination project (once that one has the
configs set and maybe adjusted for live production environment, we don't
want to modify them again by importing the dev configurations over). So,
the option can be checked manually once when exporting the project for
deployment and then with next updates the configs can be omitted from
the archive, unless you actually modify something inside the Config area
and you want to import the modifications in the destination project as
well, but a small config can also be manually adjusted on the
destination project as well. But keep in mind, if there are any
configurations inside an exported archive, those will overwrite
everything in the destination project.\
![](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1694616846/developers.dcsplus.net/Picture2.png)

Firstly, let's see what is possible to set in this configuration area.
:::

::: {#snippetname .section-block}
### My project uses multiple languages? {#languages .block-title}

Any CMS project can use multiple languages and translations. To enable
this, we just need to [add active languages]{.underline} using the
Languages config typeahead\

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1694616846/developers.dcsplus.net/Picture3.png)\
\

Having added the [active languages]{.underline} means the project will
have the languages data available on ` ____globals.language.list__ ` but
[no translation will be enabled yet.]{.underline}

If we want to use a specific language (with translations applied) as a
default, on our website project, then we can select which of the active
languages is the default, by clicking on it.

NOTE: just as well, we can omit saving a default language and just
initiate the translations inside our postscript files, calling
\_\_app.language.init method with the language code of choice.

Here we have selected German as default language, so the project will
now try to load the german translations automatically:

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1694616846/developers.dcsplus.net/Picture4.png)\
\

Of course we have to go into Pages -\> Translations, scan and save the
translations on pages, for them to actually be able to load, but the
request for the translation files will be visible (in Network area)
anyway, when accessing the project homepage, for example. If no
translations were saved for that page, the request will fail with 404
status error, which is normal. Then the platform will default to
implicit language, showing the translation phrases basically.
:::

::: {#snippetname .section-block}
### Does my project use multiple currencies / exchange rates? {#currencies .block-title}

For using multiple currencies we have to set the values inside of the
Currencies area. Here we can set the active currencies that we'll want
to use and by doing so, we provide all the data related on
` ____globals.project.currency.list__ `\

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1694616846/developers.dcsplus.net/Picture5.png)\
\

We can set a default as well, by clicking on the currency labels added.
The selected default will be the currency used as a default in the
interface and all its data will be available on
` ____globals.project.currency.display__ `

In order to use exchange rates, we'll need to request the 'live' data on
the website, in postScripts by using a dedicated helper:
` ____app.exchange.getExchangeRate__ ` which receives 2 params: 'from'
and 'to', so to obtain the exchange rate we actually need to know the
'from' currency, which is the provider (IRIX) currency, usually. We can
set this one as well in the Currencies area of the configs

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1694616846/developers.dcsplus.net/Picture6.png)\
\

This will be available on ` ____globals.project.currency.provider__ `.

Here we have selected German as default language, so the project will
now try to load the german translations automatically:

\
\

::: {.callout-block .callout-info}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### NOTE: {#note .callout-title}

the exchange rate request should be done before actually rendering the
page, when you have to display exchanged prices, so the developer would
probably want to use the customInitProp config, in order to block the
automatic rendering and manually control the start of the rendering
process, once all exchange data is available
:::
:::

To render a currencies-select element we can use the data on
`__globals.project.currency.list`. The change action can be managed
through `__app.exchange.getExchangeRate` method which will also set the
necessary data on `__app.exchange.rate` and `__globals and storage` . On
`__globals.activeCurrency` there will always be the active currency at
any given moment, being it the default one that's enabled or a custom
user-set currency, selected from the interface.
:::

::: {#snippetname .section-block}
### Do I need specific data before actually rendering any content? {#pre-render-data .block-title}

Sometimes, for rendering the content of the website, we need to gather
some data before starting rendering, so that we have it available for
all the snippets in the page.\

For this purpose, the developer can use the 'Custom init event'
property, which will be available in the page on
`__globals.project.customInitProp`

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1694616846/developers.dcsplus.net/Picture7.png)\
\

This accepts any alphanumeric value and [if set, the cms app will block
the automatic rendering process]{.underline} and bind its value to an
event listener that is linked to starting the rendering.

So, the developer will complete this value (eg: myCustomInitPropName)
and then can write any javascript logic inside a STATIC (!important)
postScript, followed by triggering that event with either
`doEvent(‘myCustomInitPropName’)` or (if they don't want to hardcode the
value itself inside the scripts)
`__hooks[__globals.project.customInitProp]()`, which will do the same
thing

\
\

::: {.callout-block .callout-info}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### NOTE: {#note-1 .callout-title}

it's important that any javascript meant to run before the rendering of
the page, is written inside the postScript of a static snippet, because
these are run before rendering
:::
:::
:::

::: {#concept-section .section .doc-section}
Other project settings and configurations {#other-settings .section-title}
-----------------------------------------

::: {.section-block}
::: {#snippetname .section-block}
### Using the minified PostScripts file {#postscripts .block-title}

enabling the use of a single file for all dynamic postScripts inside a
page implies using non-anonymous modules for requirejs, so the developer
needs to prepare all postScripts for this purpose, defining a unique id
for each module / postScript.\

So, let's say we have a dynamic snippet named \`homepage-hero\` and we
need to initialize a jQuery slider plugin for that hero area, we would
need to do that inside the postScript making sure jQuery is loaded, so
we'd be writing something like:

`                                             define([‘jquery’], function ($) {                                                                                          $(‘#HeroSlider’).initSlider();                                                                                          });                                         `

So if enabling PostScripts file, we would need to make sure that this is
not an anonymous module, so we'd have to provide an id, modifying the
first line of the postScript:

`define(‘homepageHero’, [‘jquery’], function ($) {`
:::

::: {#snippetname .section-block}
### Decloaking settings {#decloaking .block-title}

In order to better control the loading and reveal of the page, there is
a decloaking process built-in the CMS app, which ties into the rendering
process.

For standard dynamic snippets the rendering itself should take a few
milliseconds. Depending on the project and if rendering is blocked for
other requests for data fetching, the snippets will take more time to
actually render and this is where the cloaking loader comes in handy.

Some classes are being added to the body element during this time so
that the developer can write custom CSS to accommodate for a better
visual loading experience to the user. When entering a CMS page, the
body element won't have any classes (other than the ones specified in
the page HTML). This state can be used to display a (cloaking) loader
above the page. Once the snippets are rendered in the page the body
element receives the 'decloaking' and 'loaded' classes. The latter will
remain on the body, so it can be used to remove the default cloaking
loader. The 'decloaking' class will be removed after 600ms (default
setting, if not specified in config area), so we can use this one to
animate a smooth transition maybe, from loading state to revealing the
rendered content.

So within the decloaking configurations the developer can:

-   enable custom decloaking -- this will block default decloaking
    process, so that the page will be rendered in the background, but
    the classes won't be added to the body so the page won't be revealed
    until it is manually triggered from within a postScript using
    `__app.utils.decloak()` method

-   decloaking duration -- here the developer can specify an exact
    amount of time (in milliseconds) that the 'decloaking' class will be
    present on the body element. Syncing this with the duration of a
    custom animation can help with a smoother transition from loading
    state to content reveal

-   decloak snippet/delay -- this config property takes either a snippet
    name, a snippet order number or a time delay (in milliseconds, for
    values \>= 100). Providing a snippet name will trigger decloaking
    right after that specific snippet was rendered. Providing a snippet
    order number (up to 99) the developer can delay the page reveal to
    sooner or later during the rendering process, for example when
    having multiple snippets that would be out of view at page load, we
    might not want to wait for those to be rendered to reveal the
    rendered content, so we can try different values and see how the
    page is rendered.

    Setting a time delay (in milliseconds, at least 100) will timeout
    the decloaking from the start of the rendering process. NOTE: take
    into account this setting does not work with 'enabling custom
    decloaking' and also, the rendering and decloaking processes might
    perform differently depending on client computer, although it should
    be virtually similar.

Another method of controlling the reveal of the page, that is even more
exact, is with using '-rendered' events. The CMS app will automatically
trigger '\[snippetName\]-rendered' events right after the related
snippet was rendered. So, within a static snippet postScript, the
developer can bind a listener to a specific '...-rendered' event and tie
that to revealing the page content. So, for example, let's say we want
our homepage to be revealed once the hero snippet ('homepage-hero') is
rendered, we'd write inside our custom init logic (in a static snippet
postScript):

NOTE remember to also check the \`enable custom decloaking\` setting in
configs, to make sure the default decloaking is blocked.
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

# Marketing

Source: http://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc/marketing.md

::: {.nav-container}
[![TRIP](./images/logo-good.png) [ TRIP
CMS]{.brand-title}](https://developers.dcsplus.net){.navbar-brand}

::: {.nav-links}
[ Back to Docs](https://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc){.back-to-docs}

Marketing Strategy

::: {.doc-sidebar-subtitle}

::: {.doc-main role="main"}
::: {.content-section}
 Marketing & SEO
===============

::: {.section}
Marketing Strategy Guide for TRIP
=================================

This guide is designed to help travel agencies effectively utilize the
TRIP platform for their marketing efforts. Follow these steps to create
and implement a robust marketing strategy.
:::

::: {.section}
1. Establish Your Differentiators {#differentiators}
---------------------------------

Identify what sets your agency apart from the competition:

-   Best prices
-   Exceptional services
-   Expert knowledge about destinations
-   Exclusive packages and promotions
-   Best flight dates or exclusive hotel contracts

Highlight these differentiators in your marketing materials and on your
TRIP website.
:::

::: {.section}
2. List Services and Create a Promotion Plan {#promotion-plan}
--------------------------------------------

Develop a plan to promote the services you offer:

-   List all services you wish to promote.
-   Create a strategy based on your brand\'s strong points.
-   Implement relevant content in TRIP to support your promotional
    activities.
:::

::: {.section}
3. Promote Seasonal Offers and Destinations {#seasonal-offers}
-------------------------------------------

Enhance your promotions by focusing on:

-   Seasonal activities and destinations
-   Specific services and pricing for each season

Create widgets on your TRIP website where users can select activities,
transportation, and travel periods to find the best destinations and
offers.
:::

::: {.section}
4. Develop Generic Destination Pages {#destination-pages}
------------------------------------

Create pages for popular destinations and link them to:

-   Best activities and attractions
-   Hotels and periods ideal for each destination

Ensure these pages are comprehensive and appealing to potential
travelers.
:::

::: {.section}
5. Implement a Flight Calendar {#flight-calendar}
------------------------------

Provide a calendar showcasing:

-   Best flight dates and prices
-   Information from your system cache for accurate data
:::

::: {.section}
6. Highlight Most Searched Destinations {#searched-destinations}
---------------------------------------

Showcase:

-   Most popular destinations
-   Prices and offers related to these destinations
:::

::: {.section}
7. Promote Agency Packages {#agency-packages}
--------------------------

Create brand awareness by promoting:

-   Packages and products created by your agency
-   Marketing materials bundled with travel services

Include additional services such as airport transfers to streamline
operational processes.
:::

::: {.section}
8. Offer Discount Vouchers {#discount-vouchers}
--------------------------

Attract more customers by:

-   Providing discount vouchers
-   Promoting these vouchers across different channels
:::

::: {.section}
9. Upsell and Correct Information {#upsell}
---------------------------------

Ensure accurate and updated information on:

-   Flights and destinations
-   Visa requirements and important data for travelers

Create and display rules for probable routes, and update them as
necessary.
:::

::: {.section}
10. Utilize Automated Email Marketing {#email-marketing}
-------------------------------------

Enhance engagement by:

-   Generating emails based on customer actions
-   Cross-selling and collecting feedback through these emails
:::

::: {.section}
Marketing Actions
-----------------

Implement the following strategies to boost your sales:

-   **Buyer Persona:** Define user personas and create targeted market
    strategies.
-   **Age-Specific Packages:** Develop and promote packages for specific
    age groups, such as seniors.
-   **City Breaks:** Promote trending city breaks and link them to
    relevant activities and social media trends.
-   **Social Media Presence:** Identify and leverage trends, post
    consistently, and affiliate with influential online figures.
-   **SEO:** Utilize SEO best practices to improve visibility.
-   **Paid Ads:** Invest in paid ads on market-specific platforms.
-   **Email Marketing:** Use email marketing to cross-sell and promote
    destination pages.
:::

::: {.note}
**Note:** This guide provides a framework for developing and
implementing your marketing strategy using TRIP. Adapt these steps to
fit your agency\'s specific needs and resources.
:::
:::
:::
:::

# Pages

Source: http://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc/pages.md

::: {.nav-container}
[![TRIP](./images/logo-good.png) [ TRIP
CMS]{.brand-title}](https://developers.dcsplus.net){.navbar-brand}

::: {.nav-links}
[ Back to Docs](https://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc){.back-to-docs}
[Login](https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/login.html){.nav-link-item}
[Sign
Up](https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/register.html){.btn-signup}
:::
:::

::: {#doc-overlay .doc-overlay onclick="closeDocSidebar()"}
:::

::: {.doc-page}
::: {.doc-sidebar-header}
::: {.doc-sidebar-title}
Pages
:::

::: {.doc-sidebar-subtitle}
Navigation
:::
:::

-   [What is a Page?](#what-is-page){.nav-link}
-   [Properties](#properties){.nav-link}
-   [Parameters](#parameters){.nav-link}
-   [Nesting Snippets](#nesting){.nav-link}
-   [Render Workflow](#render-workflow){.nav-link}
-   [How to Use It](#how-to-use){.nav-link}
-   [Recommendations](#recommendations){.nav-link}

::: {.doc-main role="main"}
::: {.content-section}
 Pages
=====

What is a page? {#what-is-page}
---------------

"*A document which can be displayed in a web browser such as Firefox,
Google Chrome, Opera, Microsoft Internet Explorer or Edge, or Apple\'s
Safari. These are also often called just \"pages\".*" - [Developer
Mozilla](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/Common_questions/Pages_sites_servers_and_search_engines)

"*A static web page is delivered exactly as stored, as web content in
the web server\'s file system. In contrast, a dynamic web page is
generated by a web application, usually driven by server-side software.
Dynamic web pages help the browser (the client) to enhance the web page
through user input to the server.*" -
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_page)

In TRIP, besides the above definition, pages acts like containers for
[snippets.](https://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc/snippets)

Properties
----------

### Basics

A CMS page can be written using standard HTML code or TWIG code. Each
time a page is published it will be (re)rendered and written on disk.

### Full page

Full page mode enable: everything will be edited in body area (including
head) - so we can guarantee that the code is a valid html code

Full page mode disabled: we separate head and body content -- we should
be able to generate a valid html page

### Static page

You can write a full HTML page, without any snippet and you can
configure it as static.

### Crawlable page

A crawlable page means the content of the page is visible for the bots
as well. If crawlable disabled, the conetnt of the page will not be
available for any user-agent bot

Recommendations
---------------

When designing your snippets we strongly recommend to follow DRY pattern
and micro-service approach: a snippet should only be responsible for
doing one thing.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.footer-row}

::: {.content-section}
 Quick Start
===========

What is TRIP?
-------------

**TRIP** is an API-first travel booking platform designed exclusively
for **B2C** travel applications. It provides powerful RESTful APIs for
building custom online travel experiences that include real-time flight
and hotel search, secure user management, and flexible booking flows.

Key capabilities:
-----------------

-   Flight and Hotel booking APIs with real-time availability
-   Dynamic API structure using search containers
-   Secure user account management, registration, login, and MFA
-   Support for discount codes, vouchers, and markups
-   Booking approvals, refunds, and cancellation logic
-   Multi-language support
-   Multi-currency price display (payments processed in supplier\'s
    currency)
-   Integrations with IRIX and AIDA suppliers
-   Online payments through Stripe, Mobilpay, Hyperpay, Svea, and more
-   Support for multiple IRIX resellers (e.g., dev vs. prod
    environments)

TRIP API Use Cases {#use-cases}
------------------

1.  **Online Travel Booking Website**

    Create a powerful booking platform to sell services such as:

    -   Flight tickets
    -   Accommodation
    -   Activities and tours
    -   Custom-tailored travel packages

    Features include:

    -   Search, upgrade, and book services seamlessly
    -   Secure payments through multiple online payment processors, with
        global coverage via the TRIP Payment Proxy (single integration
        for a worldwide catalog of providers)

2.  **Mobile Application**

    Deliver a smooth on-the-go booking experience with a dedicated
    mobile app, synchronized with the main platform.

3.  **Membership Website**

    Offer personalized experiences and preferential discounts based on
    user type, with flexible membership tiers and benefits.

4.  **Destination Management Website**

    Launch a fully TRIP-managed destinations website, allowing you to:

    -   Create, manage, and publish content directly from the TRIP Admin
        Area
    -   Maintain complete control over destination pages and promotions

5.  **Events Website**

    Build and manage a dedicated events platform:

    -   Control static content from the TRIP Administration Area
    -   Link travel services to specific events
    -   Manage bookings separately per event
    -   Configure individual payment accounts per event
    -   Sell and manage your own inventory directly within the event
        site
:::
:::
:::

# Seo

Source: http://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc/seo.md

::: {.nav-container}
[![TRIP](./images/logo-good.png) [ TRIP
CMS]{.brand-title}](https://developers.dcsplus.net){.navbar-brand}

::: {.nav-links}
[ Back to Docs](https://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc){.back-to-docs}
[Login](https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/login.html){.nav-link-item}
[Sign
Up](https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/register.html){.btn-signup}
:::
:::

::: {#doc-overlay .doc-overlay onclick="closeDocSidebar()"}
:::

::: {.doc-page}
::: {.doc-sidebar-header}
::: {.doc-sidebar-title}
SEO in TRIP CMS
:::

::: {.doc-sidebar-subtitle}
Navigation
:::
:::

-   [What is TRIP?](#what-is-trip){.nav-link}
-   [SEO Challenges](#seo-challenges){.nav-link}
-   [Our Solution](#our-solution){.nav-link}
-   [Implementation](#implementation){.nav-link}

::: {.doc-main role="main"}
::: {.content-section}
 How to Obtain SEO with TRIP
===========================

::: {.section}
Before diving into the technical details, it\'s crucial to understand
what TRIP is and how it works:
:::

::: {.section}
What is TRIP?
-------------

TRIP is an engine/application with an API output. It allows access via
REST API requests, enabling functionalities such as:

-   Making searches
-   Booking services
-   Retrieving data for widgets

One of the main benefits of TRIP is its content availability in JSON
format. This format is browser-friendly, allowing FrontEnd developers to
create websites without backend knowledge.
:::

::: {.section}
Dynamic Content and SEO Challenges {#seo-challenges}
----------------------------------

Implementing TRIP on the FrontEnd typically involves JavaScript requests
and client-side rendering. While this modern approach enhances user
experience, it poses challenges for SEO:

-   Search engines traditionally expect content to be available on the
    page load, not gradually through dynamic JavaScript requests.
-   Dynamic content served via JavaScript may not be fully compatible
    with current search engine crawling methods.
:::

::: {.section}
Our Solution: Technical CMS {#our-solution}
---------------------------

To address these SEO challenges, we have developed a technical CMS with
the following features:

-   **Work Environment:** The CMS provides a space to write and manage
    your code.
-   **Rendering System:** The platform handles rendering based on
    User-Agent types.

The CMS adapts its rendering strategy depending on the User-Agent:

-   **For bots:** Pages are rendered server-side. The CMS makes API
    requests and serves the page as HTML with all data preloaded.
-   **For other User-Agents:** Pages are rendered client-side as usual.
:::

::: {.section}
Implement your website in TRIP CMS while considering SEO {#implementation}
--------------------------------------------------------

As mentioned above, TRIP CMS already takes care of the content rendering
part, however, in order for the platform to pre-render content, the
snippets must be implemented using Data source.

-   **Step 1:** Create your implementation strategy, starting with the
    pages that you want to be indexed and crawled.
-   **Step 2:** Set your pages as \"Crawlable page\". If it\`s a static
    page, just write your HTML, and that\`s that. If you use snippets
    with only html & css, then set the page on dynamic and the snippets
    as static.
-   **Step 3:** If your content is dynamic, meaning you need to load
    data in a page from an API, you need to implement your snippet using
    data source.
-   **Step 4:** Harnest the power of TRIP admin adn TRIP modules. Create
    entities and events to populate your pages and add custom fields to
    enhance page SEO, like fields for title or meta items.

##### The CMS adapts its rendering strategy depending on the User-Agent:

-   **For bots:** Pages are rendered server-side. The CMS makes API
    requests and serves the page as HTML with all data preloaded.
-   **For other User-Agents:** Pages are rendered client-side as usual.
:::

::: {.note}
**Note:** This approach ensures that search engines receive fully
rendered HTML content, improving SEO effectiveness while maintaining a
dynamic and responsive user experience.
:::
:::
:::
:::
