::: {.doc-main role="main"}
::: {.content-section}
::: {#intro-section .section .doc-section}
What is a snippet? {#what-is-snippet .section-title}
------------------

::: {.section-block}
"*Snippet is a programming term for a small region of re-usable source
code, machine code, or text. Ordinarily, these are formally defined
operative units to incorporate into larger programming modules.*" -
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snippet_(programming))

In TRIP, snippets are the core fundation and the most powerfull assets.
They provide modularity and flexibility by their nature. Although, they
may seem simple, their applicability is limitless.

You can use a snippet from defining a specific portion of a style sheet
or html to define complex functionalities or custom integrations.

There are two kinds of snippets: [static](#snippetstatic){.scrollto} and
[dynamic](#snippetdynamic){.scrollto}.\
You can see a static snippet like a piece of puzzle and a dynamic
snippet like a moving gear wheel.\
Usualy a snippet is designed to do only one thing.

The link between multiple snippets is made throught
[pages.](https://developers.dcsplus.net/trip/doc/pages)
:::
:::

::: {#concept-section .section .doc-section}
Concept {#concept .section-title}
-------

::: {.section-block}
Robert C. Martin conceived the term [single responsibility
principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_responsibility_principle)
which states "*gather together those things that change for the same
reason, and separate those things that change for different reasons.*"

Our snippet architecture takes the same approach. Each snippet can be
developed, deployed, and maintained independently. Each snippet should
be responsible for discrete tasks and can communicate with other
snippets to solve a larger complex of business problems.

A snippet covers the presentation tier from the [3 tier
architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multitier_architecture#Three-tier_architecture)
and facilitates communication with application layer.\
![3-tier architecture
diagram](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/c_thumb,w_200,g_face/v1553884677/developers.dcsplus.net/docs/3tier.png)
:::
:::

::: {#definition-section .section .doc-section}
Properties {#properties .section-title}
----------

::: {#snippetname .section-block}
### Name {#name .block-title}

You can name your snippet however you like, but we recommend to be as
much as possible descriptive about it\'s purpose.\
The snippet name must begin with a letter (\[A-Za-z\]) and may be
followed by any number of letters, digits (\[0-9\]), hyphens (\"-\"),
underscores (\"\_\"), colons (\":\"), and periods (\".\"). `styles_css`
`hotelItem` `search-form`

After creating a snippet it can be inserted into pages or other snippets
using it\'s placeholder ` __snippet::search-form__ `

::: {.callout-block .callout-danger}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Important {#important .callout-title}

Our render consider a snippet, and try to render it, any text that start
with **\_\_snippet::** and end with **\_\_**\
[*( \_\_ - double underscore )*]{.small}
:::
:::
:::

::: {#snippettype .section-block}
### Type {#type .block-title}

Starting with [version **3.1.2**]{.badge .badge-updated
style="font-size: 0.85rem; padding: 0.35rem 0.85rem;"} of the CMS, the
[Type]{.badge .badge-new
style="font-size: 0.85rem; padding: 0.35rem 0.85rem;"} property was
added for dynamic snippets, currently supporting these options:

-   [standard]{.badge .badge-info
    style="font-size: 0.8rem; padding: 0.3rem 0.7rem; margin-right: 0.5rem; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #3b82f6 0%, #60a5fa 100%); color: white;"}
    -- this is the default value for dynamic snippets which means the
    snippet postScript will be run immediately after the snippet was
    rendered.
-   [component]{.badge .badge-info
    style="font-size: 0.8rem; padding: 0.3rem 0.7rem; margin-right: 0.5rem; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #3b82f6 0%, #60a5fa 100%); color: white;"}
    -- this option means the CMS will not automatically run the
    postScript after having rendered its template in the page.
    Additionally, all component-type snippets are added to the new
    global (window) Array variable: `Components`. Based on the
    component-type snippets, a new `ComponentsRequireConfig` object will
    be available globally, that can be used to extend the requirejs
    config, so that the component snippets postScripts can be used with
    their exact names as aliases.
-   [module]{.badge .badge-info
    style="font-size: 0.8rem; padding: 0.3rem 0.7rem; margin-right: 0.5rem; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #3b82f6 0%, #60a5fa 100%); color: white;"}
    (from [version **3.1.3**]{.badge .badge-updated
    style="font-size: 0.85rem; padding: 0.35rem 0.85rem;"}) - this
    enables using postScripts as modules natively in the browser, with
    imports. The snippets of type
    `module`{style="background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15); color: #60a5fa; border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.3); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; font-weight: 600;"}
    can be used as dependencies for other snippets and they will be
    available in the global scope inside the `Modules` Array.
    Additionally, all module-type snippets are added to an importmap so
    they can easily be referenced by their respective snippet name, when
    importing them.

The
`component`{style="background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15); color: #60a5fa; border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.3); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; font-weight: 600;"}/`module`{style="background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15); color: #60a5fa; border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.3); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; font-weight: 600;"}
type was added as an option to facilitate building with javascript
frameworks on top of the CMS, making use of the same snippet structure.
This enables the developer to choose how to load and when to run, the
snippet script.

The
`component`{style="background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15); color: #60a5fa; border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.3); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; font-weight: 600;"}
and
`module`{style="background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15); color: #60a5fa; border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.3); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; font-weight: 600;"}
type snippets can still contain the template and the CSS styles, which
will be included in the page same as for any normal
`standard`{style="background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15); color: #60a5fa; border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.3); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; font-weight: 600;"}
dynamic snippet.

::: {.callout-block .callout-warning}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Important {#important-1 .callout-title}

In order to have the
`component`{style="background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15); color: #60a5fa; border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.3); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; font-weight: 600;"}-type
snippets inside the new **Components** array and the
`module`{style="background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15); color: #60a5fa; border: 1px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.3); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; font-weight: 600;"}-type
snippets inside the new **Modules** array, their placeholder
`__snippet::my-component-snippet__` (or
`__snippet::my-module-snippet__`) needs to be included in the page, even
if they don\'t have a usable template or if they are visibly hidden to
the user.
:::
:::
:::

::: {#snippetcategory .section-block}
### Category {#category .block-title}

You can group similar snippets under same category. This helps you when
searching to insert subsnippets.
:::

::: {#snippetsubsnippet .section-block}
### Subsnippet {#subsnippet .block-title}

One of the most coolest feature of the TRIP\'s snippets is nesting. Yes,
you can use snippet inside another snippet. There is no limit regarding
how depth nesting could go. Each depth is treated as a layer composing a
[FIFO
queue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFO_(computing_and_electronics)):
layers are render in order: first layer first, then the second one and
so on. With this in mind you should be carefull nesting snippets to
deep.

::: {.callout-block .callout-success}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Useful Tip: {#useful-tip .callout-title}

If you have a complex page which uses lots of snippets, it\'s better to
layer them. Static and dynamic snippets which doesn\'t depend on
external calls should be included directly in page, while heavy dynamic
snippets should be included into another static snippet. This way the
user sees the static data immediatly and have the best user experience.
:::
:::
:::

::: {#snippettemplate .section-block}
### Template {#template .block-title}

A template can be viewed as a simply html file. The snippet\'s template
takes place of the snippet placeholder after rendering.

To create a more outstanding experience you can write dynamic templates
using [twig](https://twig.symfony.com/doc/2.x/templates.html). We
support almost all features of twig. For a complete list of supported
features you can check
[twigjs](https://github.com/twigjs/twig.js/wiki/Implementation-Notes)

::: {.code-block}
###### Template Example

    <h1>Hotel list</h1>
    <ul>
        {% for hotel in hotels %}
            <li>{{ hotel.Name|e }}</li>
        {% endfor %}
    </ul>
:::
:::

::: {#snippetdatasource .section-block}
### Data source {#data-source .block-title}

When creating dynamic snippets sometimes you will want to gather input
from your data layer and use it in your template. That\'s why we\'ve
added a data source feature for snippets.

You can choose to use from two types of data sources:

-   **from our endpoint builder module** - you can generate public or
    private custom endpoints from TRIP\'s admin, based on others modules
    data *(from cache, search history, events, products etc\...)*. Ex:
    you can generate an endpoint that will publish your most booked
    destinations.
-   **from external sources** - this allows 3rd parties integrations.
    Ex: you may want to create a live feed of your latest blog posts.\
    [Important note here is that we only support JSON responses.]{.badge
    .badge-warning}

Each type of data source support query and route [dynamic
parameters](#snippetparamdynamic).

::: {.callout-block .callout-info}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Query string parameters {#query-string-parameters .callout-title}

For security, we will pass to the snippet\'s data source only the
parameters that are present in the snippet blueprint call.\
For the following snippet `____snippet::user({"id" : 6})__` we will pass
to it\'s data source ,if any - in our case it\'s */users*, only the *id*
query string param, even if the page where the snippet is used is
accessed with multiple query string params.\
So for the page
<https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/johnnyb/flux/published/user.html?id=6&name=coco>
which contains the above snippet only *id* param will be used.
:::
:::

The content of the specified data source is available into your twig
template under the variable **\_\_ds**.

To make your life easier when mapping the data source into your
template, the data source response is available into data source panel.

Because we are devoted supporters of [single responsibility
principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_responsibility_principle)
we allow only one data source per snippet.

The data source endpoint it\'s called before rendering the snippet\'s
template, so it might delay the rendering of the snippet depending of
how network costly it is. We recommend that snippets with large data
sources or time consuming to be layered back on a deeper render level,
to minimize the impact on the user experience.

#### Example:

::: {.code-block}
###### User profile page

    <!doctype html>
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <!-- Required meta tags -->
        <meta charset="utf-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, shrink-to-fit=no">

        <!-- Bootstrap CSS -->
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/twitter-bootstrap/3.4.1/css/bootstrap.min.css" crossorigin="anonymous">

        <title>User profile!</title>
      </head>
      <body>
        __snippet::user({"id" : 6})__
        <!-- Optional JavaScript -->
        <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jquery/3.3.1/jquery.min.js" type="text/javascript" charset="utf-8" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
        <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/twitter-bootstrap/3.4.1/js/bootstrap.min.js" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
      </body>
    </html>
:::

::: {.code-block}
###### User profile snippet: `____snippet::user({"id" : 6})__`

data source: <https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users>

    <div class="container">
    <div class="row">
       <div class="panel panel-default">
          <div class="panel-heading">
             <h4 >User Profile</h4>
          </div>
          <div class="panel-body">
             <div class="col-md-4 col-xs-12 col-sm-6 col-lg-4">
                <img alt="User Pic" src="https://x1.xingassets.com/assets/frontend_minified/img/users/nobody_m.original.jpg" id="profile-image1" class="img-circle img-responsive"> 
             </div>
             <div class="col-md-8 col-xs-12 col-sm-6 col-lg-8" >
                <div class="container" >
                    {% set user = __ds[0] %}
                   <h2>{{user.name}}</h2>
                   <p></p>
                </div>
                <hr>
                <ul class="container details" >
                   <li>
                      <p><span class="glyphicon glyphicon-user one" style="width:50px;"></span>{{user.username}}</p>
                   </li>
                   <li>
                      <p><span class="glyphicon glyphicon-envelope one" style="width:50px;"></span>{{user.email}}</p>
                   </li>
                   <li>
                      <p><span class="glyphicon glyphicon-phone" style="width:50px;"></span>{{user.phone}}</p>
                   </li>
                </ul>
                <hr>
                <div class="col-sm-5 col-xs-6 tital " >Company: {{user.company.name}} <br> <i>{{user.company.bs}}</i></div>
                 <div class="col-sm-5 col-xs-6 tital " >
                    <address>
                        street: {{user.address.street}}<br> 
                        Visit us at:<br>
                        {{user.website}}<br>
                        Box {{user.address.zipcode}}, {{user.address.suite}}<br>
                        {{user.address.city}}
                        </address>
                 </div>
             </div>
          </div>
       </div>
    </div>
:::

You can view the rendered page
[here](https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/johnnyb/flux/published/user.html)

In the above example the dynamic snippet *user* has a data source set.
When inserted in the user profile page a data source parameter was
specified `{ id: 6}`. So, when the snippet is rendered we make first a
call to <https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users?id=6> and put the
response under `__ds` variable. If we access the page specifing id in
query string [domain.com/user.html?id=7](domain.com/user.html?id=7) the
snippet will gather info about the user identified by the new id (7).

As you can see we didn\'t changed the page structure, but only specifing
dynamic parameter to the *user* snippet we are able to create user
profile page.

::: {.callout-block .callout-info}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Caching {#caching .callout-title}

If there are multiple snippets, in the same page, using the same data
source the system will make the request only once.
:::
:::
:::

::: {#snippetlibraries .section-block}
### Preloaded libraries {#preloaded-libraries .block-title}

[requirejs]{.badge .badge-info title="requirejs.org"} [jquery]{.badge
.badge-info title="jquery.com"} [toastr]{.badge .badge-info
title="github.com/CodeSeven/toastr"} [momentjs]{.badge .badge-info
title="momentjs.com"} [cookiejs]{.badge .badge-info
title="github.com/js-cookie/js-cookie"} [twigjs]{.badge .badge-info
title="github.com/twigjs/twig.js"}
:::

::: {#snippetpostscript .section-block}
### Post-script {#post-script .block-title}

Each snippet comes together with post-script which is basically a
javascript.

Post-script content is persisted on disk into a javascaript file which
has the same name as the snippet itself with the *\_postScript* suffix
added.\
Ex: for snippet hotel-item the post-script file will be
hotel-item\_postScript.js

::: {.callout-block .callout-success}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Useful Tip: {#useful-tip-1 .callout-title}

You can use the post-script of a snippet as a dependency of another
snippet. The post-script url is available under the
**http://yourdomain.com/published/js/snippetname\_postScript.js**
:::
:::

Depending of the nature of the snippet: static or dynamic, the
post-script act differently.

-   **Static** - is executed at *document.ready*
-   **Dynamic** - is executed *render.post*; after the template was
    rendered

::: {.callout-block .callout-info}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Module loader {#module-loader .callout-title}

In order to improve speed and quality of your code and because we like
modularity, all javascript files are loaded with
[RequireJS](https://requirejs.org/)
:::
:::

::: {.code-block}
###### Post-script Code Example

    requirejs(['jquery'], function( $ ) {
        "use strict";

        window.app = window.app || new application() ;
        
        function application() {}
    });
:::
:::

::: {#snippetcss .section-block}
### Css {#css .block-title}

Because you are a stylish developer, you will want to also add a drop of
your style into your snippets.

For a better perfomance the style of the snippet is appended on the
page\'s header directly.

If multiple styled snippets are grouped on the same page, the order of
the snippets in page dictates the order of the block styles in head. If
a snippet is present multiple times on the same page, it\'s style will
be appended only once with the position of the last snippet.

::: {.callout-block .callout-success}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Useful Tip: {#useful-tip-2 .callout-title}

You can create static snippets with only css property. This way you can
create a snippet that will hold the style of your entire application.
:::
:::
:::

::: {#snippetstatic .section-block}
### Static {#static .block-title}

A static snippet is rendered at page generation and not at a run time.\
It\'s data source is ignored and it\'s post-script is executed at
*document.ready* page event.

Static snippets are the fastest ones and their are usually used to keep
code modularized and organized.

#### Google maps static snippet example

::: {.code-block}
###### Template panel

    <div id="map"></div>
:::

::: {.code-block}
###### Javascript panel

    requirejs(['https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js?key=yourApiKey'], function(){
        
        var map;
    	var dcshq = {lat: 44.4167136, lng: 26.1151618};

    	map = new google.maps.Map(document.getElementById('map'), {
    		zoom: 12,
    		center: dcshq
    	});

    });
:::

::: {.code-block}
###### CSS panel

    #map {
        width:100vw;
        height:100vh;
    }

    .main {
      margin-top: 25px;
    }

    .nav-tabs {
      border-bottom: none;
    }
    .nav-tabs > li > a {
          border: none;
          border-radius: 0;
          background-color: #eee;
    }
    .nav-tabs > li > a:hover {
        background-color: #8845a6;
        color: #fff;
    }
    .nav-tabs > li.active > a {
        border: none;
        background-color: #8845a6;
        color: #fff;
    }
    .nav-tabs > li.active > a:hover,
    .nav-tabs > li.active > a:focus {
        border: none;
        background-color: #8845a6;
        color: #fff;
    }
:::

::: {.callout-block .callout-success}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Useful Tip: {#useful-tip-3 .callout-title}

Use a static snippet to include a \"heavy\" dynamic snippet if you want
to layer it down.
:::
:::
:::

::: {#snippetdynamic .section-block}
### Dynamic {#dynamic .block-title}

Dynamic snippets are those snippets which template is being updated at
run-time (page view), either it\'s updated from a data source or from a
post-script.
:::

[one of the template or css is mandatory]{.small}
:::

::: {#parameters-section .section .doc-section}
Parameters {#parameters .section-title}
----------

Because every superhero needs superpowers\... all snippets are
parameterizable. This gives you even more modularity and flexibility
when defining snippets.

Parameters are variables that are evaluated before the snippet\'s
template is rendered. They can be used inside template.

::: {#snippetparampredefined .section-block}
### Predefined variables {#predefined-variables .block-title}

::: {.code-block}
    {
      "config": {
        "paths": {
          "domain": "https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/johnnyb/flux",
          "upload": "https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/johnnyb/flux/published/uploads",
          "admin": "https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/johnnyb/flux"
        },
        "endpoints": {
          "apiGateway": "https://developers.dcsplus.net/dynapack/clients/bitusi/public/api.php",
          "translate": "https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/johnnyb/flux/published/data/cms-translate",
          "pages": "https://developers.dcsplus.net/users/johnnyb/flux/published"
        }
      },
      "app": {
        "name": "TRIP",
        "version": "1.0"
      }
    }
:::

So upload path can be accessed like
`{{ __globals.config.paths.upload }}`
:::

::: {#snippetparamdynamic .section-block}
### Dynamic pased {#dynamic-pased .block-title}

One cool thing is that snippets can react to user input through dynamic
variables. Let\'s say you want to create a widget with most viewed
hotels in a specific city. You don\'t want to create a snippet for each
city, but to have one snippet that can render hotels based on user
selected city.\
This can be easily done by using dynamic parameters.

Snippets support two types of dynamic parameters:

###### Source parameters

Those are parameters that are directly passed to snippet and may by
required for snippet\'s data source. They are enclosed between round
brackets and represent a [javascript
object](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Working_with_Objects):\
`__snippet::top-hotels({city:'Ploiesti', stars: 5})__`

Source parameters can be of two types:

-   route parameters - those are usualy for feching a single entity ex:
    */static-data/cities/7*; those parameters are passed by prefixing
    their name with colon\
    `__snippet::users({":id":21})__`\
    The above snippet\'s data source should be set as **/users/:id** and
    it will be processed to **/users/21**
-   query string parameters - those are usualy used for filtering ex:
    */static-data/cities?countryName=Romania*; those parameters are
    passed by their name\
    `__snippet::users({"id":21})__`\
    The above snippet\'s data source should be set as **/users** and it
    will be processed to **/users?id=21**

###### Parent parameters

When [nesting snippets](#nesting-section) you may find in need to pass
some variables to child snippets. To do this you can use parent
parameters. Parent parameters come after source parameters between right
brackets:

::: {.code-block}
###### Template of ***posts*** snippet with [data source](https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts)

\
`__snippet::posts__`

    <ul>
        {% for post in __ds %}
        <li>
            {{post.title}} </br>
            __snippet::post-body()[ { "id":{{post.id}}, "body": {{post.body|json_encode}} } ]__
        </li>
        {% endfor %}
    </ul>
:::

Watch how sub-snippet *post-body* is used in the above example:
`__snippet::post-body()[ { "id":{{post.id}}, "body": {{post.body|json_encode}} } ]__`

::: {.code-block}
###### Template of ***post-body*** snippet

    <div id="{{ __parent.id }}" class="post-body">
        {{ __parent.body }}
    </div>
:::

::: {.callout-block .callout-info}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Post-script variables {#post-script-variables .callout-title}

You can access snippets data-sources and parameters in post-scripts
under *window.\_\_snippets variable*
:::
:::

###### Query parameters

Sometimes you may want to change behavior based on user input which can
be visible on query string. Those parameters are automaticaly passed to
every snippet and it is accesible under **\_\_query** variable.\

::: {.code-block}
###### Example of Todos page

    <!doctype html>
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <!-- Required meta tags -->
        <meta charset="utf-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, shrink-to-fit=no">

        <!-- Bootstrap CSS -->
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/twitter-bootstrap/3.4.1/css/bootstrap.min.css" crossorigin="anonymous">

        <title>Todo list demo</title>
      </head>
      <body>
        
        <h1 class="text-center">My todo list</h1>  
       __snippet::todo-list__
       <p><i><small>endpoind: https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos</small></i></p>
        
        <!-- Optional JavaScript -->
        <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jquery/3.3.1/jquery.min.js" type="text/javascript" charset="utf-8" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
        <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/twitter-bootstrap/3.4.1/js/bootstrap.min.js" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
      </body>
    </html>

\

###### Code of Todos snippet

    {% set completed = __query.completed %}
    {% set todos = __ds %}
    <ul id="myUL">
        {% for todo in todos %}
            {% if todo.completed == completed or completed is empty %}
                <li class="completed-{{ todo.completed }}">{{ todo.title }}</li>
            {% endif %}
        {% endfor %}
    </ul>

As you can see the **completed** query parameter from
*todos.html?**completed**=1* is accesible within snippet with
**\_\_query.completed** variable
:::

::: {.callout-block .callout-success}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Useful Tip: {#useful-tip-4 .callout-title}

Usualy for filtering it\'s better to request filtered data source (using
data source parameters) but some endpoints may not have support for
filtering by desired fields.

Another use case might be for prepopulating fields, maybe keep a form
completed after a submision.
:::
:::
:::

::: {#snippetparampriority .section-block}
### Priority {#priority .block-title}

Let\'s say for the snippet \_\_snippet::user({\"id:6\"})\_\_ we have set
data source https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users.

By using this snippet without parent parameters or accesing the user
page without id query string parameter, the request for data source will
be: https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users?id=6.\
If we will access the page with id query string parameter ex:
[domain.com/user.html?id=7](domain.com/user.html?id=7), the request for
data source will be: https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users?id=7.\
If we will pass *id* as a parent parameter
`__snippet::user({"id:6"}[{ "id": {{owner.id}} }])__` the request for
data source will be: https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users?id=14
*(if the owner.id = 14)*.

::: {.callout-block .callout-info}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### Snippet parameters priority {#snippet-parameters-priority .callout-title}

Parent parameters overrides page query string parameters which overrides
default data source parameter

1.  parent
2.  query
3.  default
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {#nesting-section .section .doc-section}
Nesting snippets {#nesting .section-title}
----------------

You can insert snippets into another snippets. We call this technique:
**layering**.

::: {.callout-block .callout-info}
::: {.icon-holder}
:::

::: {.content}
#### View snippet render layer {#view-snippet-render-layer .callout-title}

You can access/view the snippet\'s render layer into your post-scripts
under\
*window\[\_\_snippets\[\'your-snippet-name\'\]\[\'layer\'\]*
:::
:::

::: {#snippetnestedpassingdata .section-block}
### Passing data between snippets {#passing-data-between-snippets .block-title}

At this moment you can only pass data between layered snippets, from
parent to child, throught parent data source parameters.
:::
:::

::: {#render-section .section .doc-section}
Render workflow {#render-workflow .section-title}
---------------

::: {.section-block}
Comming soon\...
:::
:::

::: {#debug-section .section .doc-section}
Debugging {#debugging .section-title}
---------

::: {.section-block}
You can see the order of the rendering of snippets and also the
parameters available for each snippet if you access in javascript
console **\_\_snippets** into your page.

![console.log(\_\_snippets)](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1556208512/developers.dcsplus.net/docs/console_snippets_write.png)
![\_\_snippets-output](https://res.cloudinary.com/deld1w6hq/image/upload/v1556208513/developers.dcsplus.net/docs/console_snippets_output.png)
:::
:::

::: {#howtouseit-section .section .doc-section}
How to use it {#how-to-use .section-title}
-------------

::: {.section-block}
One of the ways of using could be to define snippets corresponding to
business capabilities. A business capability is something a business
does in order to provide value to its end users. Identifying business
capabilities and corresponding snippets requires a high level
understanding of the business. For example, the business capabilities
for an online travel agency might include the following:

-   Search form for flights
-   List flight items
-   Flight item
-   User contact details
-   Payment
-   Landing page

Once the business capabilities have been identified, the required
snippets can be built corresponding to each of these identified business
capabilities.

After creating a snippet it can be inserted into pages or other snippets
using it\'s placeholder ` __snippet::search-form__ `
:::
:::

::: {#recommendations-section .section .doc-section}
Recommendations {#recommendations .section-title}
---------------

::: {.section-block}
When designing your snippets we strongly recommend to follow DRY pattern
and micro-service approach: a snippet should only be responsible for
doing one thing.

Name your snippets as much as possible intuitive *(for best performance
avoid using dot \[.\] in naming)*

If you have a complex page which uses lots of snippets, it\'s better to
layer them. Static and dynamic snippets which doesn\'t depend on
external calls should be included directly in page, while heavy dynamic
snippets should be included into another static snippet. This way the
user sees the static data immediatly and have the best user experience.

While there is no limit regarding maximum depth while nesting snippets,
you should try to avoid going to deep.

Use a static snippet to hold your main style

Use a static snippet to izolate portion of content for reuse.
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.content-section}
 CMS Tips & Tricks
=================

::: {#definition-section .section .doc-section}
Building a project -- tips & tricks {#building-project .section-title}
-----------------------------------

::: {#snippetname .section-block}
### Initial preparations {#initial-prep .block-title}

When starting to develop a new project, the developer has the choice to
start from scratch or to import a given project. We'll now focus on
building from scratch, to try and take advantage of all the CMS
utilities and helpers so that we can build a project-base as a
bootstrapper project for future projects as well.

From the start, as we've seen so far, the configs will play an important
part into achieving key built-in functionalities, so for sure we will
need a static snippet that we can include in all dynamic pages and that
will contain that base-logic for the project, preparing the data and
starting up the rendering, etc.

Without any configurations, the project would work just fine, rendering
whatever snippets we include, but we want to prepare for more than that.

Even adding one or more active languages and setting a default language,
will automatically trigger a translations request and, provided we have
saved all translations, it should all render just fine.

But in order to use all tools available, we will most likely need that
bootstrapping static snippet postScript. Additionally, it will help
knowing the tools provided by the CMS app, so here is a cheatsheet:
:::

::: {#snippetname .section-block}
### Basic tips / cheatsheet {#cheatsheet .block-title}

##### *Languages and translations*

The active languages configs need to be provided in order to activate
the use of languages/translations.

The active languages data will then be available on
`__globals.project.language.list.`

If a default language is provided as well, its data will be available on
`__globals.project.language.default`

If no default language is provided, the developer needs to initialize
the use of a specific language within a static postScript. To initialize
using a language (at page load) we can use this method:

`__app.language.init(langcode, callback, errorCallback)`

providing the language code (without it, method will fallback to
default) and callback function. Using this method, we make sure the app
has everything set up for languages and translations use.

Active language data will be available on `__app.language.data`, for
easy access in snippets postScripts and for snippet templates, we'll
have `__globals.activeLanguage` containing the language code and of
course all the languages data on `__globals.project.language.list` as
mentioned before

By default, the latest active language data is persisted in local
storage on the '\_\_lang' key, so the last used language will be
remembered and re-used on reoccurring visits.

CMS app takes care of the page rendering, API requests with
authentication and also managing critical data like languages,
translations, currencies. Using the integrated methods and helpers,
ensures that the information is there for subsequent page changes or
reloads and that the data is always set and persisted on local app +
global variables, for easy access from postScripts and from inside the
TWIG templates, as well.

Because the translations are made so that they will be available both on
client-side, as well as server-side, they are intended for on-demand
rendering, serving the content in different languages for search-engine
indexing purposes. But when dealing with a booking flow and
short-lifespan data, there is no indexing involved and the process
should be as smooth and as fast as possible, which translates into the
best user experience possible. This can be achieved by carefully
controlling the steps involved and the way the interface is rendered and
displayed, which means optimizing the loading and rendering of the
content. A single page application type implementation is therefore the
best approach and this can be achieved easily building on top of the
existing CMS app layer. A vue modular approach, ties perfectly with the
CMS snippets and postScripts concept and gives full control for future
maintenance and up-scaling the app.
:::

::: {#snippetcategory .section-block}
##### *Steps to building the SPA booking app* {#steps-to-building-the-spa-booking-app .block-title}

-   Project should contain a basic starter STATIC snippet which will
    contain javascript logic for setting prerequisites and managing data
    before page rendering + initializing
-   Basic layout snippets can be defined as normal -- head, header,
    footer, etc.
-   Dedicated snippets for different modules of the vue app should be
    put in concept, such as a search-area module which can be further
    split into service-based dedicated modules.
-   Going further on the booking-flow, a step-driven approach is useful,
    since this is a common denominator within all booking platforms. So,
    we then add a search-loading module, then a listing module, then
    details, then prebooking, each one being logically divided into
    smaller parts, like the listing module, for example, should contain
    a filters-area component, a sorting area, an items-list +
    pagination, a map submodule maybe etc.
-   All these should tie in together on top of the CMS app layer which
    provides the basic data and helper methods that can be reused,
    referenced and shared all throughout the flow. The vue app should
    use all the available tools in the page from global variables to the
    CMS app itself and it should centralize the data here, using the app
    object as the single source of truth, like a centralized store. This
    way, from any module or component the data can be accessed and with
    the use of in-page events, the timings can be synced, as well.
-   The step-driven approach should give a sense of the routing implied,
    as well. Most projects will share the same basic steps from search
    to listing to booking. Between these steps we won't want to reload
    or change the actual page, to save redundant requests, even if the
    assets are cached. Going through the flow and gathering the data
    should be easy enough, but we will need to keep the user at a given
    step, if for any reason the page is refreshed. So, refreshing on the
    booking page, for example, should keep the user on the booking step,
    rather than showing a blank search form :) Of course, the app will
    have to make multiple requests to be able to load the booking step
    from scratch, but it should be able to do that. So to achieve this,
    we'll need to use url params that keep the basic information
    regarding the booking flow, going through the steps. From search id,
    to search code, to flight itinerary code, etc. This way, when the
    user reloads the booking step, the app can check the params and
    retrace the way back, making the requests needed for that step and
    also gathering all the needed data in the page.
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.footer-row}

CMS Languages & Translation Example
===================================

TRIP languages module {#languages-module}
=====================

[ ]{lang="EN-US"}

[ Multiple languages can be added in TRIP, including RTL languages.\
The languages can be accessed via API using the endpoint: **/languages**
]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

\

Multi-language hotel content {#hotel-content}
============================

[ ]{lang="EN-US"}

[ For hotel, if you suppliers provide translated content, you need to
enable the languages in TRIP and import the static data.\
On the website part, if you want to request the hotel data per language,
in the dynapack request you need to add also the parameter lang and also
in the hotel details request. ]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

-   In the first search request ( /dynamic-package? ) you need to add
    the POST parameter \_s\[CID\]\[h\]\[0\]\[hotel\]\[lang\]: en\_EN -
    The language ISO code in which you want to receive the results
-   The code must be the one added by you in TRIP\`s admin
    area/Languages
-   Also, the language must be available in IRIX.
-   The next request that you need to do with language is the Hotel
    details GET request. Example: /v3/hotels/{hotelID}?lang=en

\

HTML text translation {#html-translation}
=====================

Translation example based on the standard Skeleton available in CMS TRIP
------------------------------------------------------------------------

[ ]{lang="EN-US"}

[The active language in the website will be persisted using the browser
**localStorage**. This means it will persist even if the user closes the
browser and returns some time later.\
]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}[Note: To manage
clearing the storage at an interval or on specific user actions, the
removal of the used localStorage keys, specified below, has to be
implemented as needed and is not provided by the current
application.]{lang="EN" style="font-size:9.0pt;line-height:115%"}

[For the translations to be applied, the project will need a server
configuration enabled which will imply the availability of the
\`defaultLanguage\` property on the *\_\_globals* var available on the
window scope: *\_\_globals.client.defaultLanguage*]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

[\
The **localStorage keys** that are used are:]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

**[1]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}**[. a dynamic
key, depending on website domain: **location.hostname + \'.lang\'**, so
it will be something like \'**my.domain.com.lang**\' and its value will
be a JSON data object:\
{ Code: \'en\', Rtl: false }\
or, containing more details:\
{ Code: \'en\', Name: \'English\', Rtl: false, ISO: \'en\_GB\', \... }\
depending on how you use the set method below]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

**[2]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}**[. a dynamic
key, depending on website domain: location.hostname +
\'.langUrlRequired\', so something like
\'**my.domain.com.langUrlRequired**\' and its value will be bool *true\
*This storage item will be used if the developer wants it that accessing
a page without a specific lang URL param, will revert active language to
the default language]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

[ ]{lang="EN-US"}

[Global (window) variables and methods that are available:\
\
]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

**[Variables]{lang="EN"}**

[ｷ[                
]{style="font:7.0pt \"Times New Roman\""}]{lang="EN-US"}**[\_\_globals.client.defaultLanguage
(= \'en\')]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}**

[- this will be available in server configuration from installation
step, if translations will be used on the website]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

[ｷ[                
]{style="font:7.0pt \"Times New Roman\""}]{lang="EN-US"}[ ]{lang="EN-US"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}**[\_\_globals.activeLanguage
]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}**

[- this will be available if any translation is available in the
website. Otherwise, \_\_globals won\'t have the \'activeLanguage\'
property\
This var can be used to render the selected language in your languages
selector, since \_\_globals object is also available in snippet
templates (TWIG)\
So, the TWIG code in your languages selector could look like this:\
\
\<select onchange=\"setLanguage(event.target.value)\"\>\
{% for language in \_\_ds.\_embedded.languages %}\
\<option\
value=\"{{ language.Code }}\"\
{{ language.Code == \_\_globals.activeLanguage ?
\'selected=\"selected\"\' : \'\' }}\>\
{{ language.Name }}\
\</option\>\
{% endfor %}\
\</select\>]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;
line-height:115%"}

**[\
Query params: ]{lang="EN"}**

[- **lang** - this has priority over *default language* and *storage
language*, so providing a specific \`lang\` query param, will override
the default and it will trigger replacement in storage. This is not
mandatory (by default) unless the \`requiredUrlParam\` localStorage key
is present (see below)]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

**[\
Methods:]{lang="EN"}**

[ｷ[                
]{style="font:7.0pt \"Times New Roman\""}]{lang="EN-US"}**[
setLanguage(value, doNotReload, callbackFn, requiredUrlParam)]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}**

[- this method will be used to change the active language (for example
when user selects another language on the website interface)\
\
- this is also used when the query param ***lang*** is found in the URL.
So accessing an URL:\
\[URL\]?lang=ar\
will automatically trigger *setLanguage method* and change the language
to arabic\
So, **implementing the language change** can be as easy as adding the
method inside an onchange attribute to your language selector element:\
\
\<select name=\"language\"
onchange=\"setLanguage(event.target.value)\"\>\
\<option value=\"\"\>Select language\</option\>\
{% for lang in languages %}\
\<option value=\"{{ lang.Code }}\"\>{{ lang.Name }}\</option\>\
{% endfor %}\
\</select\>\
\
**setLanguage** fn parameters:]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

[ [    ]{style="font:7.0pt \"Times New Roman\""}]{lang="EN-US"
style="font-family:OpenSymbol"}***[value]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}***[ is the only parameter
that is mandatory. It can either be:\
- string == the 2 letters language code you want enabled, or\
- object - the entire language object as it is received from
\`/languages\` API endpoint\
- ***doNotReload*** parameter is optional and it is useful if you want
to use the method without automatically triggering page reload. Since
the page is rendered from dynamic snippets (which contain the
translations) the language and translations need to be available before
starting rendering, therefore once the language is changed the pages
needs to be rendered again.This is done automatically if you do not
specifically provide this second param \`true\`. It can be set to
\`false\` to keep the default behaviour\
- ***callbackFn*** parameter is optional and it is useful when setting
the second param \`true\` to manually have control on refreshing the
page or for different additional use cases. It can be set to \`null\` if
the second was set \`false\` and you rely on the automatic page reload\
- ***requiredUrlParam*** parameter is optional and can be set to
\`true\` if you need to change the default behaviour with translations
being applied on pages even if the active language is not present in URL
as \`lang\`. By default, the app will apply translations based on the
language saved in localStorage without the need to carry the query URL
param \`lang\` from a page to another. So setting this to \`true\` will
change this to actually revert to default language when a page doesn\'t
have a specific, valid \`lang\` URL param, like \`lang=es\`.\
This param sets a different localStorage key which can be managed
separately too, without the need to use the *setLanguage* method. The
storage key is composed of the same domain prefix location.hostname and
\'.requiredUrlParam\', so it will be something like:\
\`my.domain.com.requiredUrlParam\` with value true or any value for that
matter. The app will only check if the key is set.]{lang="EN"
style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

[For disabling this option, the localStorage key can be removed
completely]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;
line-height:115%"}

[So, managing this feature is as easy as toggling the presence of this
specific key, like so:\
to enable it:\
- localStorage.setItem(location.hostname + \'.requiredUrlParam\',
true);\
to disable it:\
- localStorate.removeItem(location.hostname + \'.requiredUrlParam\');\
which is also what the setLanguage method does when provided with a
Boolean value for that 4[th]{style="position:relative;top:-5.0pt"}
parameter, meaning that if the parameter is omitted the storage is not
changed.\
\
]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;
line-height:115%"}

[ｷ[                
]{style="font:7.0pt \"Times New Roman\""}]{lang="EN-US"}**[translate(\'string\')
- ]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}**[function used
inside javascript to output translated texts. It accepts one *mandatory*
parameter which is the actual string to be translated. This string
should be a static plain (non-rich) text, which can contain punctuation
marks]{lang="EN" style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

[ｷ[                 ]{style="font:7.0pt \"Times New Roman\""}
]{lang="EN-US"} [ **{% verbatim %}{%filter translate %}{% endverbatim
%}This text will be translated{% verbatim %}{% endfilter %}{%
endverbatim %}** - Not relevant for javascript since this is the format
for **Twig** language, used inside snippets template. This is the exact
format needed for the keys to be scannable and to be extracted and
displayed in the translation interface. The text should be plain
(non-rich) text and can contain punctuation marks.
]{style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%"}

[ ]{lang="EN-US"}

[ ]{lang="EN-US"}

[ ]{lang="EN-US"}

::: {style="margin: 2rem 0; padding: 2rem; background: rgba(30, 41, 59, 0.4); border-left: 4px solid #60a5fa; border-radius: 8px;"}
::: {style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding-bottom: 1rem; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(96, 165, 250, 0.2);"}
 Implementation in Short {#implementation-in-short style="color: #60a5fa; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;"}
-----------------------

Quick guide to implementing translations and dynamic languages
:::

::: {style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem;"}
### Implementing Translations and Dynamic Languages: {#implementing-translations-and-dynamic-languages style="color: #cbd5e1; font-size: 1.1rem; margin-bottom: 1.5rem;"}

::: {style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 1.2rem; background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.5); border-radius: 6px; border-left: 3px solid #60a5fa;"}
#### **1.** User Interaction for Language Change {#user-interaction-for-language-change style="color: #93c5fd; font-size: 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.8rem;"}

User interaction for language change should trigger the
`setLanguage`{style="background: rgba(96, 165, 250, 0.15); padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 3px; color: #93c5fd; font-family: 'Courier New', monospace;"}
method passing the new language code:

::: {style="background: #0f172a; padding: 1rem; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid rgba(96, 165, 250, 0.2);"}
``` {style="margin: 0; color: #e2e8f0; font-family: 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.5;"}
$('.lang-selector').on('change', function(e) {
    setLanguage(e.target.value);
});
```
:::
:::

::: {style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 1.2rem; background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.5); border-radius: 6px; border-left: 3px solid #60a5fa;"}
#### **2.** Alternative: URL Parameter Method {#alternative-url-parameter-method style="color: #93c5fd; font-size: 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.8rem;"}

Or, just redirect user to the same page with the query (URL) param
`lang=es`{style="background: rgba(96, 165, 250, 0.15); padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 3px; color: #93c5fd; font-family: 'Courier New', monospace;"}
to change the language to Spanish.
:::

::: {style="padding: 1.2rem; background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.5); border-radius: 6px; border-left: 3px solid #60a5fa;"}
#### **3.** Determine Current Active Language {#determine-current-active-language style="color: #93c5fd; font-size: 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.8rem;"}

Use
`__globals.activeLanguage`{style="background: rgba(96, 165, 250, 0.15); padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 3px; color: #93c5fd; font-family: 'Courier New', monospace;"}
in page to determine the current active language.
:::
:::
:::
